heading: The browser tracing verify snippet is a syntax error
title: Fix the tracing verify snippet on the browser getting-started page: await inside a non-async function
body:
`platform-includes/getting-started-verify/javascript.mdx:53-68` tells the reader to update the button handler so that it starts a span around a simulated longer operation, and shows `function triggerError() { await Sentry.startSpan(...) }`. The function is not `async`.

Observed with the snippet copied verbatim into a page: Chrome reports `Uncaught SyntaxError: await is only valid in async functions and the top level bodies of modules`, discards the whole script block, and the "Break the World" button next to it throws `ReferenceError`. With `async function triggerError()` the same page produces the span (`test Example Frontend Span`) inside the pageload span envelope.

What to change:

- Make the handler `async function triggerError()` in the snippet, and keep the button call as it is.
- Say what arrives: one span envelope with the pageload segment and the manual span as a child, no transaction envelope, because the default lifecycle is stream (DOC-Q1).

heading: Three React Router page snippets do not run on React 19
title: Fix the React Router v6 and v7 page snippets that fail on React 19
body:
Three snippets on the React Router pages fail when copied verbatim into a React 19 app. The declarative-mode snippet at `guides/react/features/react-router/v7.mdx:71-108` renders with `ReactDOM.render` (`:101`), which react-dom 19 no longer exports: `TypeError: import_react_dom.default.render is not a function` at boot, nothing renders, and the SDK reports its own docs page crash. The same call sits at `v6.mdx:94`, `v6.mdx:150` and `v7.mdx:155`.

The `useRoutes` snippet at `v7.mdx:122-160` imports `wrapUseRoutes` (`:131`) but calls `wrapUseRoutesV7` (`:147`), and uses `Sentry`, `ReactDOM` and `BrowserRouter` without importing them: `ReferenceError: Sentry is not defined`, the SDK never initializes and zero envelopes arrive. `v6.mdx:117-155` has the same mismatch.

The custom `errorElement` snippet at `v7.mdx:239-255` is a `jsx` block that contains the TypeScript cast `useRouteError() as Error` (`:244`) and imports from `react-router-dom` (`:240`) while the page installs `react-router`: esbuild stops with `Expected ";" but found "as"` and an unresolved import. The same cast is at `v8.mdx:246` and `v6.mdx:239`.

With the three defects fixed, the page's wiring works: pageload and navigation segments named `/users/:userId` with source `route`, and the `errorElement` boundary captures the route render error.

What to change:

- Render with `ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById("root")).render(...)`, as `v8.mdx:104` already does, in all four places.
- In the `useRoutes` snippets import `* as Sentry from "@sentry/react"`, call `Sentry.wrapUseRoutesV7` (or `Sentry.wrapUseRoutes`), and import `BrowserRouter` and `ReactDOM`.
- Drop the cast or tag the block `tsx`, and import `useRouteError` from the package the page installs.

heading: The Vue Router page's only full example is Vue 2 code on a page that says v4 is supported
title: Add a Vue 3 example to the Vue Router instrumentation page
body:
`guides/vue/features/vue-router.mdx:8` says the routing instrumentation supports vue-router v2, v3 and v4, and the page's one full example at `:13-43` is Vue 2 code: `import Vue from "vue"` (`:14`), `import Router from "vue-router"` (`:17`), `Vue.use(Router)` (`:22`), `new Router` (`:24`), `new Vue` (`:37`).

Observed on the guide's own Vue 3 install (vue 3.5.42, vue-router 4.6.4): the snippet does not build, esbuild reports `No matching export for import default` for both imports. The guide's init at `guides/vue/index.mdx:71-126` with `browserTracingIntegration({ router })` works, and `routeLabel: "path"` gives `/users/:id` segments with source `route`.

What to change:

- Add a Vue 3 tab (`createApp`, `createRouter`, `Sentry.init({ app, integrations: [Sentry.browserTracingIntegration({ router })] })`) next to the Vue 2 one, or lead with it.

heading: The tracingOptions.hooks snippet on the Vue component tracking page is a syntax error
title: Add the missing comma to the tracingOptions.hooks snippet on the Vue component tracking page
body:
`guides/vue/features/component-tracking.mdx:56-69` has no comma after `trackComponents: true` (`:63`). Copied verbatim, esbuild stops with `Expected "}" but found "hooks"`. With the comma added the snippet works: `ui.mount` for every component, five `ui.update` spans and `ui.unmount` for the removed component, all under the pageload segment.

What to change:

- Add the comma.

heading: The Express, Fastify, Koa, Hapi and Connect guides' ESM tabs import the instrument file without its extension
title: Fix the extensionless instrument import on the Express, Fastify, Koa, Hapi and Connect guides and the esm-without-import page
body:
`platform-includes/getting-started-use/javascript.express.mdx:22` starts the ESM app with `import "./instrument";`, while the config step creates `instrument.mjs`. Node ESM does not probe extensions: the app never starts, `Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module .../instrument ... Did you mean to import "./instrument.js"?`. With `import "./instrument.mjs"` the same app produces exactly the `--import` output. The same extensionless import sits at `common/install/esm-without-import.mdx:55`, and the orphaned `platform-includes/getting-started-add-top-level-import/javascript.express.mdx` imports `./instrument.js`. The Fastify tab has the same defect at `platform-includes/getting-started-use/javascript.fastify.mdx:20`, with the same `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` (QS-fastify, variant esm-tab), and so does the Koa tab at `getting-started-use/javascript.koa.mdx:20`; on Koa the corrected first-line import starts the app but loses every router and middleware span and the route names, so the Koa tab should rely on the `node --import` command instead (QS-koa, variants esm-tab and self-import). The Hapi tab at `getting-started-use/javascript.hapi.mdx:28` fails the same way, and its corrected first-line import loses nothing (QS-hapi, variants esm-tab and self-import), and so does the Connect tab at `getting-started-use/javascript.connect.mdx:20` (QS-connect, variant esm-tab). The NestJS guide has its own page, `guides/nestjs/install/esm-without-import.mdx:41-51`, whose `main.ts` imports `./instrument` without extension and does not start as ESM either (QS-nestjs, variant esm-verbatim).

What to change:

- Import `./instrument.mjs` in the Express, Fastify, Hapi and Connect ESM tabs, drop the import from the Koa tab in favour of `--import`, matching the file the config step creates, and fix `esm-without-import.mdx:55` the same way.

heading: The late-initialization page is built on the @sentry/node/preload entry that v11 removed
title: Rewrite or remove the late-initialization install page for v11
body:
`common/install/late-initialization.mdx` (supported by the Node, Connect, Express, Fastify, Hapi, Hono and Koa guides) tells readers to run `node --require @sentry/node/preload app.js` (`:37`) or `node --import @sentry/node/preload app.js` (`:68`) and to select modules with `SENTRY_PRELOAD_INTEGRATIONS` (`:106`, `:132`).

Observed on develop: `Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: Package subpath './preload' is not defined by "exports" in @sentry/node/package.json`; the package exports `.`, `./import`, `./vite`, `./rollup`, `./webpack` and `./esbuild` only. `common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:1359` records that the `init`, `preload` and `loader` entry points were removed from every server SDK, and names the replacement: `--import` the SDK and call `Sentry.init()` later. The Fastify run hit the same error; the page lists Fastify at `:9` and `:114` (QS-fastify, variant late-init), as did the Koa run, with Koa listed at `:116` (QS-koa, variant late-init), and the Hapi run, with Hapi listed at `:115` (QS-hapi, variant late-init), and the Connect run, with Connect listed at `:113` although no Connect integration exists to preload (QS-connect, variant late-init), and the Hono run, with Hono listed at `:11` (QS-hono, variant late-init).

What to change:

- Rewrite the page around the v11 shape (`--import` the SDK, call `Sentry.init()` when the DSN is known) and drop `@sentry/node/preload` and `SENTRY_PRELOAD_INTEGRATIONS`, or remove the page from the v11 docs.
- Check the v11 docs tickets for an existing owner before filing.

heading: Three Angular snippets do not compile under the tsconfig ng new generates
title: Fix the Angular manual-setup, error handler and component tracking snippets that fail to build
body:
`guides/angular/manual-setup.mdx:246-275` (the Angular 19+ tab) calls `inject(TraceService)` at `:270` but imports only `ApplicationConfig`, `ErrorHandler`, `inject`, `provideAppInitializer`, `Router` and `* as Sentry`: `ng build` fails with `TS2304 Cannot find name 'TraceService'`. With `inject(Sentry.TraceService)` the app runs and pageload and navigation segments are named after the route (`/users/:id/`, source `route`).

`guides/angular/features/error-handler.mdx:67-82` extends `Sentry.SentryErrorHandler` with `handleError(error: any): void` (`:76`) and fails with `TS4114 This member must have an override modifier` under the strict tsconfig `ng new` generates (`noImplicitOverride: true`).

`guides/angular/features/component-tracking.mdx:80-94` and `:106-122` fail with `TS2304` for `OnChanges`, `SimpleChanges` and `OnDestroy` (only `Component` and `OnInit` are imported), `TS2339 Property 'user' does not exist`, and `NG8001` for the `app-icon` and `app-button` elements the template uses. With the imports and the input added, the trace directive, `TraceClass` and `TraceMethod` all emit their spans.

What to change:

- Call `inject(Sentry.TraceService)` in the app.config snippet.
- Write `override handleError(error: any): void` in the custom error handler.
- Import `Input`, `OnChanges`, `OnDestroy` and `SimpleChanges` in the component tracking examples and declare the `user` input the template reads, or trim the template to elements the example defines.

heading: The Fastify error handler page imports from a package that does not exist
title: Fix the Fastify error handler page: @sentry/fastify does not exist and fastify() is never imported
body:
`guides/fastify/features/error-handler.mdx:14` reads `import { setupFastifyErrorHandler } from "@sentry/fastify";`. No such package exists, in the develop tarballs or in the monorepo's `packages/`: the snippet fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package '@sentry/fastify'`. It also calls `fastify()` at `:16` without importing it.

What to change:

- Import from `@sentry/node` and add the `fastify` import, or retire the page in favour of the `fastifyIntegration` options (DOC-Q38).

heading: The Svelte v5 tab of the tracing verify snippet binds onClick, which Svelte 5 compiles to nothing
title: Change onClick to onclick in the Svelte v5 tab of the tracing verify snippet
body:
`guides/svelte/index.mdx:254-267` (the Svelte v5+ tab) writes the verify button with `onClick={...}` at `:257`, and `:249` says clicking it triggers a frontend error and a performance trace. Svelte 5.57.0 compiles `onClick` into `event("Click", ...)`: the rendered button has only its `id` and `type`, clicking it sends no span and no event, and neither the compiler, dev mode nor the runtime warns. With `onclick`, which the errors tab at `:217` already uses, the same snippet sends the `Example Frontend Span` and the error.

What to change:

- Change `onClick` to `onclick` in the Svelte v5+ tab.

heading: The Koa verify snippet uses a router the guide never creates
title: Add the router to the Koa getting-started snippets that the verify step relies on
body:
`platform-includes/getting-started-verify/javascript.koa.mdx:7` and `:13-15` tell the reader to add `router.get("/debug-sentry", ...)` to the main application file. The guide's application file (`getting-started-use/javascript.koa.mdx`) creates no router and no step installs `@koa/router`; pasted as instructed the app dies at startup with `ReferenceError: router is not defined`, captured as `auto.node.onuncaughtexception`. The only Koa snippet that creates a router, `getting-started-add-top-level-import/javascript.koa.mdx`, is rendered by no page.

What to change:

- Add `npm install @koa/router` to the install step and `import Router from "@koa/router"; const router = new Router(); app.use(router.routes());` to both getting-started-use tabs, as the unrendered include already does.

heading: The Solid guide's tracing snippet needs a package the guide never installs
title: State on the Solid guide that the tracing snippet requires @solidjs/router
body:
`guides/solid/index.mdx:31` installs `@sentry/solid` only, and the `index.jsx` snippet with the performance option (`:76`, `:89`) imports `solidRouterBrowserTracingIntegration` from `@sentry/solid/solidrouter`. That module imports `@solidjs/router`, an optional peer: without Solid Router installed the build fails with `Could not resolve "@solidjs/router"`. With the router installed the snippet builds and runs.

What to change:

- Say that the performance snippet requires `@solidjs/router`, and show `Sentry.browserTracingIntegration()` for apps without Solid Router.

heading: The Connect guide and integration page describe an instrumentation that v11 removed; every printed app crashes
title: Rewrite the Connect guide and integration page for v11, whose SDK has no Connect instrumentation
body:
`common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:1370` records that the Connect instrumentation was removed, and the develop build confirms it: `@sentry/node` exports neither `setupConnectErrorHandler` nor `connectIntegration`, installs no `Connect` integration (46 with tracing, 23 without), and carries no orchestrion config or diagnostics-channel subscriber for connect. The docs still describe it in six places.

`platform-includes/getting-started-use/javascript.connect.mdx:11` and `:28` call `Sentry.setupConnectErrorHandler(app)` after `connect()`: every app the guide prints crashes with `TypeError: Sentry.setupConnectErrorHandler is not a function` before it listens, under `--import`, CommonJS, a first-line import and `NODE_OPTIONS`; the orphaned `getting-started-add-top-level-import/javascript.connect.mdx:9` and `:24` do the same. `common/configuration/integrations/connect.mdx:23-27` passes `integrations: [Sentry.connectIntegration()]`, which throws inside the instrument file so the SDK never initializes; `:3`, `:19` and `:21` say the integration is enabled by default and captures spans with `@opentelemetry/instrumentation-connect` (and the sentence says "for the Hapi framework"). The integrations table row at `platform-includes/configuration/integrations/javascript.connect.mdx:7`, the request-handler row at `v10-to-v11/index.mdx:436` and the `Connect` entry of `common/install/late-initialization.mdx:113` repeat it.

With the handler line deleted the guide app runs and delivers the generic Node telemetry only: `http.server` segments named `GET` with source `url` and no `http.route`, no handler or middleware span, logs, and no automatic capture of a thrown handler error (DOC-Q53).

What to change:

- Delete the `setupConnectErrorHandler(app)` line from both tabs and the orphaned include, and say that v11 has no Connect-specific instrumentation: requests appear as method-named `http.server` segments.
- Replace the Connect integration page with a removal notice pointing at the migration entry, drop the table row, drop Connect from the request-handler row at `:436` and from the late-initialization list.

heading: The NestJS tracing verify snippet kills the process after one request
title: Fix the NestJS tracing verify snippet: its delayed throw is an uncaught exception that exits the app
body:
`platform-includes/getting-started-verify/javascript.nestjs.mdx:30-49` updates `/debug-sentry` with `Sentry.startSpan(...)` whose callback throws inside `setTimeout(..., 99)`. The route answers 200 and the test span is sent, then the throw fires outside the Nest pipeline: captured as `auto.node.onuncaughtexception`, and the Nest process exits, so the app is dead after one hit. The snippet also shows no controller class and no `Sentry` import.

What to change:

- Throw synchronously inside the callback or await a delay, wrap the snippet in a controller with `import * as Sentry from "@sentry/nestjs"`, and say the result is a span inside the request trace.

heading: The NestJS ESM install page's start script is not a runnable command
title: Replace the NestJS ESM start script with a command that runs
body:
`guides/nestjs/install/esm.mdx:33-36` shows `"start": "--import ./instrument.mjs nest start"`. Executed as an npm script it fails with `sh: --: invalid option`: the line names no `node` binary, and `nest start` does not accept `--import`. The `NODE_OPTIONS` form at `:41` works, as does `node --import ./dist/instrument.js dist/main.js`.

What to change:

- Show a real command such as `node --import ./instrument.mjs dist/main.js`, or lead with the `NODE_OPTIONS` form.

heading: The GCP Functions pages call three exports that do not exist
title: Fix the nonexistent exports on the Google Cloud Functions pages: wrapBackgroundFunction, pgIntegration and ioredisIntegration
body:
`guides/gcp-functions/index.mdx:102` and `:145` (the Background tabs of Verify and Tracing) call `Sentry.wrapBackgroundFunction(...)`. The package exports `wrapHttpFunction`, `wrapEventFunction` and `wrapCloudEventFunction` only; the Functions Framework fails to load the file with `TypeError: Sentry.wrapBackgroundFunction is not a function` and exits. The config include (`platform-includes/getting-started-config/javascript.gcp-functions.mdx:71`) already uses `wrapEventFunction`, which works.

`guides/gcp-functions/tracing/instrumentation/automatic-instrumentation.mdx:31` and `:35` add database instrumentation with `Sentry.pgIntegration()` and `Sentry.ioredisIntegration()`. Neither exists; the package re-exports `postgresIntegration` and `redisIntegration` from `@sentry/node`, and the snippet throws before `Sentry.init` runs.

What to change:

- Rename both Background tabs to `Sentry.wrapEventFunction`, and replace `pgIntegration()` and `ioredisIntegration()` with `postgresIntegration()` and `redisIntegration()`.

heading: Two AWS Lambda snippets do not parse
title: Fix the stray parenthesis in the AWS Lambda ESM verify handler and Promise.rejected on the wrapper page
body:
`guides/aws-lambda/index.mdx:48-54`, the ESM verify tab, ends the handler with `}));`, one `)` too many: loading the file gives `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ')'`, captured through `onuncaughtexception`, and no span. With `});` the handler works. `guides/aws-lambda/configuration/lambda-wrapper.mdx:51-52` calls `Promise.rejected(...)` twice inside `Promise.allSettled`: `TypeError: Promise.rejected is not a function`.

What to change:

- Change `}));` to `});` and `Promise.rejected` to `Promise.reject`.

heading: The Effect metrics layer breaks the whole program on Effect v3
title: Drop the metrics layer from the Effect v3 snippet, or say it needs Effect v4
body:
`guides/effect/index.mdx:111-115` (the v3 Server tab with the metrics option) merges `Sentry.SentryEffectMetricsLayer` into the layer. With effect 3.22.2 the layer fails to build with `Service not found: effect/Scope`, the program never runs and nothing is sent; with effect 4.0.0-rc.112 the same layer builds. The metrics option (`:27`) also has no verify section.

What to change:

- Drop the metrics layer from the v3 snippet or state that it needs Effect v4, and add a metrics verify snippet or remove the option until it works on both majors.

heading: The Nitro guide's install fails on current Nitro betas and its config never registers the verify route
title: Fix the Nitro guide's version claim and add serverDir to its config
body:
`guides/nitro/index.mdx:23` says a Nitro application 3.0.260415-beta or newer, and `:50` installs `@sentry/nitro`. `npm install` fails with `ERESOLVE` for every Nitro beta newer than 3.0.260415-beta, the registry's latest 3.0.260903-beta included, because the peer range accepts only 3.0.0, 3.0.260311-beta and 3.0.260415-beta; the exact 260415 beta installs.

`:86-99` wraps `defineNitroConfig({ ... })` with no `serverDir`, and `:208` adds `routes/debug-sentry.ts` at the project root. Nitro 3 defaults to `serverDir: false`, scans nothing, and every route including `/debug-sentry` answers 404 with no event; with `serverDir: "./server"` and the file at `server/routes/debug-sentry.ts` the route creates the issue.

What to change:

- State the exact Nitro versions the peer range accepts and that newer betas need `--legacy-peer-deps` until the range is widened; add `serverDir: "./server"` to the config snippet and name the verify file `server/routes/debug-sentry.ts`.

heading: The guide states the instrumentation model backwards and never names the plugin
title: Rewrite the Bun guide's instrumentation step around @sentry/bun/plugin
body:
The Bun guide at `guides/bun/index.mdx:88` and `:100` tells the user to run `bun --preload ./instrument.js app.js`, and the alert at `:90-94` states that Sentry's auto-instrumentation does not work with bundled code and that bundling requires manual instrumentation. `@sentry/bun/plugin` is not named anywhere on the page, and `logs` is used as an onboarding block at `:182` but is missing from the options at `:20-22`.

What was observed on bun 1.4.0: a bundle built with `Bun.build({ plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` from `@sentry/bun/plugin` records library and framework spans, while running the same app unbundled with `bun run` records none. `packages/bun/src/plugin.ts:14` states the plugin is build-only. The unbundled diagnostic message is printed only with `debug: true`.

What to change:

- Keep the `--preload` step, described as what guarantees init order.
- Add a "Build with the Sentry plugin" step showing `Bun.build({ entrypoints: [...], plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` imported from `@sentry/bun/plugin`.
- Replace the alert at `:90-94` with a plain statement: library and framework instrumentation requires a build with the plugin; `bun run` on unbundled source records manual spans plus `Bun.serve`, `node:http` and `fetch` spans.
- Add `logs` to the onboarding options at `:20-22`, or remove the block at `:182`.

heading: Stream-mode includes call `'static'` the default; develop defaults to `'stream'`
title: Fix inverted traceLifecycle default in the stream mode includes
body:
The three stream-mode includes present stream mode as opt-in, in four places. `platform-includes/performance/enable-stream-mode/javascript.bun.mdx:5`, `javascript.deno.mdx:5` and `javascript.cloudflare.mdx:8` (Cloudflare Pages) and `:35` (Cloudflare Workers) all say "Opt in by setting the `traceLifecycle` option to `'stream'`", and each file closes with "set `traceLifecycle` to `'static'` (the default)" (`javascript.bun.mdx:25`, `javascript.deno.mdx:24`, `javascript.cloudflare.mdx:62`).

On develop the default is `'stream'`. `packages/core/src/client.ts:243` (`:242` at the pin) normalizes `traceLifecycle: options.traceLifecycle === 'static' ? 'static' : 'stream'`, and the comment directly above it (`:237-238`) states the same rule: every value except an explicit `'static'` resolves to stream. No runtime overrides it. Cloudflare reads `SENTRY_TRACE_LIFECYCLE` at `packages/cloudflare/src/options.ts:73`, but that read returns `undefined` when the variable is unset (`:107-109`), so it never changes the default, and `packages/deno/src/integrations/deno-serve.ts:28` describes `'stream'` as the default too.

The docs already say this on another page: `docs/platforms/javascript/common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:23` calls stream mode "the new default", and `:198` tells the reader to set `traceLifecycle: 'static'`, or the `SENTRY_TRACE_LIFECYCLE=static` environment variable, to keep the previous model. The includes contradict the migration guide on the same site.

What to change:

- Reframe all four opt-in sentences as opt-out (`javascript.bun.mdx:5`, `javascript.deno.mdx:5`, `javascript.cloudflare.mdx:8` and `:35`): `'stream'` is the default, `'static'` is what a user sets.
- Replace the `traceLifecycle: "stream"` sample lines with `"static"` examples, or drop them.
- Add the missing comma after `tracesSampleRate: 0.2` in the Pages snippet at `javascript.cloudflare.mdx:19`; the Workers snippet at `:40-56` already parses.
- Match the wording of `migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:23` and `:198`, including the `SENTRY_TRACE_LIFECYCLE=static` escape hatch.

Confirmed on Node on 2026-09-09: with no `traceLifecycle` option every Elysia span carried `sentry.trace_lifecycle: stream` and only span envelopes arrived; transaction envelopes needed an explicit `'static'` (QS-elysia, variants guide and static).

heading: Deno crons page recommends denoCronIntegration(), which throws on Deno 2.9.0 and later
title: Stop recommending denoCronIntegration() on the Deno crons page
body:
`platform-includes/crons/setup/javascript.deno.mdx:1` heads its first section "Automatic Check-Ins (Recommended)" and `:12` tells the reader to pass `Sentry.denoCronIntegration()` to `Sentry.init`.

That call crashes startup on Deno 2.9.0 and later. `packages/deno/src/integrations/deno-cron.ts:23` assigns `Deno.cron = new Proxy(Deno.cron, ...)` inside `setupOnce`, i.e. inside `Sentry.init`. On Deno 2.8.3 `Deno.cron` is a writable data property and the integration works: a cron firing at the minute boundary produced one `in_progress` and one `ok` check-in. From Deno 2.9.0 `Deno.cron` is a getter-only accessor, so the assignment throws `TypeError: Cannot set property cron of #<Object> which has only a getter` and the process exits 1 before any user code runs.

There is a second failure mode without the unstable flag. When `Deno.cron` is absent the guard at `deno-cron.ts:18-21` returns silently, so the integration is an inert no-op and the SDK gives no warning, while the reader's own `Deno.cron(...)` call throws `TypeError: Deno.cron is not a function`. The integration is also not in the Deno default set (`packages/deno/src/sdk.ts:31-49`), although its own JSDoc at `deno-cron.ts:64` says "Enabled by default in the Deno SDK".

What to change:

- Remove the "Recommended" framing and the `denoCronIntegration()` snippet, or state that it makes `Sentry.init` throw on Deno 2.9.0 and later and works only up to Deno 2.8.3.
- Lead with the `Sentry.withMonitor` / `Sentry.captureCheckIn` sections already on the page.
- State that `Deno.cron` needs `--unstable-cron`, and that without the flag the integration silently does nothing.
- Say that the integration has to be passed in `integrations` explicitly; it is not in the Deno default set.

heading: Bun OpenTelemetry setup includes import @sentry/node-core and call APIs that no longer exist
title: Delete the Bun OpenTelemetry setup includes and drop Bun from custom-setup
body:
Three Bun OpenTelemetry includes are written against a package and APIs that no longer exist. `platform-includes/performance/opentelemetry-setup/javascript.bun.mdx:5` and `:48` import `SentryContextManager, validateOpenTelemetrySetup` from `@sentry/node-core`; `error-monitoring-only/javascript.bun.mdx:3` and `with-custom-sampler/javascript.bun.mdx:3` do the same. `javascript.bun.mdx:12` and `:55` pass `skipOpenTelemetrySetup: true`, `error-monitoring-only/javascript.bun.mdx:30` calls `provider.addSpanProcessor(...)`, `SentrySampler` is constructed at `javascript.bun.mdx:6`, `:26`, `:49`, `:67` and `error-monitoring-only/javascript.bun.mdx:4`, `:27`, and `with-custom-sampler/javascript.bun.mdx:4` and `:13` use `wrapSamplingDecision`.

On develop there is no `node-core` package under `packages/`, a merge the migration guide records at `docs/platforms/javascript/common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:1396`. `skipOpenTelemetrySetup`, `SentryContextManager`, `validateOpenTelemetrySetup`, `SentrySpanProcessor`, `SentrySampler` and `wrapSamplingDecision` appear nowhere in `packages/*/src`; the only `SentrySampler` string left in the repository is a stale comment in `packages/node/src/integrations/node-fetch/undici-instrumentation.ts` (`:265` at the pin, `:256` on develop). `packages/opentelemetry/src/index.ts` is nine lines and exports only `getScopesFromContext`, `SentryPropagator`, `SentryTracerProvider`, the `AsyncLocalStorageLookup` type, `setOpenTelemetryContextAsyncContextStrategy` and `registerPrepareSpanScope`.

This cannot be repaired by swapping imports. With the sampler, the span processor and the context manager all gone, there is no custom OpenTelemetry setup path left to document for Bun. `enableOpenTelemetrySetup: false` is not a replacement for `skipOpenTelemetrySetup: true` either: it is already the Bun default, since `packages/bun/src/types.ts:21-23` documents `@default false` and Bun's `_init` delegates to `initNode` (`packages/bun/src/sdk.ts:158`), where `packages/node/src/sdk/index.ts:253` applies `options.enableOpenTelemetrySetup ?? false`. There is nothing for a Bun reader to set.

What to change:

- Delete the three `javascript.bun` files under `platform-includes/performance/opentelemetry-setup/`.
- Drop `javascript.bun` from the `supported` list in `docs/platforms/javascript/common/opentelemetry/custom-setup.mdx`, the only page that includes them, so nothing else breaks.
- If that page stays for other platforms, fix its body too: `:35`, `:53` and `:66` name the same removed symbols, and `:122` and `:132` still pass `skipOpenTelemetrySetup: true`.

heading: Agents SDK page claims instance-name span attributes and instance-name conversation IDs; neither is true
title: Correct the Agents SDK span attribute and conversation ID claims
body:
`docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/agent-tracing/agents-sdk.mdx:11` says callable RPC spans carry "the agent class and instance name as attributes". `:43` says "The automatic conversation ID defaults to the **agent instance name**", and `:45` builds override guidance on that premise, warning about per-user instances and singletons named `"default"`.

Neither claim holds on develop. `packages/cloudflare/src/instrumentations/agents/types.ts:61-70` builds the span attributes from `instance._ParentClass?.name` alone, setting `gen_ai.agent.name` to the base agent class; no instance name is attached. The conversation id is a `uuid4()` minted per instance and persisted to Durable Object storage (`types.ts:173`, `:180`), rotated to a fresh `uuid4()` when `message:clear` fires (`instrumentChatAgentConversation.ts:34-36`). `types.ts:104` says the instance `name` is deliberately not used. Recorded telemetry matches: callable RPC spans arrive with `gen_ai.agent.name` set to the base class, and conversation ids are hex uuid4 values that change after the chat is cleared.

What to change:

- Fix `:11` to name only the agent class attribute.
- Rewrite the Conversation IDs section around a generated uuid4 per instance that rotates on chat clear.
- Replace the `"default"` / per-user override rationale, which rests on the false premise.
- Check the link into this page from `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/durableobject.mdx:31`; the page moved to `agent-tracing/` and nothing else needs moving.

heading: The page for Remix on Cloudflare Workers contradicts the verified run
title: Rewrite the Remix on Cloudflare page for Workers and fix the Vite plugin options
body:
`docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/remix.mdx` is 60 lines and does not describe a working Workers setup: `:39-49` installs only `@sentry/remix` with no `@sentry/cloudflare`, and `:55-58` embeds the shared include. In that include, the Cloudflare branch at `platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.remix.mdx:250-294` covers Cloudflare Pages only, and the "Capture Server-Side Errors" step at `:296-329` sits outside any PlatformSection and tells every reader to import from bare `@sentry/remix` at `:314`. Separately, `guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx:30` presents `_experimental.useDiagnosticsChannelInjection` as something you must enable.

Verified on the develop line: Remix v2 (2.17.5) with the Remix Vite plugin on workerd, `compatibility_date: "2026-05-01"`, `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]`. Install `@sentry/remix` and `@sentry/cloudflare`; npm needs `--legacy-peer-deps`, because `@remix-run/cloudflare` pins `@cloudflare/workers-types` `^4` while wrangler 4 pins `^5`. In `app/entry.server.tsx`, `export const handleError = sentryHandleError` imported from `@sentry/remix/cloudflare`. In the worker entry, `Sentry.withSentry()` from `@sentry/cloudflare` around a handler built with `createRequestHandler(instrumentBuild(remixBuild))`; do not reach for `makeWrappedCreateRequestHandler` from `@sentry/remix/cloudflare` as well, which on Cloudflare reports every request twice, as two `http.server` transactions in two different traces. In `vite.config.ts`, `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` from `@sentry/cloudflare/vite` at its defaults alongside the Remix plugin, with `ssr: { target: 'webworker', noExternal: ['mysql', /^@sentry\//, '@opentelemetry/api'] }` (`noExternal: true` is the blunt version of the same thing). Build with `remix vite:build`: a plain `vite build` under Vite 6 silently builds only the client and skips `build/server`.

This item prescribes `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` because that is what was run. The Remix Vite plugin's own Cloudflare behavior, `sentryRemixVitePlugin` from `@sentry/remix/vite`, which on the v11 line applies the build-time instrumentation transform itself, was not exercised in this audit.

Works today:

- Loader, action and resource-route errors, parameterized route names with `http.route`, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers, `db` spans from `mysql`, `Sentry.logger` logs.
- Per-request isolation, with the `withSentry` plus `instrumentBuild` entry above.

Known limits:

- Importing from bare `@sentry/remix` in a `webworker` SSR build leaves `handleError` undefined and captures nothing.
- `wrapRequestHandler` from `@sentry/cloudflare/request` establishes no request isolation on Workers: it is the one Cloudflare wrapper that never calls `setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy`, so under concurrency every `setTag`, `setUser` and request-data write is global to the isolate and bleeds into unrelated later requests, and no event carries request data at all. It exists for runtimes that cannot enable `nodejs_compat`, such as Shopify Oxygen.
- A route with no loader or action stays method-only.
- With `instrumentBuild` alone the event's `transaction` field is unset, because nothing calls `isolationScope.setTransactionName`, so error grouping loses the route.
- Without `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` there are no database spans and no warning; `mysql2` is unusable on workerd.

What to change:

- Rewrite `guides/cloudflare/frameworks/remix.mdx`: add `@sentry/cloudflare` to the install at `:39-49`, add a Workers entry section, point `handleError` at `@sentry/remix/cloudflare`, and add a database-spans section.
- Correct `guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx` to the shipped top-level options `buildTimeInstrumentation` and `autoInstrumentation`, both defaulting to `true`: the prose at `:30`, the snippets at `:40-47` and the `SdkOption` blocks at `:150-166`, which still document `_experimental.autoInstrumentation` and `_experimental.useDiagnosticsChannelInjection` as defaulting to `false`.
- Add the `wrapRequestHandler` isolation warning to the two Hydrogen pages that document exactly that shape, `guides/cloudflare/frameworks/hydrogen-remix.mdx` and `guides/cloudflare/frameworks/hydrogen-react-router.mdx`.

heading: The page for Elysia on Cloudflare Workers contradicts the verified run
title: Add an Elysia on Cloudflare Workers page and drop the Bun/Node-only runtime claim
body:
No page mentions Elysia on Cloudflare Workers. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/elysia/index.mdx:25` lists the prerequisites as "Bun or Node.js 18+ (with @elysiajs/node adapter)" and the install tabs at `:55-60` plus the config snippet at `:82` cover Bun and Node only. `platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:3-5` promises a span for every Elysia lifecycle phase (`request_handler.elysia` for Handle, `middleware.elysia` for the rest) with no runtime qualifier, and `:9-12` has a "Runtime Behavior" section covering exactly two runtimes. The Cloudflare framework list at `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23` has no Elysia entry and `guides/cloudflare/frameworks/` has no `elysia.mdx`.

Verified on the develop line: Elysia 1.4.30 on workerd with `compatibility_date: "2026-05-01"` and `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]`. Install `@sentry/cloudflare @sentry/elysia elysia`. Construct the app as `withElysia(new Elysia({ aot: false }))` before any route is registered, and export `Sentry.withSentry((env) => ({ dsn: env.SENTRY_DSN, tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }), { fetch: request => app.fetch(request) })`. Do not call `init` from `@sentry/elysia` on Workers: its `sdk.js` imports `node:os` and `@sentry/bun`, so the Worker fails to build; `Sentry.withSentry` from `@sentry/cloudflare` is what supplies the client, and `withElysia` is the only part of `@sentry/elysia` used. Ahead-of-time compilation must be off: with the default, workerd refuses to start the Worker because Elysia's generated handler runs `new Function` and touches randomness in global scope. For database spans, build with Vite: `plugins: [cloudflare(), sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()]` from `@sentry/cloudflare/vite`, then `vite build` and point wrangler at the emitted config.

Works today:

- Unhandled errors via Elysia's global error hook, parameterized route names, per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans with headers, `Sentry.logger` logs, and `db` spans through the Vite build.

Known limits:

- A `wrangler`-bundled Worker emits no database spans.
- No Elysia lifecycle spans on Workers: every transaction comes back with `spans: []`, because the `app.trace()` handler that creates them depends on `rootSpanForRequest`, which only the Bun branch of `app.wrap` populates.
- `withElysia` must wrap the instance before routes are registered, or only the error path gets the route name.
- `mysql2` on workerd needs `disableEval: true` in the connection options, and the pool must be created at module scope.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/elysia.mdx` with the wiring above and list it at `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23`.
- Add a Cloudflare Workers entry to `guides/elysia/index.mdx:25`, add a Cloudflare bullet to the Runtime Behavior list at `platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:9-12`, and scope the lifecycle-span promise at `:3-5` to Bun and Node so it no longer reads as universal.

heading: The page for Elysia on Deno contradicts the verified run
title: Document Elysia on Deno: init from @sentry/deno, or add denoServeIntegration
body:
`docs/platforms/javascript/guides/elysia/index.mdx:25` lists prerequisites as Bun or Node 18+ with the node adapter, and the install and configure snippets at `:52-70` and `:78-120` have only Bun and Node tabs, with `Sentry.init` imported from `@sentry/elysia`. `platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:9-12` enumerates exactly two runtimes and `:6` claims parameterized route names unconditionally. A grep for `deno` over the Elysia guide returns nothing.

Verified on Elysia 1.4.30 and Deno 2.9.0: install the packages with npm into a real `node_modules`, set `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}` in `deno.json`, and pick one of two wirings. (1) Call `Sentry.init()` from `@sentry/deno` before `Deno.serve` and import only `withElysia` (and `fetchIntegration`) from `@sentry/elysia`. (2) Keep `Sentry.init()` from `@sentry/elysia` and pass `integrations: [denoServeIntegration()]`, imported from `@sentry/deno`. Both need `@sentry/deno` installed alongside `@sentry/elysia`; both were exercised in the `static` and `stream` trace lifecycles. Mount with `Deno.serve({ port }, withElysia(new Elysia()).get(...).fetch)`. Add `import "@sentry/deno/import";` as the first line for database spans, and pass `integrations: [fetchIntegration()]` for outgoing requests.

Works today:

- Route errors, mechanism `auto.http.elysia.on_error`.
- `GET /users/:id` with op `http.server` and source `route`, with the Elysia lifecycle phases as child spans.
- Per-request isolation and incoming trace continuation, with either wiring.
- Outgoing `http.client` spans plus `sentry-trace`/`baggage`, with `fetchIntegration()`, which `@sentry/elysia` exports (it re-exports the `@sentry/bun` integration).
- Database spans for `mysql`, and logs.

Known limits:

- `@sentry/elysia`'s own `init()` on its own delegates to `@sentry/bun` and does not instrument `Deno.serve`: there is no `http.server` span, every Elysia lifecycle phase becomes its own root transaction on one process-wide trace, incoming trace headers are ignored and the isolation scope carries the previous request's route into the next event. An outgoing `fetch` still produces an `http.client` span under the default `stream` lifecycle, but as a parentless segment; under `static` it is dropped for having no active span.
- The wiring decides the reported SDK: with `Sentry.init` from `@sentry/deno` events carry `sdk.name: sentry.javascript.deno`; with the `denoServeIntegration()` variant they keep `sentry.javascript.bun` and `contexts.runtime.name: bun`, and sessions are emitted.
- `mysql2` cannot be imported while the Deno import hook is active: Deno compiles `require('*.json')` as JavaScript (denoland/deno#36240) and the import throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'`. Use `mysql@2`.

What to change:

- `guides/elysia/index.mdx:25` and the snippets at `:52-70`, `:78-120`: add Deno tabs with both wirings described above.
- `platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:6,9-12`: add a Deno bullet and qualify the route-name claim.
- `common/configuration/integrations/fetchIntegration.mdx:10`: it states the integration "only works inside the Cloudflare Workers runtime", which the Deno runs disprove.

heading: The page for Nuxt on Bun contradicts the verified run
title: Add a Bun section to the Nuxt Nitro deployment presets page
body:
`docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/features/nitro-deployment-presets.mdx:7` says the presets "work out of the box" and `nitro-deployment-presets.mdx:9-11` carves out only Cloudflare Pages, while the documented start command at `guides/nuxt/index.mdx:72` is `node --import ./.output/server/sentry.server.config.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`. Nothing under `guides/nuxt/` mentions Bun.

Verified on Nuxt 4.5.2 (Nitro 2.13.4) with `@sentry/nuxt` 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on Bun 1.4.0: build with `NITRO_PRESET=bun npx nuxt build` and run with `bun run .output/server/index.mjs`. No inject mode and no start-up flag are needed: on develop, commit ec50b3e8f1 bundles `sentry.server.config.ts` into the Nitro build and imports it from a generated Nitro plugin, so `Sentry.init` runs at server startup by itself. Both `autoInjectServerSentry` modes are deprecated as of that commit and keep working until v12. The `sentry.server.config.ts` source file stays where it is, but it is no longer emitted to `.output/server/sentry.server.config.mjs`, which also makes the Node start command at `nuxt/index.mdx:72` obsolete on both runtimes. What Bun does need is the server instrumentation: install `@sentry/bun` alongside `@sentry/nuxt` and pass `integrations: [bunServerIntegration(), fetchIntegration()]` from it to the existing `Sentry.init` in `sentry.server.config.ts`. The root cause is a runtime gap rather than a preset choice: Bun never publishes the `http.server.request.start` diagnostics-channel event the Node instrumentation opens the request span from (measured: 0 events on Bun against 1 on Node), so no preset avoids it. `bunServerIntegration()` is the right integration for the `bun` preset, which serves through `Bun.serve`; the default `node-server` preset also runs under Bun, yields zero spans, and needs `bunHttpServerIntegration()` instead. The capability list below rests on the three recorded follow-up runs, which all prescribe `bunServerIntegration()` alone; the pairing with `fetchIntegration()` was exercised in a further run whose result was never recorded, and that run also observed that with `fetchIntegration()` alone the `http.client` span is a root span rather than a child of the request.

Works today, with `bunServerIntegration()` added:

- Unhandled server-route errors via the Nitro error hook, with or without the extra integrations
- `http.server` spans named `GET /users/:id` with source `route`, `http.route`, and the `url.path.parameter.id` and `params.id` attributes
- Per-request isolation and a fresh trace per request
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation
- `mysql2` database spans, provided `nitro: { externals: { external: ['mysql2'] } }` is set in `nuxt.config.ts`
- `Sentry.logger` log envelopes
- Events keep `sdk: sentry.javascript.nuxt` and the Nuxt event processors throughout

Known limits:

- Without `bunServerIntegration()` there is no request span at all: every event in the process shares one trace id, a stale `transaction` name leaks from an unrelated earlier request onto every later event, names are not route-based, incoming trace headers are ignored, and the mysql2 span is dropped as well, because its subscriber is bound with `requiresParentSpan: true` and has no request span to attach to.
- The `nitro.externals.external` entry and the database span are two separate problems. Without the entry the query itself fails with `genFunc$1 is not a function`, with or without Sentry; with the entry but without `bunServerIntegration()` the query succeeds and no span is recorded.
- Drivers that rely on Sentry's build-time channel injection, `mysql` v2 among them, must stay inside the Nitro bundle. Bun installs no runtime require hook, so an externalized driver of that kind is never instrumented.
- Unparameterized routes stay method-only (`GET`) under the `stream` default and take the URL path (`GET /api/ping`) under `traceLifecycle: 'static'`; the source is `url` in both.
- Manually captured events still carry no `transaction` field, even after the request span exists.

What to change:

- `guides/nuxt/features/nitro-deployment-presets.mdx`: add a Bun section next to the Cloudflare Pages one covering `NITRO_PRESET=bun npx nuxt build`, `bun run .output/server/index.mjs`, the two `@sentry/bun` integrations (with `bunHttpServerIntegration()` as the `node-server` variant) and the Nitro externals rule.
- `guides/nuxt/index.mdx:72`: the `node --import ./.output/server/sentry.server.config.mjs` command no longer matches the SDK, which bundles the server config into the Nitro build; replace it and add `bun run .output/server/index.mjs` for Bun.
- `guides/nuxt/install/limited-server-tracing.mdx:32` documents `autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import'`, which is now deprecated, and the warning at `:16-23` and `:19` claims that mode "will not capture data from database calls, queues, ORMs, third-party libraries" — a Node control run with exactly that setting produced `db SELECT users`, `db mysql2.pool.connect` and `http.client` spans, so the restriction as written is stronger than the SDK's behaviour.
- Document the alternative and its cost: replacing the whole init with `@sentry/bun` in `sentry.server.config.ts` produces the same spans, but events then report `sdk: sentry.javascript.bun` and the Nuxt event processors are dropped.

heading: The page for Nuxt on Deno contradicts the verified run
title: Correct the Nuxt Nitro preset page for Deno: keep the node-server preset
body:
`docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/features/nitro-deployment-presets.mdx:7` claims that the SDK supports different Nitro deployment presets, "most of which work out of the box", and the 11-line file then documents only Cloudflare Pages at `:9-11`. The Nuxt guide has no Deno mention anywhere, so a reader picking the `deno_server` preset gets no warning. `guides/nuxt/install/cli-import.mdx:37` gives the start command as `node --import ...`, which has no Deno equivalent.

Verified on Nuxt 4.5.2 with `@sentry/nuxt` 10.67.0 and Deno 2.9.0: do not set a Nitro preset. Build the default `node-server` output with `npx nuxt build`, keep `sentry: { autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import' }` in `nuxt.config.ts` and a root `sentry.server.config.ts` that calls `Sentry.init()`, then run the output under Deno with `cd .output/server && PORT=<port> deno run --allow-net --allow-read --allow-write --allow-env --allow-sys --allow-ffi --unstable-byonm ./index.mjs`. Nitro's node-server entry uses `node:http`, which the SDK instruments on Deno, and the module injects the config import into the entry correctly with this preset. For database drivers add `nitro: { externals: { inline: ['generate-function', 'named-placeholders'] } }`. For outgoing requests, add `winterCGFetchIntegration()` from `@sentry/vercel-edge` to `Sentry.init`.

Works today:

- Errors from nitro route handlers, with request data and source context.
- Parameterized `GET /api/users/:id` with source `route`, in both trace lifecycles, and `getActiveSpan()` defined inside handlers. A control run of the same output under Node produced the same shape.
- Database spans for `mysql2`, with the `externals.inline` entry above; on the node-server output they attach to ordinary route handlers with no code change.
- `http.client` spans and `sentry-trace`/`baggage` on `fetch` and nitro's `$fetch`, with `winterCGFetchIntegration()`. It was measured on the `deno_server` build under the default `stream` lifecycle, and `@sentry/vercel-edge` is an extra package to install.
- Logs.

Known limits:

- With `nitro: { preset: 'deno_server' }` there is no request instrumentation at all: no `http.server` spans, `getActiveSpan()` is undefined in handlers, every request shares one isolation scope and one trace id so tags and users leak, and incoming trace headers are ignored.
- With `deno_server` and `autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import'`, the module writes the config import into a file literally named `.output/server/deno.json start` instead of the entry, so the wrapper entry that imports `./sentry.server.config.mjs` before `./index.mjs` has to be written by hand.
- Under `deno_server` with `traceLifecycle: 'static'`, an outgoing `fetch` outside an explicit `Sentry.startSpan` is dropped with `no_parent_span`, because there is no server span to parent it to.
- Outgoing `fetch` is not instrumented on Deno without the integration above.
- Route-name enrichment does not run on error responses, on Deno and on Node alike: a thrown handler reports `GET /api/users/boom` with source `url`.
- The runtime debug line "Bundler plugin ran, injected libraries=[]" does not mean instrumentation is missing; that list is only filled during the build.
- Per-request isolation and incoming trace continuation were measured only on the `deno_server` build, where they fail. They are not yet measured on the node-server output.

What to change:

- `guides/nuxt/features/nitro-deployment-presets.mdx:7`: qualify the "work out of the box" claim; add a Deno section next to Cloudflare Pages at `:9` with the run command and the `deno_server` warning.
- `guides/nuxt/install/cli-import.mdx:37`: the `node --import` start command has no Deno equivalent; give the `deno run` form for the node-server output.
- Cross-link a Deno framework page for Nuxt.

heading: The page for Astro on Bun contradicts the verified run
title: Name Bun in the Astro runtime alert and add a Running on Bun section
body:
The runtime alert at `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/index.mdx:21-29` says the SDK "currently only works on Node runtimes, such as Node adapter or Vercel with Lambda functions" and that other non-Node runtimes are not supported (`:23-27`), which reads as excluding Bun. Nothing under `guides/astro/` mentions Bun, and nothing under `guides/bun/` mentions Astro.

Verified on Astro 7.3.1 with the `@astrojs/node` ^11.1.5 standalone adapter and `@sentry/astro` 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on Bun 1.4.0 and re-run on 1.4.2: in `astro.config.mjs` set `output: 'server'`, the `node({ mode: 'standalone' })` adapter, `sentry({ sourcemaps: { disable: true }, enabled: { client: false, server: true } })` and `vite: { ssr: { noExternal: ['mysql2'] } }`, which is required for build-time database instrumentation. Put a root `sentry.server.config.mjs` guarded with `Sentry.isInitialized()`, run `astro build`, then `bun --preload ./sentry.server.config.mjs dist/server/entry.mjs`. The preload is required, because the integration injects the init only into `.astro` page chunks, so an app whose first request hits an API route would otherwise run uninstrumented. Install `@sentry/bun` and add its `fetchIntegration()` to the server init, guarded on `typeof globalThis.Bun !== 'undefined'` so Node deployments of the same build do not double-count. Database spans need one more workaround for a Bun bug: Bun's `node:diagnostics_channel` does not keep a channel alive once it has subscribers, so the SDK reads `hasSubscribers = true` while the injected wrapper reads `false`. Pin the channels on `globalThis` next to `Sentry.init()` in `sentry.server.config.mjs` — `globalThis.__sentryPinnedChannels ??= ['mysql2:query', 'mysql2:execute', 'mysql2:connect', 'mysql2:pool:connect', 'orchestrion:mysql:query', 'orchestrion:mysql2:query', 'orchestrion:mysql2:execute'].map(name => dc.tracingChannel(name))` — which is harmless on Node and can be applied unconditionally. Loading the driver early is not a substitute here: it fixes mysql2 and not `mysql`@2.

Works today:

- Unhandled endpoint errors via the Astro request middleware, mechanism `auto.middleware.astro`
- Route names `GET /users/[id]` with source `route` and `http.route`
- Per-request isolation across concurrent requests
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation
- Outgoing `fetch` spans and propagation headers, with `fetchIntegration()` added
- `mysql2` and `mysql`@2 database spans on both lifecycles and both mysql2 code paths, with the channel pin above
- `Sentry.logger` log envelopes

Known limits:

- The build needs a `@sentry/bundler-plugins` matching this SDK line; with an older one `npx astro build` dies with "The requested module @sentry/core does not provide an export named ServerRuntimeClient".
- `contexts.runtime` reports `node` on Bun, so Bun events cannot be told apart from Node ones in Sentry.
- ContextLines prints `Failed to read file: native` once per captured event on Bun.
- Errors thrown while an `.astro` page renders were not exercised; the error probe is an endpoint. Browser-side capture was not exercised either, because the run used `enabled: { client: false, server: true }`.

What to change:

- `guides/astro/index.mdx:21-29`: amend the alert to name Bun as working on the Node adapter output.
- Add a "Running on Bun" section to that page with the `bun --preload ./sentry.server.config.mjs dist/server/entry.mjs` start command, the `astro.config.mjs` options above, the runtime-gated `fetchIntegration()`, the channel pin and the capability list.

heading: The page for Astro on Deno contradicts the verified run
title: Correct the Astro runtime note: Deno with @deno/astro-adapter works
body:
`docs/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/index.mdx:21-29` carries an Alert titled "What runtime do you use?" saying the SDK only works on Node runtimes such as the Node adapter or Vercel with Lambda functions, pointing Cloudflare users elsewhere, and calling other non-Node runtimes not supported. That reads as excluding Deno. `grep -rni deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/` returns zero hits, and `guides/deno/` never mentions Astro.

Verified on Astro 7.3.1 in SSR mode (`output: 'server'`) with `@deno/astro-adapter` 0.6.0 and `@sentry/astro` 10.67.0 on Deno 2.9.0: install the packages with `npm install` into a real `node_modules` rather than `deno add`, set `deno.json` to `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}`, add the `sentry()` integration in `astro.config.mjs`, keep a root `sentry.server.config.js` that calls `Sentry.init()`, add a `src/middleware.ts` whose first line imports that config, build normally and run the built `dist/server/entry.mjs` with Deno. The middleware is a required step, not a convenience: without it `Sentry.init` never runs for requests that only hit `.ts`/`.js` endpoint routes, so those requests produce nothing at all.

Works today:

- Route errors, mechanism `auto.middleware.astro`, with request URL and source context.
- `GET /users/[id]` with source `route`, in both trace lifecycles.
- Per-request isolation across concurrent requests.
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation.
- Database spans for `mysql2`, injected by the Vite plugin `@sentry/astro` adds during `astro build`.
- Logs.

Known limits:

- Outgoing `fetch()` is not instrumented on Deno: no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers, so the downstream service starts a new trace. Adding `fetchIntegration` from `@sentry/cloudflare` in `sentry.server.config.js` restores both, but `@sentry/astro` does not depend on `@sentry/cloudflare`, so that package has to be installed on purpose. Calls made with `node:http`/`node:https` are traced without it, and a call wrapped in `Sentry.startSpan` with headers taken from `Sentry.getTraceData()` also works.
- A route that only exists as a `.ts`/`.js` endpoint is uninstrumented unless `src/middleware.ts` imports the server config.

What to change:

- `guides/astro/index.mdx:21-29`: amend the Alert to name Deno as a supported runtime and link out.
- Add a Deno framework page for Astro with the `@deno/astro-adapter` setup, the mandatory middleware import, the `npm install @sentry/cloudflare` step and the `fetchIntegration` snippet.
- `common/configuration/integrations/fetchIntegration.mdx:10`: it says the integration "only works inside the Cloudflare Workers runtime", which this run disproves.

heading: The page for SvelteKit on Deno contradicts the verified run
title: Correct the SvelteKit adapter note: adapter-node runs on Deno
body:
`docs/platforms/javascript/guides/sveltekit/manual-setup__v10.7.0.mdx:21-36` holds the "Notes on SvelteKit adapter compatibility" section, whose "Currently not supported" heading at `:31` is followed at `:32` by a bullet saying non-Node server runtimes are not yet supported, while `:28` lists adapter-node as fully supported. That reads as excluding Deno, and the current `manual-setup.mdx` has no adapter-and-runtime section at all. `grep -rni deno` over the SvelteKit guide returns nothing.

Verified on SvelteKit with adapter-node and `@sentry/sveltekit` 10.67.0 on Deno 2.9.0: build with `vite build` under Node, using `sentrySvelteKit()` imported from `@sentry/sveltekit/vite`, then start the adapter output with `HOST=<host> PORT=<port> deno run --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys --allow-ffi build/index.js`. For outgoing requests, register `fetchIntegration` from `@sentry/cloudflare`, already installed as a dependency of `@sentry/sveltekit`, in `src/hooks.server.js`, gated on Deno so Node builds are not double-instrumented. For `mysql2`, prime its `package.json` in the CJS require cache before the SDK installs its module hooks, either with a preload file (`createRequire(import.meta.url)('mysql2/package.json')` started through `deno run --preload ./prewarm-json.mjs`) or with the same two lines at the very top of `src/hooks.server.js`.

Works today:

- Errors from `+server.js` handlers, mechanism `auto.function.sveltekit.handle_error`.
- `GET /users/[id]` with source `route`.
- Per-request isolation and incoming trace continuation.
- `http.client` spans plus `sentry-trace`/`baggage`, with `fetchIntegration()`.
- Database spans for `mysql` with no extra flags, and for `mysql2` with the prewarm above, parented under the SvelteKit `http.server` span in both trace lifecycles.
- Logs.

Known limits:

- Without `fetchIntegration()`, neither a global `fetch()` nor SvelteKit's `event.fetch` produces an `http.client` span or carries trace headers on Deno.
- `mysql2` fails on first use unless its `package.json` is in the require cache before `Sentry.init`: Deno compiles `require('*.json')` as JavaScript while a module hook is registered (denoland/deno#36240), and the route throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'`. The prewarm above is the fix; `mysql` needs nothing.
- The "@sentry/server-runtime-injection was bundled into your application" warning can fire on Deno while instrumentation is working, so it is no signal of a broken setup.

What to change:

- Fix `manual-setup__v10.7.0.mdx:21-36` to name Deno with adapter-node as supported.
- Restore an adapter-and-runtime section in `manual-setup.mdx` and add a Deno framework page with the run command and the `fetchIntegration` snippet.
- `common/configuration/integrations/fetchIntegration.mdx:10`: it says the integration "only works inside the Cloudflare Workers runtime", which this run disproves.

heading: The Bun integrations table lists three integrations that are not installed and omits twelve that are
title: Correct the Bun integrations table in platform-includes/.../javascript.bun.mdx
body:
`platform-includes/configuration/integrations/javascript.bun.mdx:5-37` lists `dedupeIntegration` (`:9`), `nativeNodeFetchIntegration` (`:24`) and `inboundFiltersIntegration` (`:14`) as auto-enabled, and `pinoIntegration` at `:47`, while `fsIntegration` is shown for Bun with no row.

What was observed: the Bun SDK installs 42 integrations at `6f2da7483d`, and 43 on develop head, where `mastraIntegration()` joined `getTracingIntegrations()`. It ships `fetchIntegration` rather than `nativeNodeFetchIntegration`, installs inbound filtering as `EventFilters`, and does not install `dedupeIntegration`. Integrations installed with no row in the table: `fetchIntegration`, `bunHttpServerIntegration`, `processSessionIntegration`, `expressIntegration`, `fastifyIntegration`, `hapiIntegration`, `koaIntegration`, `awsIntegration`, `langGraphIntegration`, `postgresJsIntegration`, `spanStreamingIntegration` and `mastraIntegration`. The list is produced by `getDefaultIntegrations()` in `packages/bun/src/sdk.ts:77-79`, which spreads `getDefaultIntegrationsWithoutPerformance()` at `:47-74`, plus `packages/server-utils/src/integrations/index.ts:30-62` (`:30-63` on develop head). `spanStreamingIntegration` is not part of that list: the client adds it in `packages/core/src/server-runtime-client.ts:56`, so a table generated from `getDefaultIntegrations()` alone would still miss it. The channel-based integrations only produce spans after a `Bun.build` with `@sentry/bun/plugin`.

What to change:

- Drop the `dedupeIntegration` row; rename `nativeNodeFetchIntegration` to `fetchIntegration`; rename `inboundFiltersIntegration` to the installed `eventFiltersIntegration`.
- Add rows for the twelve installed integrations listed above.
- Add a "Requires `@sentry/bun/plugin`" column and tick it for the channel-based rows.
- Fix the gating so `common/configuration/integrations/pino.mdx` is shown for Bun, and give `fsIntegration` a row or hide it.

heading: Express, Koa, Hapi, Fastify and Next.js work on Bun and no page says so; Hono has an undocumented bundling caveat
title: Add a frameworks page to the Bun guide and a Bun caveat to the Hono guide
body:
The Bun guide has no frameworks section, and `guides/express/`, `guides/fastify/`, `guides/koa/`, `guides/hapi/` and `guides/nextjs/` contain no mention of the Bun runtime (the seven case-insensitive matches under `guides/nextjs/` are "Bunyan" and "bundle"). `guides/hono/index.mdx:12,84-85,278-280` covers Bun; `guides/elysia/index.mdx:5` inherits from Bun.

Observed on bun 1.4.0: under `bun run`, Express, Koa, Hapi and Fastify produce URL-named server transactions (`GET /user/42`, source `url`), no child spans and no captured error. After `Bun.build` with `sentryBunPlugin`, the same apps produce route-named transactions (`GET /user/:id`, `GET /user/{id}` on Hapi), middleware/router/handler spans and captured errors (`auto.http.express`, `auto.middleware.koa`, `auto.function.hapi`, `auto.function.fastify`), matching Node. Hono via `@sentry/hono/bun` works with `bun run` and after bundling only while `hono` stays external; with `hono` inlined, transactions fall back to `GET /user/42` and no error is captured. The per-framework Bun items DOC-F1 to DOC-F17 carry the verified wiring for every other framework.

What to change:

- Add `guides/bun/frameworks/index.mdx` with a table: framework, behavior under `bun run`, behavior after `Bun.build` + plugin, guide to follow.
- Note that database clients must be created at module scope.
- Add a "Bun" pointer to the Express, Fastify, Koa and Hapi guides.
- Add "keep `hono` external when bundling" to the Hono guide's Bun tab.

heading: The guide never mentions the runtime hook or which instrumentation is automatic
title: Document the @sentry/deno/import hook in the Deno guide
body:
`guides/deno/index.mdx` renders `import * as Sentry from "npm:@sentry/deno"` through the `___SDK_PACKAGE___` placeholder at `:44` and `:66` (the literal specifier is not in the file), and shows two permission flags. It never states that the database, messaging, AI and framework integrations in the default set require the `@sentry/deno/import` hook, nor that the `Deno.serve` and `node:http` server spans work without it. `packages/deno/README.md:60-83` has a version of this section, but its `--import=@sentry/deno/import` form at `:70` does not resolve.

What was observed on deno 2.9.0 and 2.8.3: a first-line `import '@sentry/deno/import';` before `Sentry.init` registers the hook and instruments `mysql.createConnection`. `--import=@sentry/deno/import` fails with `Module not found`; `--import=./node_modules/@sentry/deno/build/import.mjs` registers the hook. Without the hook the SDK installs 39 integrations at `6f2da7483d`, reports no injection and prints nothing. The `deno-mysql` and `deno-pg` e2e apps use the first-line import form, with `nodeModulesDir: "manual"` and an installed `node_modules`. Any dependency that `require()`s a JSON file currently crashes under the hook.

What to change:

- Add an "Enable library instrumentation" step to `guides/deno/index.mdx` with first-line `import '@sentry/deno/import';` as the primary form.
- State that the hook needs the package resolvable from `node_modules`, so `deno.json` has to set `nodeModulesDir` to `"auto"`, or to `"manual"` with an install step, which is what every Deno e2e app does.
- Show the file-path `--import` flag as the alternative; do not show the bare specifier form.
- State that dependencies which `require()` a JSON file fail to import under the hook.
- State which instrumentation works without the hook.

heading: The Deno integrations table lists 8 auto-enabled integrations; the SDK installs 40
title: Correct the Deno integrations table in platform-includes/.../javascript.deno.mdx
body:
`platform-includes/configuration/integrations/javascript.deno.mdx:5-12` lists eight auto-enabled integrations: `breadcrumbs`, `contextLines`, `dedupe`, `denoContext`, `functionToString`, `globalHandlers`, `inboundFilters`, `linkedErrors`. Row `:21` has five cells instead of six, so `zodErrors` renders a check under the Cron column.

What was observed: the Deno SDK installs 39 integrations at `6f2da7483d` and 40 on develop head, where `mastraIntegration()` joined `getTracingIntegrations()`. Beyond the eight in the table it adds `RequestData`, `DenoServe`, `DenoHttp`, `NormalizePaths`, `Express`, `Fastify`, `Hapi`, `Koa`, `Graphql`, `Mongo`, `Mongoose`, `Mysql`, `Mysql2`, `Redis`, `Postgres`, `Prisma`, `Tedious`, `GenericPool`, `Kafka`, `Amqplib`, `LruMemoizer`, `Aws`, `LangChain`, `LangGraph`, `VercelAI`, `OpenAI`, `Anthropic_AI`, `Google_GenAI`, `PostgresJs`, `Firebase`, `SpanStreaming` and, on develop head, `Mastra`. `DenoServe` and `DenoHttp` produce every Deno transaction. Outgoing `fetch` produces breadcrumbs only. The library integrations need the `@sentry/deno/import` hook. The installed list comes from `packages/deno/src/sdk.ts:28-49`.

What to change:

- Rewrite the table from `packages/deno/src/sdk.ts:28-49` so every installed integration has a row.
- Add a "Requires `@sentry/deno/import`" column and tick the library, messaging and AI rows.
- Add rows for `denoServeIntegration` and `denoHttpIntegration`, noting they produce Deno transactions, and state that outgoing `fetch` yields breadcrumbs only.
- Fix the cell count of row `:21`.
- Remove `javascript.deno` from the `supported:` list of the `modules`, `onuncaughtexception`, `unhandledrejection` and `console` common pages.
- Remove `javascript.deno` from the `notSupported` list of `common/configuration/integrations/breadcrumbs.mdx`: the Deno SDK installs `breadcrumbsIntegration()` (`packages/deno/src/sdk.ts:39`) and exports it (`packages/deno/src/index.ts:164`).

heading: The permission section is incomplete and the two commands are shown as alternatives
title: Show one complete deno run command with all four permission flags in the Deno guide
body:
`guides/deno/index.mdx:100` shows `deno run --allow-net=<ingest> index.ts` and `:119` shows `deno run --allow-read=./src index.ts` as two separate commands, while the init snippets on the same page name the file `main.ts`. Neither `--allow-env` nor `--allow-sys` is mentioned, and `packages/deno/README.md` mentions no flag at all.

What was observed on deno 2.9.0: with only `--allow-net` and `--no-prompt`, events carry `server_name: null`, no OS version, an absolute filesystem path as the frame filename and no context lines. With the `@sentry/deno/import` hook line present, the same flags do not degrade but crash: `NotCapable: Requires env access, run again with the --allow-env flag`, raised from the vendored `debug` package inside `@sentry/server-runtime-injection` at module load (getting-started reproduction QS-deno, 2026-09-08). With all permissions granted, the same app reports the hostname, the OS version, an `app:///`-prefixed filename and context lines. No warning is printed in the restricted run. Every Deno e2e app runs with `--allow-net --allow-env --allow-read`; `deno-mysql`, `deno-pg` and `deno-redis` add `--allow-sys --allow-write`, and `deno-streamed` adds `--allow-sys`.

What to change:

- Replace the two commands at `:100` and `:119` with a single `deno run --allow-net=<ingest> --allow-read --allow-env --allow-sys main.ts`, using the same filename as the init snippets.
- Add a table naming what each flag unlocks: `--allow-net` event delivery, `--allow-read` source context lines and app-relative frame paths, `--allow-env` `SENTRY_*` lookups and `serverName`, `--allow-sys` hostname and OS version.
- Add the same table to `packages/deno/README.md`.

heading: Fastify and Hono work on Deno without the hook, Express, Koa and Hapi need it and crash with it, and no page says any of this
title: Add a frameworks page to the Deno guide and Deno notes to four Node framework guides
body:
The Deno guide has no frameworks section, and the Fastify, Express, Koa and Hapi guides contain no mention of Deno. Only `guides/hono/index.mdx:88-89,302-304` covers Deno.

What was observed on deno 2.9.0, with and without a first-line `import '@sentry/deno/import';`: Fastify works with no hook, producing `GET /user/:id` (source `route`), a handler span and an `auto.function.fastify` error, because Fastify publishes its own `node:diagnostics_channel` events. Hono via `@sentry/hono/deno` works with no hook. Express, Koa and Hapi without the hook produce URL-named transactions (`GET /user/42`, source `url`), no child spans and no captured error. With the hook, all three fail at import: Express and Hapi with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'`, Koa with `Cannot resolve module "./index.js"`. Fastify also fails at import under the hook. The per-framework Deno items DOC-F18 to DOC-F34 carry the verified wiring for every other framework.

What to change:

- Add `guides/deno/frameworks/index.mdx` with a table: framework, behavior without the hook, behavior with the hook, guide to follow.
- State plainly that Fastify and Hono are supported on Deno with no extra step, and that Express, Koa and Hapi produce URL-named server transactions without error capture, and fail to import under the hook.
- Add a "Deno" note to the Fastify guide (works as is) and to the Express, Koa and Hapi guides (server transactions only), each linking to the new page.

heading: Five places document the @sentry/cloudflare/nodejs_compat entrypoint that v11 removes
title: Remove the @sentry/cloudflare/nodejs_compat entrypoint from the Cloudflare docs for v11
body:
Five places document the `@sentry/cloudflare/nodejs_compat` entrypoint: the alert at `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:63`, the whole of `guides/cloudflare/features/nodejs-compat.mdx` (50 lines, the entrypoint at `:6` and `:10`), `guides/cloudflare/configuration/integrations/prisma.mdx:8`, `platform-includes/configuration/integrations/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:19`, and the two-entrypoint table in `common/agent-tracing/vercelai.mdx:66-71`, inside the Cloudflare section at `:60-73`.

What was observed: on `develop`, `@sentry/cloudflare` exposes only `.`, `./request` and `./vite`; importing `@sentry/cloudflare/nodejs_compat` fails with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`. The subpath still exists on the last released state. `MIGRATION.md:1394-1399` records the removal (`:1600-1605` at develop head), and `common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:948-959` already carries the migration half for upgraders. These five pages will be wrong when v11 ships.

What to change, in the v11 docs update:

- Delete `guides/cloudflare/features/nodejs-compat.mdx` and keep it available in the v10 version selector.
- Remove the alert at `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:63`.
- Rewrite the Prisma note at `configuration/integrations/prisma.mdx:8` and the entrypoint table in `common/agent-tracing/vercelai.mdx:66-71` to describe the single `@sentry/cloudflare` entry.
- Change `platform-includes/configuration/integrations/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:19` accordingly.

heading: features/d1.mdx documents a removed function and hides that D1 is automatic
title: Rewrite features/d1.mdx around automatic D1 instrumentation
body:
`guides/cloudflare/features/d1.mdx:6-16` is the whole body of the page and instructs the user to wrap their binding with `instrumentD1WithSentry(env.DB)` at `:13`.

What was observed: on `develop` that export is gone, and `withSentry` instruments every D1 binding found on `env` (`packages/cloudflare/src/instrumentations/worker/instrumentEnv.ts:64-68` at `6f2da7483d`, `:61-65` at develop head, recorded in `MIGRATION.md:1401-1416`). The automatic path is what `dev-packages/cloudflare-integration-tests/suites/d1` exercises. D1 spans use the `db.query` op, batches are named `D1 batch`, single queries are named by the sanitized query summary under the stream lifecycle and by the raw query under the static one (`instrumentD1.ts:137`), and the `cloudflare.d1.*` attributes are set in `instrumentD1.ts:114-116,142-146,178`. On the released line the wrapper already has no effect beyond the automatic instrumentation, and the page does not say so. The page will be wrong when v11 ships.

What to change:

- Rewrite `features/d1.mdx` to state that D1 bindings on `env` are instrumented automatically by `withSentry`, with no per-binding call.
- Document the span op `db.query`, the `D1 batch` span name, the query-summary naming for single queries, and the `cloudflare.d1.*` attributes listed above.
- Replace the `instrumentD1WithSentry` snippet with a note that the function exists before 11.0 and is not needed.

heading: The Vite plugin page documents _experimental options that no longer exist and says the plugin is a no-op by default
title: Update features/vite-plugin.mdx to the shipped Cloudflare Vite plugin options
body:
`guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx:150-166` documents `_experimental` (`:150-154`), `_experimental.autoInstrumentation` (default `false`, `:156-160`) and `_experimental.useDiagnosticsChannelInjection` (default `false`, `:162-166`), with the claim at `:164` that "When disabled or omitted, the plugin is a no-op". `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:77-92` passes `useDiagnosticsChannelInjection: true`. The page carries an experimental Alert at `:8-11` and names only `mysql` as an instrumented package (`:15`, `:59`).

What was observed: `packages/cloudflare/src/vite/index.ts:12-55` defines `wranglerConfigPath` (`:23`), `buildTimeInstrumentation` (default `true`, `:37`) and `autoInstrumentation` (default `true`, `:54`); a grep of `packages/cloudflare/src` for `_experimental` and `useDiagnosticsChannelInjection` returns nothing. `buildTimeInstrumentation` injects `diagnostics_channel.tracingChannel` calls into bundled packages; `autoInstrumentation` wraps the Worker entry with `withSentry` and configured Durable Object, Workflow, Agent and WorkerEntrypoint classes, in both `vite build` and `vite dev`. The instrumented packages are the entries in `packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/config/index.ts:50-80` (29 at `6f2da7483d`; `:51-81` and 30 at develop head, where Mastra was added). The new defaults are pinned by the `vite` and `vite-autoinstrument` integration suites. The page will be wrong when v11 ships.

What to change:

- Replace the two `_experimental` option blocks at `:150-166` with `buildTimeInstrumentation` and `autoInstrumentation`, with their real defaults and effects; keep the `wranglerConfigPath` entry at `:130-148`, which is already correct.
- Remove `useDiagnosticsChannelInjection` from the snippet at `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:77-92`.
- List the instrumented packages.
- Move the page out of the experimental section and remove the experimental Alert at `:8-11`.

heading: wrapRequestHandler is imported from the main entry, and the honoIntegration page survives its removal
title: Import wrapRequestHandler from @sentry/cloudflare/request and drop the honoIntegration page
body:
The "Don't have access to onRequest?" expandable at `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:207-238` holds a snippet at `:217-232` that imports `@sentry/cloudflare` at `:219` and calls `Sentry.wrapRequestHandler` at `:230`. `guides/cloudflare/configuration/integrations/hono.mdx:14` says `honoIntegration` is "enabled by default", under a deprecation Alert at `:8-12`.

What was observed: on `develop`, `wrapRequestHandler` is defined in `packages/cloudflare/src/request.ts:13` and reachable only through the `@sentry/cloudflare/request` subpath; the package exposes `.`, `./request` and `./vite`, and the main entry exports only `_INTERNAL_wrapRequestHandler` (`packages/cloudflare/src/index.ts:117`). The Hydrogen pages already use the subpath (`frameworks/hydrogen-react-router.mdx:187`, with prose at `:175` and `:179`). `honoIntegration` is deprecated on the released line and removed per `MIGRATION.md:1445-1453`; the integrations page is guide-local, so nothing hides it. The package README carries the same main-entry import (`packages/cloudflare/README.md:88` and `:99`). These pages will be wrong when v11 ships.

What to change:

- Change the import at `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:219` to `@sentry/cloudflare/request`.
- Delete `guides/cloudflare/configuration/integrations/hono.mdx`, which already carries a deprecation notice and needs removing rather than a second one.
