- Replace the bare redirect in `guides/cloudflare/frameworks/hono.mdx` with the install step and the `app.use(sentry())` wiring.
- Fix the `wrapRequestHandler` import in the `@sentry/cloudflare` README.

heading: The frameworks section is missing React Router, says "Pages", and the TanStack Start page cannot render its wrangler step
title: Add a Cloudflare React Router page and fix frameworks/index.mdx and tanstack-start.mdx
body:
`guides/cloudflare/frameworks/index.mdx:6` says the section is "to instrument your Cloudflare Pages applications", and `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23` lists eight frameworks. There is no `frameworks/react-router.mdx`. `frameworks/tanstack-start.mdx:54-57` pulls `getting-started-config` for platform `javascript.cloudflare.splitlayout`, for which no include file exists, so the wrangler step renders nothing; the page never installs `@sentry/tanstackstart-react` although its snippets at `:80,137,206` import it. `guides/tanstackstart-react/manual-setup/index.mdx:377` says "This setup doesn't work for Cloudflare deployments." with no link.

What was observed at `6f2da7483d`: of the 21 e2e apps that carry a wrangler config, only `sveltekit-cloudflare-pages` targets Pages. `react-router-8-cloudflare` wires `Sentry.withSentry` in `workers/app.ts:12` and `@sentry/react-router/cloudflare` in `app/entry.server.tsx:1`. `tanstackstart-react-cloudflare` is the reference wiring for TanStack Start. The per-framework Cloudflare items DOC-F35 to DOC-F51 carry the verified wiring for the remaining frameworks, including the ones with no first-party code path.

What to change:

- Add `frameworks/react-router.mdx` from the `react-router-8-cloudflare` wiring, and list React Router at `index.mdx:16-23`.
- Fix the include platform name at `tanstack-start.mdx:54-57` and add the `@sentry/tanstackstart-react` install step.
- Reword `frameworks/index.mdx:6` to cover Workers.
- Link the Cloudflare page from `guides/tanstackstart-react/manual-setup/index.mdx:377`.

heading: The v10-to-v11 page has no Bun section and names neither the Bun plugin nor the Deno import hook
title: Add the per-runtime channel-instrumentation setup to the v10-to-v11 page
body:
`common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx` covers the Cloudflare changes in detail (`:948-993`) and has a "Deno Changes" section at `:933-939`, but it names none of `@sentry/bun/plugin`, `sentryBunPlugin` or `@sentry/deno/import`, and it has no Bun section at all. Its `:689` tells the reader "Most setups need no changes.", the same framing as the channel-instrumentation section of the SDK's `MIGRATION.md:282-288`.

What was observed: on Bun, library and framework spans require a `Bun.build` with `sentryBunPlugin` from `@sentry/bun/plugin`, and are not produced under `bun run`. On Deno, they require a first-line `import '@sentry/deno/import';`. On Cloudflare, they require the Vite plugin from `@sentry/cloudflare/vite` with `buildTimeInstrumentation` left at its default. Each of these subpaths exists on `develop` and is exercised by the corresponding e2e apps and integration suites.

What to change:

- Add a Bun section to `common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx` with the `Bun.build({ plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` step and a sentence that `bun run` on unbundled source records no library or framework spans.
- Add the hook paragraph to the Deno section at `:933-939`: a first-line `import '@sentry/deno/import';` before `Sentry.init`, with the package resolvable from `node_modules`.
- Reword `:689` so "Most setups need no changes." does not stand for Bun and Deno, and say which runtime needs a build step and which needs an import.

heading: There is no runtime-by-framework or runtime-by-integration matrix, and every table is hand-maintained
title: Add a runtime-by-framework support matrix for Bun, Deno and Cloudflare
body:
There is no page comparing framework support across Bun, Deno and Cloudflare. Framework support is documented today only in the Hono guide (four runtimes), the Elysia guide, and the Cloudflare framework pages. The Cloudflare integrations table at `platform-includes/configuration/integrations/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:5-17` is missing four rows the SDK installs - `conversationIdIntegration`, `httpServerIntegration`, `consoleIntegration` and `spanStreamingIntegration` - and two of its existing rows are wrong: `:8` names `inboundFiltersIntegration` where the SDK installs `eventFiltersIntegration`, and `:17` marks `honoIntegration` auto-enabled although it is removed on `develop`.

What was observed across 51 verified framework and runtime cells on `develop`: 50 of the 51 combinations run. Hono, Astro, React Router and TanStack Start pass every capability on Cloudflare with the documented wiring. Every framework SDK runs on Bun and on Deno, with the wiring recorded in the per-framework items DOC-F1 to DOC-F51. Express, Koa, Hapi and NestJS run on Cloudflare Workers behind the `enable_nodejs_http_server_modules` compatibility flag. Fastify on Cloudflare Workers is the one combination that does not run. Outgoing `fetch` is not instrumented on Deno in any framework. The Cloudflare default set is `packages/cloudflare/src/baseSdk.ts:51-72` (dedupe, eventFilters, functionToString, conversationId, linkedErrors, fetch, httpServer, requestData, console, plus the registered channel subscribers) with `spanStreamingIntegration` added by `packages/core/src/server-runtime-client.ts:56`.

What to change:

- Add a runtime-by-framework matrix page with one row per framework and one column per runtime, each supported cell linking to the framework page or section for that runtime.
- Mark Fastify on Cloudflare as not supported, and note the Deno outgoing-fetch limit once, above the table.
- Add the four missing rows to the Cloudflare integrations table, rename `:8` to `eventFiltersIntegration`, and drop the `honoIntegration` row at `:17` with the integration (DOC-C5).

heading: The page for Hono on Bun misses the wiring or the limits
title: Document Hono on Bun: unbundled run and the Bun.build plugin variant
body:
The Hono guide names Bun at `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hono/index.mdx:12`, has a Bun install tab at `hono/index.mdx:84-86` and a Bun setup snippet at `hono/index.mdx:278-300`, but it never shows how to start the app or what the runtime delivers. The Bun guide teaches only `bun --preload ./instrument.js app.js` (`bun/index.mdx:100`) and carries a "Bundled Code Limitation" alert at `bun/index.mdx:90-94`. `sentryBunPlugin`, `@sentry/bun/plugin` and `Bun.build` appear nowhere in the docs.

Verified on Hono 4.13.x with `@sentry/hono/bun` 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on Bun 1.4.0 and re-run on 1.4.2: install `@sentry/hono` plus `@sentry/bun`, call `app.use(sentry(app, { dsn, tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }))` on a fresh `new Hono()`, export `{ port, fetch: app.fetch }`, and run `bun app.ts`. No instrument file and no `--preload` are needed, because the middleware calls `Sentry.init` itself. `traceLifecycle` defaults to `stream` on this line, which names the request span `http.server GET /users/:id` and the database span `db SELECT users`; under `traceLifecycle: 'static'` the same run gives a transaction `GET /users/:id` and a span `db SELECT * FROM users`. One Bun bug needs a workaround: Bun garbage-collects a `node:diagnostics_channel` channel that only Sentry's subscriber holds, so a driver whose first query happens later in the process silently loses its spans; pin the channels by keeping a strong reference right after the middleware is registered, `globalThis.__sentryPinnedChannels ??= ['mysql2:query', 'mysql2:execute', 'mysql2:connect', 'mysql2:pool:connect'].map(name => dc.tracingChannel(name))`, which is harmless on Node. Building the same entry with `Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./app.ts'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun', sourcemap: 'external', plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` from `@sentry/bun/plugin` and running `bun dist/app.js` adds spans for `mysql`@2; the bundled captures cover errors, route names, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch`, both database drivers and logs, and do not drive the isolation route.

Works today:

- Unhandled handler errors, with the route as the transaction name
- Parameterized route names (`GET /users/:id`, source `route`)
- Per-request isolation across concurrent requests
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation
- Outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers
- `mysql2` 3.20.0+ database spans with no build step, as long as the driver is loaded and queried early or the channels are pinned as above
- `Sentry.logger` log envelopes, flushed on a roughly 5 second timer and needing no `enableLogs` option

Known limits:

- Drivers that do not publish `node:diagnostics_channel` events themselves, such as `mysql`@2, produce spans only in the `Bun.build` bundle.
- Do not pass `external: ["@sentry/*"]` to `Bun.build` for a Hono app. Externalizing `@sentry/*` while `hono` is inlined gives two copies of hono's `GET_MATCH_RESULT` symbol and every request 500s inside `@sentry/hono`'s `requestHandler`. Either pass no `external` at all (the verified recipe), or externalize `hono` together with `@sentry/*`, which then behaves exactly like the unbundled run.

What to change:

- `guides/hono/index.mdx`: add a "Run your app" step with a Bun tab showing `bun app.ts` and the `Bun.build` + `sentryBunPlugin()` variant, state that the `--preload` step is not needed here, and name the span names a reader will see under the `stream` default and under `static`.
- `guides/bun/index.mdx:90-94`: rewrite the alert so it describes the plugin build as the supported way to instrument bundled code.
- `packages/hono/README.md:172-190`: the Bun section ends in the Node recipe (`serve` from `@hono/node-server`); replace it with the `export default app` form the docs page shows.

heading: The page for Elysia on Bun misses the wiring or the limits
title: Add a Bun database instrumentation section to the Elysia guide and fix four include statements
body:
The Bun wiring on the Elysia guide is correct; three statements around it are not. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/elysia/index.mdx:4-5` declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.elysia` with `fallbackGuide: javascript.bun`, `elysia/index.mdx:23-25` lists the prerequisites, `elysia/index.mdx:56` shows `bun add @sentry/elysia`, and the alert at `elysia/index.mdx:47-50` ("You do **not** need `@elysiajs/opentelemetry`") is confirmed by the run. The defects are in the includes: `platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:1` opens this server guide with a `BrowserTracing` paragraph; `javascript.elysia.mdx:5` claims the ops are `request_handler.elysia` and `middleware.elysia` where the observed ops are plain `handler` and `middleware`; and `platform-includes/performance/enable-stream-mode/javascript.elysia.mdx:25` says `'static'` is "the default" where this line defaults to `'stream'`. On top of that, nothing on the page or in its includes says how database and library instrumentation behaves on Bun.

Verified on Elysia 1.4 with `@sentry/elysia` 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on Bun 1.4.0: `Sentry.init` either inline in the entry or in an `instrument.ts` imported first, `Sentry.withElysia(new Elysia())` wrapping the fresh instance before any route is chained, then `bun app.ts`. No `--preload`, no `@elysiajs/opentelemetry`, and no build step for the base capabilities. For libraries that need the plugin build, build with `Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./app.ts'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun', sourcemap: 'external', plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` from `@sentry/bun/plugin` and run `bun dist/app.js`. Pass no `external` at all, and no `packages: 'external'` or `packages: '*'`: the follow-up run recorded that any of those puts the instrumented packages back outside the bundle and the spans disappear again. `sentryBunPlugin()` is build-only; calling `Bun.plugin(sentryBunPlugin())` from a `--preload` file crashes the app at import.

Works today:

- Unhandled handler errors via the SDK's global `onError` hook
- Route names `GET /users/:id` with source `route`, on the success and error paths
- Per-request isolation across concurrent requests
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation, plus response trace headers
- Outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers
- `mysql2` database spans under a plain `bun app.ts`; database instrumentation as a whole is recorded partial, and this is the half that works
- `Sentry.logger` log envelopes

Known limits:

- On Bun only libraries that publish `node:diagnostics_channel` events themselves are instrumented under a plain `bun app.ts`; every other instrumented library needs the plugin build above. The failure is silent: with `debug: true` the SDK logs "No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping" and still reports "Integration installed: Mysql", and without `debug` there is no output at all.
- Every event, transaction and span reports `sdk.name: "sentry.javascript.bun"`, never `sentry.javascript.elysia`, under both init placements and both lifecycles.
- Events captured inside a handler carry no transaction name, because the name is set after the handler runs.
- The SDK's own hooks are visible in every trace as `sentryOnRequest`, `sentryOnAfterHandle` and `sentryOnError` spans, and the first pool use adds `db mysql2.pool.connect` and `db mysql2.connect`.

What to change:

- `guides/elysia/index.mdx`: add a "Database and library instrumentation on Bun" section after Configure with the bundle recipe and the "no `external`" rule. Leave the alert at `:47-50` as it is; the run confirms it.
- `platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:11`: qualify "No additional runtime instrumentation needed" for the database and library case.
- `platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:1`: drop the `BrowserTracing` paragraph from this server guide.
- `platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:5`: the observed ops are `handler` and `middleware`, not `request_handler.elysia` and `middleware.elysia`.
- `platform-includes/performance/enable-stream-mode/javascript.elysia.mdx:25`: the `traceLifecycle` default is `'stream'`, not `'static'`. DOC-R1 covers javascript.bun.mdx, javascript.deno.mdx and javascript.cloudflare.mdx, not this file.

heading: No page documents Express on Bun
title: Add an Express on Bun page covering the Bun.build plugin step
body:
No guide page pairs Express with Bun. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/express/index.mdx:4-5` declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.node` with `fallbackGuide: javascript.node` and renders `getting-started-node` (`express/index.mdx:12`), whose only run shape is `node --import ./instrument.mjs app.mjs` (`platform-includes/getting-started-node/javascript.mdx:88,95`). The Bun guide teaches `bun --preload ./instrument.js app.js` (`guides/bun/index.mdx:100`) and names no framework. The pairing does exist elsewhere in the docs but never with instructions: 81 common integration pages list `javascript.express` and `javascript.bun` together in `supported:`, and `common/configuration/integrations/mysql2.mdx:30` states "This integration only works in the Node.js and Bun runtimes".

Verified on Express 4.22.1 with `@sentry/bun` 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on Bun 1.4.0 and re-run on 1.4.2: install `@sentry/bun` instead of `@sentry/node`, plus the `mysql` driver, put `Sentry.init` in `instrument.ts` imported as the first line of `app.ts`, create the database connection at module scope, keep plain `app.listen(port)`, then build with `Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./app.ts'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun', external: ['@sentry/*'], sourcemap: 'external', plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` from `@sentry/bun/plugin` and run `bun dist/app.js`. The `external: ['@sentry/*']` entry is what lets the process-wide client from the unbundled `instrument.ts` and the injected channels inside the bundle agree on one client. It is specific to this app shape and must not be generalized to every Bun framework: the same flag is fatal for a Hono app (DOC-F1).

Works today:

- Unhandled route errors, one event, no `setupExpressErrorHandler` call needed
- Route names `GET /users/:id` with source `route`, plus middleware and handler child spans
- Per-request isolation across concurrent requests
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation
- Outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers
- `mysql` database spans
- `Sentry.logger` log envelopes

Known limits:

- Without the bundle, running `bun app.ts` or `bun --preload ./instrument.ts app.ts` gives URL-sourced transaction names, no middleware, handler or database spans, and no automatic error capture. The `node:http` server span and the `http.client` span for outgoing `fetch` still arrive, and so do logs, which is what makes the gap easy to miss.
- The SDK emits no warning about the missing instrumentation unless `debug: true` is set.

What to change:

- New page `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/frameworks/express.mdx`: the `@sentry/bun` and `mysql` install, the `instrument.ts` + first-import placement, the `build.ts` recipe with its `external` entry and the warning not to reuse that entry for other frameworks, the `bun dist/app.js` run command, and the capability list above.
- Keep `Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler(app)` documented on that page for the unbundled quick start: it is the only thing that captures errors there, with mechanism `auto.middleware.express` rather than `auto.http.express`, and it is harmless in the bundled build.
- State on that page that a missing instrumentation is silent without `debug: true`.

heading: No page documents Fastify on Bun
title: Add a Fastify on Bun page and split Bun db instrumentation by driver
body:
Nothing documents Fastify on Bun: `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/fastify/index.mdx:4-5` is `sdk: sentry.javascript.node` with `fallbackGuide: javascript.node` and Node-only includes at `fastify/index.mdx:12-14`, while `guides/bun/index.mdx:100` shows only `bun --preload ./instrument.js app.js` and `guides/bun/index.mdx:90-94` carries the "Bundled Code Limitation" alert. The Bun claim already exists in the docs elsewhere — `common/configuration/integrations/fastify.mdx` says "This integration only works in the Node.js and Bun runtimes" — only the guide is missing.

Verified on Fastify 5.7.1 with `@sentry/bun` 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on Bun 1.4.0 and re-run on 1.4.2: install `@sentry/bun` plus `mysql2`, put `Sentry.init` in `instrument.mjs`, import it as the first line of `app.mjs` or pass `bun --preload ./instrument.mjs app.mjs`, and run the app directly. No `Bun.build` step and no `sentryBunPlugin()` are needed for Fastify itself. For drivers that need code injection, build with `Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./app.mjs'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun', external: ['@sentry/*'], sourcemap: 'external', plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` from `@sentry/bun/plugin` and run `bun dist/app.mjs`; the follow-up run used `external: ['@sentry/bun', 'mysql']` instead, which is equally safe because the plugin removes the packages it instruments from the `external` list again. `sentryBunPlugin()` is build-only: `Bun.plugin(sentryBunPlugin())` in a `--preload` file crashes the app at import, so the bundle is the only route for injected drivers.

Works today:

- Unhandled route-handler errors, attached to the request transaction
- Route names `GET /users/:id` with source `route`, plus two `handler` child spans per request (`handler GET /users/:id` and `handler fastify - route-handler`); the source is directly assertable under `traceLifecycle: 'static'`
- Per-request isolation across concurrent requests
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation
- Outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers; the client-span name differs by lifecycle
- `mysql2` 3.20.0+ database spans with no build step, covering `execute()`, the promise wrapper and pool connections. Verified at mysql2 3.24.3 on Fastify 5.12.3 in the follow-up run; the original cell, which used only `mysql`@2, recorded database spans as partial. Unlike injected drivers, mysql2 does not need a module-scope connection: a connection created inside the request still gets spans, because the subscription happens at `Sentry.init()` time.
- `Sentry.logger` log envelopes

Known limits:

- Drivers Sentry instruments by code injection, `mysql`@2 among them, produce no span under a plain run; they need the bundle above, with the connection created at module scope.
- The missing database span is silent: the query succeeds and returns rows, and the SDK says nothing unless `debug: true` is set, so the app looks fully instrumented while it has no database visibility.
- Fastify still answers its own 500 body while the error is reported.

What to change:

- New page `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/frameworks/fastify.mdx` with the `@sentry/bun` and `mysql2` install, `instrument.mjs`, run command and the capability list.
- Rewrite `guides/bun/index.mdx:90-94` into a "Database instrumentation on Bun" section that splits behaviour by driver rather than stating one rule, and says the failure is silent without `debug: true`.

heading: No page documents Koa on Bun
title: Add a Koa on Bun page covering the sentryBunPlugin build
body:
No page joins Koa and Bun. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/koa/index.mdx:4-5` declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.node` with `fallbackGuide: javascript.node` and includes `getting-started-node` (`koa/index.mdx:12`), whose run command is `node --import ./instrument.mjs app.mjs` (`platform-includes/getting-started-node/javascript.mdx:95`). The Bun guide stops at `bun --preload ./instrument.js app.js` (`guides/bun/index.mdx:100`) and its "Bundled Code Limitation" alert at `guides/bun/index.mdx:90-94` steers Bun users away from the only setup that works here.

Verified on Koa 2.16.4 with `@koa/router` 12.0.2 and `@sentry/bun` 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on Bun 1.4.0 and re-run on 1.4.2, driver `mysql`@2.18.1, `tracesSampleRate: 1.0`: install `@sentry/bun` instead of `@sentry/node`, put `Sentry.init` in `instrument.ts` imported as the first line of `app.ts`, create the database connection at module scope, then build with `Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./app.ts'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun', external: ['@sentry/*'], sourcemap: 'external', plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` from `@sentry/bun/plugin` and run `bun dist/app.js`. The capabilities below were exercised under `traceLifecycle: 'static'`; `stream` is the default on this line and changes span names (`db SELECT users` and `http.client GET 127.0.0.1` where static gives `db SELECT id, name FROM users` and `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:.../downstream`).

Works today:

- Unhandled handler errors. No `Sentry.setupKoaErrorHandler(app)` call is needed, but that is a v11-wide change rather than a Bun finding: on v11 Express, Fastify, Koa and Hapi errors are captured by their integrations (`common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:713-721`), while `platform-includes/getting-started-use/javascript.koa.mdx:11,28` still presents the call as required.
- Route names `GET /users/:id` with source `route`, plus a `router` child span
- Per-request isolation across concurrent requests
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation
- Outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers
- `mysql`@2 database spans nested under the router span, with the connection created at module scope
- `Sentry.logger` log envelopes, in the bundled and unbundled runs alike

Known limits:

- Without the plugin build, Koa is uninstrumented on Bun: URL-sourced transaction names, no router or database spans, and handler errors are never captured.
- The failure is silent. The SDK emits no warning unless `debug: true` is set, so a Bun and Koa user following the Bun guide gets transactions and logs and believes the setup works while every route error is dropped.

What to change:

- New page `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/frameworks/koa.mdx`: the `@sentry/bun` install, `instrument.ts` placement, the `build.ts` recipe, `bun run build.ts && bun dist/app.js`, and the capability list.
- `guides/bun/index.mdx:90-94`: rewrite the "Bundled Code Limitation" alert. This cell is one of four that contradict it, and the new Koa page is unreachable advice while it stands.
- `platform-includes/getting-started-use/javascript.koa.mdx:11,28`: drop the `Sentry.setupKoaErrorHandler(app)` instruction, which the v10-to-v11 migration guide already supersedes.

heading: No page documents Hapi on Bun
title: Add a Hapi on Bun page covering the sentryBunPlugin build
body:
Grepping `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hapi/` for "bun" returns nothing. That guide is `sdk: sentry.javascript.node` with `fallbackGuide: javascript.node` (`hapi/index.mdx:4-5`) and renders `getting-started-node` (`hapi/index.mdx:12`), while `platform-includes/getting-started-use/javascript.hapi.mdx:17,42` still instruct `await Sentry.setupHapiErrorHandler(server)` in both the CJS and the ESM tab. The Bun guide's alert at `guides/bun/index.mdx:90-94` is the only statement about bundling, and it is backwards for this combination.

Verified on `@hapi/hapi` 21.3.10 with `@sentry/bun` 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on Bun 1.4.0 and re-run on 1.4.2, driver `mysql`@2.18.1, `tracesSampleRate: 1.0`: install `@sentry/bun`, put `Sentry.init` in `instrument.ts` imported as the first line of `app.ts`, create the database connection at module scope and call `db.connect()`, `await server.start()`, then build with `Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./app.ts'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun', external: ['@sentry/*'], sourcemap: 'external', plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` from `@sentry/bun/plugin` and run `bun dist/app.js`.

Works today:

- Unhandled route-handler errors. No `setupHapiErrorHandler` call is needed in the bundled build, because the handler registers itself from the orchestrion `@hapi/hapi` start and initialize channels; the export is deprecated on develop. This is a v11-wide change rather than a Bun finding: `common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:713-721` already states that Express, Fastify, Koa and Hapi errors are captured by their integrations.
- Route names `GET /users/{id}` with source `route`, plus a `router` child span; the child span is named `router /users/{id}` under the `stream` default and `router GET /users/{id}` under `traceLifecycle: 'static'`
- Per-request isolation across concurrent requests
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation
- Outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers
- `mysql`@2 database spans nested under the router span
- `Sentry.logger` log envelopes, in the bundled and unbundled runs alike

Known limits:

- Without the plugin build there is no Hapi instrumentation: URL-sourced names and no router or database spans. Handler errors are captured only if you also call `await Sentry.setupHapiErrorHandler(server)`; in the plugin build the handler registers itself and the extra call is idempotent, producing exactly one event.
- Hapi answers its own 500 body unchanged in every variant.

What to change:

- New page `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/frameworks/hapi.mdx`: install, `instrument.ts` placement, the `build.ts` recipe, `bun run build.ts && bun dist/app.js`, and the capability list.
- Note on that page that the error handler registers itself from the `@hapi/hapi` start and initialize channels in the bundled build, that the `setupHapiErrorHandler` export is deprecated on develop, and that an extra call is idempotent — while `platform-includes/getting-started-use/javascript.hapi.mdx:17,42` still instructs it.
- `guides/bun/index.mdx:90-94`: rewrite the "Bundled Code Limitation" alert, as DOC-F1 and DOC-F4 also ask. This is the second cell that contradicts it.

heading: No page documents Oak on Bun
title: Add an Oak on Bun page covering the Bun.serve routes map
body:
Oak appears nowhere in the docs, on any runtime. The Bun guide, `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx:1-212`, names no framework and never mentions `Bun.serve` or a routes map, and `docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/integrations/bunserver.mdx:18` is the only description of the `Bun.serve` instrumentation but says nothing about how server spans are named. `Bun.serve` itself appears in the docs only on that integration page.

Verified on Oak 17.2.0 with `@sentry/bun` 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on Bun 1.4.0. Oak is JSR-only, so installation needs an `.npmrc` with `@jsr:registry=https://npm.jsr.io` and `npm install "@oak/oak@npm:@jsr/oak__oak@17.2.0"`, followed by `npm install @sentry/bun mysql2`; `bun add @oak/oak` fails outright and `bun add` could not resolve the SDK packages' transitive `@sentry/*` dependencies, so the npm route is required. Put `Sentry.init` in `instrument.ts` imported first, create the `mysql2` connection at module scope, mount the app through `Bun.serve`, and run `bun app.ts` — no bundle and no `sentryBunPlugin()` were needed for any capability here. For route names, build the routes map from the Oak router at startup and keep `fetch` as the fallback: `const handler = req => app.fetch(req); const routes = {}; for (const r of router) routes[r.path] = handler; Bun.serve({ port, routes, fetch: handler })`. That map shape comes from the follow-up run; the cell app named spans with a router-level middleware instead.

Works today:

- Unhandled handler errors, with mechanism `auto.http.bun.serve`; with an Oak error middleware in place the mechanism becomes `oak`, and a user-registered Oak `error` listener stops the re-throw, after which the app has to capture the error itself
- Route names `GET /users/:id` with source `route` and `url.template` once the routes map is passed, in both lifecycles and on the error path. The recorded verdict for route names is partial: see the naming limit below
- Per-request isolation across concurrent requests
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation
- Outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers
- `mysql2` database spans with no build step, because mysql2 publishes its own `node:diagnostics_channel` events. This is the generalizable half of the Bun story: "no library spans without a bundle" is not a universal rule, but a driver without native channels still needs the `sentryBunPlugin` bundle
- `Sentry.logger` log envelopes correlated to the request trace

Known limits:

- Mounted with `fetch` only, server spans take the raw pathname with source `url` under `traceLifecycle: 'static'` (`GET /users/7`, high cardinality) and collapse to a bare `GET` under the `stream` default.
- Even with the routes map, routes using regex constraints, optional params or `(.*)` are derived into the map and still fall back to source `url` (`/api/opt` from `/api/opt/:a?`, `/api/star/a/b` from `/api/star/(.*)`), while a path that Oak answers with a 404 can still be labelled `GET /api/num/:id(\d+)` with source `route`.
- Mounted with `app.listen()` the SDK still emits method-only server spans, but errors are never captured, the database span is not emitted at all, the outgoing-`fetch` span detaches onto the process trace as its own root, logs carry a stale process trace id, and request isolation leaks across concurrent requests (all three concurrent events carried one tag and one trace id).
- Neither naming approach works under `app.listen()`; bundling with `@sentry/bun/plugin` does not change route naming either, and neither does init placement or lifecycle.
- Browser-side capture was not exercised.

What to change:

- New page `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/frameworks/oak.mdx` with the JSR install, the `Bun.serve` mount and routes map, the `bun app.ts` run command, and the capability list.
- Document the second naming option beside the map: a router-level `router.use` middleware calling `Sentry.updateSpanName` and setting the `sentry.segment.name.source` attribute to `route`, which also names the error path. `updateSpanName` alone leaves the source as `custom`. The routes map is preferable because it also sets `url.template` and runs once at startup.
- `common/configuration/integrations/bunserver.mdx`: add that server span names come from the `Bun.serve` routes map.

heading: No page documents Fresh on Bun
title: Add a Fresh on Bun page for the built server output
body:
Fresh has no guide: there is no `fresh` entry under `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/` and no page in `docs/` or `platform-includes/` mentions the Fresh framework. The Bun guide (`guides/bun/index.mdx:1-212`) documents only the `--preload` flow and its alert at `guides/bun/index.mdx:90-94` gives no guidance for a Vite-built SSR bundle, `common/configuration/integrations/bunserver.mdx:18` claims errors are captured automatically, and `common/enriching-events/transaction-name/index.mdx:90-103` documents `Sentry.updateSpanName` (at `:100`) but never the name source. `sentry.segment.name.source` appears in the docs only in the v10-to-v11 migration guide, at `:594`.

Verified on Fresh 2 (`@fresh/core` 2.3.3) built with `deno task build` and served on Bun 1.4.0: keep `@sentry/bun` and the database driver out of the SSR bundle with `ssr.external: ['@sentry/bun', 'mysql2', 'mysql2/promise']` and `build.rollupOptions.external: [/^@sentry\//, /^mysql2/]` in `vite.config.ts`, and install those packages one directory above the Fresh app, because the app directory's `node_modules` is Deno-managed (`nodeModulesDir: "manual"`). Then add an `entry.ts` next to the build output and start it with `bun entry.ts`: `import './instrument.ts'; import server from './app/_fresh/server.js'; Bun.serve({ port, fetch: req => server.fetch(req) });`. That mount is what makes the SDK see requests at all. Create the `mysql2` pool at module scope in the instrument module.

Works today:

- Per-request isolation across concurrent requests
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation
- Outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers
- `mysql2` database spans with no build plugin
- `Sentry.logger` log envelopes
- Route names `GET /users/:id` with source `route`, once a middleware registered before `app.fsRoutes()` renames the root span from `ctx.route` and sets the `sentry.segment.name.source` attribute to `route`. `updateSpanName` alone leaves the source as `custom`, and `setAttribute('sentry.source', 'route')` is the v10 key and is ignored on v11

Known limits:

- Unhandled route and middleware errors are not captured automatically, because Fresh renders its own 500 before anything reaches `Bun.serve`. The request span is still sent with status `internal_error`, so the reader sees a failing transaction and no event. Report the error from one of three equivalent hooks: `Sentry.captureException(ctx.error, { mechanism: { type: 'fresh._error', handled: false } })` in `routes/_error.tsx`; `app.onError('*', ...)` in `main.ts`, which needs no try/catch and re-throw; or a middleware registered before every other `app.use`. Do not rely on `captureConsoleIntegration`: it captures only while Fresh's built-in error page is in use and stops entirely once `_error.tsx` or `onError` exists.
- The plugin build is not an alternative here. Fresh compiles the whole framework into `server-entry.js` and its `App` hard-codes the error hook to a no-op, so a `Bun.build` with `sentryBunPlugin()` does not change this, unlike the Bun framework pages that present that build as the fix.
- Fresh's own OpenTelemetry spans never reach Sentry: every transaction arrived with `spans: []` apart from the ones the SDK created.
- Browser-side capture was not exercised, and `/assets/*` static-file serving, which still calls `Deno.stat` and `Deno.open`, was not exercised under Bun.

What to change:

- New page `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/fresh/index.mdx` with the build and externals config, the `entry.ts` mount and `bun entry.ts`, the node_modules placement rule, the error hook, the naming middleware and the capability list. Which `fallbackGuide` it takes is a scoping decision this run does not settle, since Fresh was also probed on Deno and on Cloudflare.
- `common/configuration/integrations/bunserver.mdx:18`: qualify the automatic error capture claim.
- `common/enriching-events/transaction-name/index.mdx:90-103`: document that `sentry.segment.name.source` is the v11 attribute for the name source and that the v10 `sentry.source` key is ignored.

heading: No page documents NestJS on Bun
title: Add a NestJS on Bun page covering the Bun.build plugin step
body:
No page mentions NestJS on Bun. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nestjs/index.mdx:4-5` sets `sdk: sentry.javascript.nestjs` with `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`, the prerequisites include at `nestjs/index.mdx:14` resolves to the Node prerequisites, the init comes from the `getting-started-config` include at `nestjs/index.mdx:57` and the `{filename: main.ts}` "Import this first!" snippet sits at `nestjs/index.mdx:75`; `platform-includes/getting-started-install/javascript.nestjs.mdx:3-15` has no Bun tab. The Bun guide's only bundling statement is the alert at `guides/bun/index.mdx:90-94`.

Verified on NestJS 11 (`@nestjs/core` + `@nestjs/platform-express` ^11.2.3) with `@sentry/nestjs` and `@sentry/bun` 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on Bun 1.4.0, driver `mysql` ^2.18.1: a `tsconfig.json` with `experimentalDecorators` and `emitDecoratorMetadata`, `Sentry.init` from `@sentry/bun` in `src/instrument.ts` imported as the first line of `src/main.ts` with `import 'reflect-metadata';` as the second, `SentryModule.forRoot()` plus the `SentryGlobalFilter` `APP_FILTER` provider in `src/app.module.ts`, then `Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./src/main.ts'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun', sourcemap: 'external', external: [...], plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` from `@sentry/bun/plugin`, run as `bun run build.ts && bun dist/main.js`. The `external` list must carry Nest's lazily required optional peers (`@nestjs/microservices`, `@nestjs/microservices/microservices-module`, `@nestjs/websockets`, `@nestjs/websockets/socket-module`, `@nestjs/platform-express/multer`, `class-validator`, `class-transformer`, `cache-manager`) or the build fails to resolve them; `@sentry/bun` and `mysql` may also be listed, because the plugin removes the packages it instruments from that list again.

Works today:

- Unhandled controller errors, via the mandatory `SentryGlobalFilter`
- Per-request isolation across concurrent requests
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation
- Outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers
- `mysql` database spans in the bundled build
- `Sentry.logger` log envelopes

Known limits:

- Route names and the Express middleware and handler child spans exist only in the bundled build. Running `bun src/main.ts` gives URL-sourced names under `traceLifecycle: 'static'` (`GET /users/42`, source `url`) and, under the `stream` default, a span named just `http.server GET` with no path at all, so every route collapses into one name. Child spans are absent either way.
- Initializing from `@sentry/nestjs` instead of `@sentry/bun` costs the server span entirely: unbundled, no server span of any kind is emitted and events lose their transaction name.
- Without the `SentryGlobalFilter` provider, controller errors are swallowed and no event is sent.
- There is no runtime hook that substitutes for the bundle. `Bun.plugin(sentryBunPlugin())` at runtime breaks `@nestjs/common`'s CommonJS named exports and the app does not boot (`SyntaxError: Export named 'Injectable' not found`), and `@sentry/server-runtime-injection/register` is a no-op on Bun because `node:module.registerHooks` is undefined there.
- The unbundled failure is silent: there is no warning at all unless `debug: true` is set.
- There are no Nest-specific spans in either lifecycle, and `SentryModule.forRoot()` contributed no visible spans on Bun; the piece from `@sentry/nestjs` that demonstrably mattered is `SentryGlobalFilter`.
- Browser-side capture was not exercised.

What to change:

- New page `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/frameworks/nestjs.mdx` with the tsconfig requirement, the `@sentry/bun` init and the `reflect-metadata` import order, the module wiring, the full build recipe with its `external` list, the `bun run build.ts && bun dist/main.js` commands, and the capability list.
- State on that page that the unbundled path can be given route names from app code with a global Nest interceptor that reads `req.route.path` and, on the root span, calls `updateName`, sets `http.route` and sets `sentry.segment.name.source` to `route` (the v10 `sentry.source` key does not work) — and that this restores the name only, not the child spans.
- `guides/bun/index.mdx:90-94`: replace the "Bundled Code Limitation" alert rather than amending it. For NestJS the bundle is the only path to library instrumentation.
- `platform-includes/getting-started-install/javascript.nestjs.mdx:3-15`: add a Bun tab.

heading: No page documents Next.js on Bun
title: Add a Next.js on Bun page for bun --bun, the fetch integration and the channel pin
body:
No page describes Next.js on Bun. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nextjs/index.mdx:4` is `sdk: sentry.javascript.nextjs`, the runtime list at `nextjs/index.mdx:51-53` names only Client, Server and Edge, and the documented `register()` block at `nextjs/index.mdx:122-134` branches only on `NEXT_RUNTIME === "nodejs"` (`:126`) and `"edge"` (`:129`), with `export const onRequestError = Sentry.captureRequestError;` at `:134`. The Bun guide never mentions Next.js. One include already assumes the combination without saying how: `platform-includes/logs/usage/javascript.nextjs.mdx:7` implies Bun is a supported Next.js server runtime.

Verified on Next.js 15.5.4 (app router) with `@sentry/nextjs` 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on Bun 1.4.0 and re-run on 1.4.2: `withSentryConfig` imported from the `@sentry/nextjs/config` subpath in `next.config.mjs`, the standard `instrumentation.ts` with the `nodejs` branch and `captureRequestError` re-exported as `onRequestError`, then `bun --bun ./node_modules/.bin/next build` and `bun --bun ./node_modules/.bin/next start -p <port>`. Pin `typescript` to 5.x or `next build` dies, and do not pass `sendDefaultPii`, which no longer exists on this line and is a TypeScript build error. Install `@sentry/bun` alongside `@sentry/nextjs` and add its `fetchIntegration()` to `integrations` in `sentry.server.config.ts`. Database and cache spans need a second addition in the same file, a workaround for a Bun bug: Bun garbage-collects the `node:diagnostics_channel` objects that only Sentry's subscriber references, so every subscription made by `Sentry.init()` is gone a tick later. Keep a strong reference to them right after the init call:

`import * as dc from 'node:diagnostics_channel'; globalThis.__sentryKeptChannels = ['mysql2:query', 'mysql2:execute', 'mysql2:connect', 'mysql2:pool:connect', 'ioredis:command', 'ioredis:connect'].map(name => dc.tracingChannel(name));`

Works today:

- Unhandled route-handler errors
- Route names `GET /api/users/[id]` with source `route`
- Per-request isolation across concurrent requests
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation
- Outgoing `fetch` spans and propagation headers, with `fetchIntegration()` added
- Database and cache spans for drivers that publish native diagnostics channels — mysql2 3.20.0 or later, ioredis 5.11.0 or later, node-redis 5.12.0 or later — once the channels are pinned as above, under both lifecycles
- `Sentry.logger` log envelopes

Known limits:

- Drivers below the native-channel cutoff stay unreachable on Next.js, because they need build-time injection and only `ioredis` is un-externalized for it.
- There is no Sentry-specific Bun build step and none is possible: Next.js is built by webpack or turbopack, so the `sentryBunPlugin()` path other Bun framework pages rely on cannot be used here, and `@sentry/nextjs/build/import-hook.mjs` no-ops under Bun. The `[Sentry] Runtime hook not registered` line that reports this is only visible with `debug: true`.
- `contexts.runtime` reports `{ name: 'node' }` on every event even though `process.versions.bun` is set, so Bun events cannot be told apart from Node ones in Sentry.
- Edge-runtime routes, middleware, server actions and browser-side capture were not exercised.

What to change:

- New page `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/frameworks/nextjs.mdx` with the install, the `fetchIntegration()` from `@sentry/bun`, the channel pin, the `typescript` 5.x requirement, the `bun --bun` build and start commands, and which `instrumentation.ts` branch runs under `bun --bun`.
- `guides/nextjs/index.mdx:151`: `withSentryConfig` now comes from `@sentry/nextjs/config`. That is a v11-wide change documented in the v10-to-v11 guide at `:1022`, not a Bun step, and the Next.js guide still shows the old import.
- Add a troubleshooting note under `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nextjs/` for a project root or ancestor directory named `app`; it applies to Node too.

heading: No page documents SvelteKit on Bun
title: Add a SvelteKit on Bun page for the adapter-node output
body:
The SvelteKit guide states that Bun is unsupported: `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/sveltekit/index.mdx:5-9` categorises it as `server-node`, and the adapter box at `platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.sveltekit.mdx:36-48` heads its list "**Fully supported Node.js runtimes**" (`:39`), lists `adapter-node` at `:42`, and then says at `:45-46` "Currently not supported - Non-Node.js server runtimes ... are not yet supported".

Verified on SvelteKit 2.70.3 with `@sveltejs/adapter-node` and `@sentry/sveltekit` 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on Bun 1.4.0 and re-run on 1.4.2: `sentrySvelteKit()` first in the Vite plugin list, imported from `@sentry/sveltekit/vite` — the bare `@sentry/sveltekit` import fails hard with "does not provide an export named sentrySvelteKit". The `sveltekit()` plugin needs `experimental: { instrumentation: { server: true }, tracing: { server: true } }`; without those options no transaction or span envelope is emitted at all, on Node as well as Bun, while errors still arrive. In `src/hooks.server.ts` export both `handleErrorWithSentry` and `export const handle = Sentry.sentryHandle();`, the latter being what renames and re-attributes the root span. Put `Sentry.init` in `src/instrumentation.server.ts`, run `vite build`, then `bun build/index.js`. Install `@sentry/bun` alongside `@sentry/sveltekit` and pass its `fetchIntegration()` into `Sentry.init`, gated with `typeof globalThis.Bun !== 'undefined'` so Node builds do not get a duplicate span. Database spans need one more line in the same file, a workaround for a Bun bug: `import 'mysql2/promise';` next to the `Sentry.init` call. Bun drops a `node:diagnostics_channel` subscription once the channel object becomes unreachable, so a driver that first loads after `Sentry.init()` publishes to fresh, unsubscribed channels; importing it in the same file keeps the channels reachable.

Works today:

- Unhandled server-route errors with source context lines
- Route names `GET /api/users/[id]` with source `route` and `http.route`
- Per-request isolation across concurrent requests
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation, plus the SSR meta tags for the browser
- Outgoing `fetch` spans and propagation headers, with `fetchIntegration()` added
- `mysql2` database spans, with the driver imported in `src/instrumentation.server.ts`
- `Sentry.logger` log envelopes

Known limits:

- A route that answers 500 still reports `status: "ok"` on its `http.server` span once kit tracing is on.
- `contexts.runtime.name` is `node` on Bun, so Bun events cannot be told apart from Node ones in Sentry.
- SvelteKit 2.70 has no `svelte.config.js`; the kit config, including the adapter swap, lives inside the `sveltekit()` Vite plugin.
- Browser-side capture was not exercised; this run drove the server through curl only.

What to change:

- New page `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/frameworks/sveltekit.mdx`: the adapter-node build, `bun build/index.js`, the runtime-gated `fetchIntegration()`, the driver import, the config-location note and the capability list.
- `platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.sveltekit.mdx:36-48`: name Bun in the adapter and runtime compatibility box, and correct `:45-46`, which currently rules out non-Node server runtimes outright.
- `platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.sveltekit.mdx:365, :403, :458`: the plugin import path is `@sentry/sveltekit/vite`, not the package root. This is runtime-independent and breaks the documented setup on Node too.
- `platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.sveltekit.mdx:219-225`: the "SvelteKit 3" tab writes `sveltekit({ tracing: { server: true } })` at `:223` where kit 2.70.3 needs the `experimental` wrapper and the `instrumentation` option beside it.

heading: No page documents React Router on Bun
title: Add a React Router on Bun page requiring the instrumentations export
body:
No page joins React Router and Bun. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/react-router/index.mdx:5-9` declares `categories: [javascript, browser, server, server-node]`, the start commands at `react-router/manual-setup.mdx:400-401` are `NODE_OPTIONS='--import ./instrument.server.mjs'` only, and the "Incomplete Auto-instrumentation" alert at `manual-setup.mdx:434-438` warns at `:436` that the direct-import fallback leaves instrumentation incomplete.

Verified on React Router 8 framework mode with a custom Express server and `@sentry/react-router` 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on Bun 1.4.0 and re-run on 1.4.2: rewrite `app/entry.server.tsx` to use `renderToReadableStream` with `Sentry.wrapSentryHandleRequest(handler)` and `export const handleError = Sentry.createSentryHandleError({ logErrors: true })`, because Bun resolves `react-dom/server` to a build that has no `renderToPipeableStream`. Add `export const instrumentations = [Sentry.createSentryServerInstrumentation()];` to the same file: the docs already show it at `manual-setup.mdx:273` as an optional React Router 7.15+ feature, and on Bun it is required, because Bun has no diagnostics-channel injection for `node:http` and this export is the only source of server spans. Install `@sentry/bun` at the same version, deduped to a single `@sentry/core`, and pass `integrations: process.versions.bun ? [fetchIntegration(), bunHttpServerIntegration()] : []` to the `Sentry.init` in the instrumentation file imported as the very first line of `server.js`; the runtime gate matters because the same build under Node with an unconditional `fetchIntegration()` produces two client spans for one fetch. For database spans add `await import("mysql2/promise")` right after `Sentry.init()` as well — that import and `bunHttpServerIntegration()` are jointly necessary, either alone yields zero database spans — or pin the tracing channels instead. `ssr.noExternal: ['mysql2']` is not needed. Start with `bun server.js`.

Works today:

- Unhandled loader errors; the mechanism sharpens from `react-router` to `react_router.loader` once server spans exist
- `http.server` spans named `GET /users/:id` with source `route`, from the `instrumentations` export alone, in both lifecycles
- Per-request isolation, one trace per request
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation, plus request and IP data on events
- Outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers
- `mysql2` database spans
- `Sentry.logger` log envelopes

Known limits:

- Without the `instrumentations` export and `bunHttpServerIntegration()` the server SDK produces only errors and logs on Bun. The `instrumentations` export alone restores route-named `http.server` spans; `bunHttpServerIntegration()` additionally restores per-request isolation, incoming-trace continuation, outgoing-`fetch` spans and database spans.
- With `fetchIntegration()` but without `bunHttpServerIntegration()`, `traceLifecycle: 'static'` sends the propagation headers but delivers no span envelope at all, only a client report.
- `Sentry.createSentryHandleRequest({ renderToPipeableStream, ... })`, the wiring the guide shows, cannot be used on Bun. The customization escape hatch at `manual-setup.mdx:284-330` (`getMetaTagTransformer` plus `wrapSentryHandleRequest`) also builds on `renderToPipeableStream` and needs a Bun variant.
- The debug line "No diagnostics-channel injection detected. Channel-based integrations will not record spans" still fires after the fix and is misleading.
- `contexts.runtime.name` is `node` on Bun.
- Action errors and browser-side capture were not exercised; the error probe is a loader.

What to change:

- New page `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/frameworks/react-router.mdx` with the server-entry rewrite including the `instrumentations` export, the runtime-gated `@sentry/bun` integrations, the startup driver import, the `bun server.js` start command and the capability list.
- `react-router/manual-setup.mdx:400-401`: add the Bun equivalent of the start commands.
- `react-router/manual-setup.mdx:273`: say that the `instrumentations` export is required rather than optional on Bun.

heading: No page documents TanStack Start on Bun
title: Document TanStack Start on Bun: verified setup and its limits
body:
None of the 11 files under `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/tanstackstart-react/` contains the string "bun". `tanstackstart-react/index.mdx:5-9` declares `categories: [javascript, server, server-node, browser]`, the guide is flagged Beta at `manual-setup/index.mdx:17`, the single documented start command is `node --import ./.output/server/instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs` (`manual-setup/index.mdx:358`), and the only non-Node runtime named anywhere is Cloudflare, as an exclusion (`manual-setup/index.mdx:377`).

Verified on TanStack Start (React) 1.168.35 with the Nitro node-server preset and `@sentry/tanstackstart-react` 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on Bun 1.4.0: the documented wiring builds and runs on Bun as it stands — `sentryTanstackStart()` from `@sentry/tanstackstart-react/vite` last in the Vite plugin list (`manual-setup/index.mdx:220-241`), `sentryGlobalRequestMiddleware` and `sentryGlobalFunctionMiddleware` in `createStart()` in `src/start.ts` (`manual-setup/index.mdx:416-438`), and `wrapFetchWithSentry` on the server entry. No `globalThis` shim around `@sentry/tanstackstart-react` is needed; a module-scope database import builds fine. Start with `bun --preload ./.output/server/instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`. Database spans additionally need a workaround for a Bun bug — Bun garbage-collects the `node:diagnostics_channel` objects the SDK subscribed to, so the subscriptions are gone shortly after startup. Pin them in `instrument.server.mjs` after `Sentry.init`: `globalThis.__sentryKeepChannelsAlive = ['orchestrion:mysql:query', 'orchestrion:mysql2:query', 'orchestrion:mysql2:execute'].map(name => diagnosticsChannel.tracingChannel(name));`. Patching `dc.tracingChannel` from the preload does not work, so the channel names have to be listed. Use the `stream` lifecycle for this: under `static` each database span arrives as its own transaction.

Works today:

- Unhandled errors from `server.handlers` routes, with `wrapFetchWithSentry` on the server entry
- `Sentry.logger` log envelopes
- `mysql` database spans, with the channel pin above: the same build gave `["middleware globalRequestMiddleware"]` without it and `["middleware globalRequestMiddleware", "db SELECT", "db SELECT users"]` with it

Known limits:

- Per-request isolation is recorded broken: three concurrent requests plus a sentinel all carried the tags of the last request and one identical trace id. A process-global isolation scope leaks tags, and would leak user data, between requests with no error anywhere.
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` is recorded broken: the headers were ignored and the event kept the process trace id.
- Outgoing `fetch` spans are recorded broken with the wiring above.
- Parameterized route names such as `GET /api/user/$id` were not produced by the recorded runs.
- Browser-side capture was not exercised, and `contexts.runtime` reports `node` under Bun.
- Follow-up runs for those four capabilities were carried out with `bunHttpServerIntegration()` from `@sentry/bun` added to `Sentry.init`, and their results were never recorded, so none of the four is stated here as fixed. Their raw output is suggestive, showing an `http.client` span with populated propagation headers under `GET /api/fetch` and a root span named `GET /api/user/$id` from the Vite plugin's inlined route patterns, but it comes from a different app shape and needs one recorded run before a page can promise it.

What to change:

- `tanstackstart-react/manual-setup/index.mdx`: add a Bun section giving `bun --preload ./instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs` next to the command at `:358`, the channel pin with its `stream`-lifecycle note, and the limits above.
- State on that page that the "No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks" warning Bun prints is a false alarm once the Vite plugin has done the build-time injection, so it should not be read as an error.

heading: No page documents Remix on Bun
title: Add a Remix v2 on Bun page for the Bun.build server bundle
body:
No page joins Remix and Bun, and the current Remix guide documents no server entry, no instrumentation file and no run command for any runtime. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/remix/index.mdx:12-16` carries the Remix 3 alert as the only runtime or version caveat, and `remix/index.mdx:58-97` ("Configure Server-Side Performance Monitoring") covers only `withSentry` in `root.tsx`; the page's headings are Install, Configure Server-Side Performance Monitoring, Tunneling, Data, Verify, Next Steps. `remix/manual-setup.mdx:49` is the plain install and the whole page is 83 lines covering only Install. The server-entry, instrumentation-file and run-command content a Bun page would build on exists today only on the noindex `remix/manual-setup__v8.x.mdx` (`:166-225`, `:285-294`).

Verified on Remix v2 (`@remix-run/*` ^2.17.5, the `@remix-run/dev` Vite plugin with the `@remix-run/express` adapter, express 4, vite 5) and `@sentry/remix` 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on Bun 1.4.0 and re-run on 1.4.2, driver mysql2 3.24.3: `instrument.mjs` imported as the first line of `server.mjs`, `export const handleError = Sentry.sentryHandleError` in `app/entry.server.tsx`, `sentryRemixVitePlugin()` from the `@sentry/remix/vite` subpath in `vite.config.ts` (it moved there in v11; see the migration guide at `:1287-1294`), the `mysql2` pool at module scope, then bundle the server entry with `Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./server.mjs'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun', plugins: [sentryBunPlugin(), keepExternal] })` from `@sentry/bun/plugin` and run `bun dist/server.js`. Express is kept external by a small plugin placed _after_ `sentryBunPlugin()` — `{ name: 'keep-external', setup(b) { b.config.external = [...(b.config.external ?? []), 'express']; } }` — not by an `external` array entry, because the Sentry plugin removes the packages it instruments from that list; the route-names run reached a working state without externalizing express at all, so the two recorded runs differ here. Because the bundle inlines `@remix-run/server-runtime`, Sentry's `createRequestHandler` patch never runs, so hold the adapter handler in a variable and wrap it yourself: `app.all('*', (req, res, next) => Sentry.withIsolationScope(scope => { scope.setSDKProcessingMetadata({ normalizedRequest: { url, method: req.method, headers: req.headers } }); return Sentry.continueTrace({ sentryTrace, baggage }, () => remixHandler(req, res, next)); }))`. The `setSDKProcessingMetadata` call is what puts request data on events.

Works today:

- Unhandled loader errors via the `handleError` hook
- Route names `GET users/:id` with source `route` — no leading slash — plus `function LOADER routes/users.$id` children, identical on the Node control
- Per-request isolation and incoming trace continuation, with the wrapper above
- `mysql2` database spans
- `Sentry.logger` log envelopes

Known limits:

- Plain `bun server.mjs` sends errors and logs only, with no transactions or spans at all, and its events carry no `transaction` field, so errors group without a route. Isolation and incoming-trace continuation do work in that mode, and so do trace headers on outgoing `fetch`; adding `fetchIntegration()` from `@sentry/bun` also gives it an `http.client` span under the `stream` default, while under `static` the parentless client span is dropped. The repo's own e2e app `create-remix-app-express/server.mjs` uses this wiring and would produce zero spans on Bun.
- Outgoing `fetch` spans in the bundled shape did not reproduce on the re-run: the recorder saw `sentryTrace: null, baggage: null` on every attempt, in both modes.
- The bundle is `target: 'bun'` and cannot be run under Node.
- The bundle is emitted without sourcemaps unless you enable them, so events lose context lines. `sourcemap: 'external'` is the expected fix and was not exercised.
- Re-externalizing `@remix-run/*` instead of express restores isolation natively but removes every span, database spans included; bundling and transforming express breaks AsyncLocalStorage propagation across `next()` on Bun.
- Browser-side capture was not exercised.

What to change:

- New page `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/frameworks/remix.mdx` with the build recipe, the `keep-external` plugin, the handler wrapper and the capability list.
- `guides/remix/`: the guide needs the server entry, instrumentation file and run command that exist today only on the noindex v8 page, for every runtime — a Bun page has nothing to build on otherwise.
- `remix/manual-setup.mdx`: cite the plain install at `:49`; `:64` is the profiling variant.

heading: No page documents SolidStart on Bun
title: Add a SolidStart on Bun page with the @sentry/bun integrations
body:
Nothing under `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/` mentions Bun. `solidstart/index.mdx:5-8` gives only `categories: [browser, server]`, `solidstart/index.mdx:277` tells you to add an `--import` flag to `NODE_OPTIONS`, and the two start scripts at `solidstart/index.mdx:297-298` are `start:vinxi` with `NODE_OPTIONS` and `start:node` with `node --import ./.output/server/instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`; `solidstart/install/cli-import.mdx:33,45` repeats them. The whole guide targets SolidStart 1 (`app.config.ts` with `withSentry`, `NODE_OPTIONS` and `vinxi`); `sentrySolidStart` appears in the docs only in the v8-to-v9 migration note about the removed `sentrySolidStartVite` plugin. A SolidStart 2 page is therefore needed for every runtime, not only Bun.

Verified on SolidStart 2 (`@solidjs/start` 2.0.2, Nitro 3) with `@sentry/solidstart` 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on Bun 1.4.0: in `vite.config.ts` use `sentrySolidStart({ sourcemaps: { disable: true } })` from `@sentry/solidstart/vite` alongside `solidStart({ appRoot: './src', middleware: './src/middleware.ts' })` and `nitro({ serverDir: './server' })` — the last is what makes `server/plugins/sentry.ts` load at all. Put `Sentry.init` inside that Nitro plugin, add `sentryBeforeResponseMiddleware()` in `src/middleware.ts`, run `vite build`, then `bun .output/server/index.mjs`. Install `@sentry/nitro` alongside `@sentry/solidstart` and `@sentry/bun`, with `npm install --legacy-peer-deps`: `@sentry/nitro` 10.67.0 pins a nitro range that the 3.0 beta cannot satisfy. Add `bunHttpServerIntegration()` and `fetchIntegration()` from `@sentry/bun` to `integrations`, guarding the fetch one on `typeof Bun !== 'undefined'` so a Node deployment of the same build does not get two spans; the two integrations were probed in separate follow-up runs and never together in one run. Database spans need a workaround for a Bun bug: Bun garbage-collects the SDK's `diagnostics_channel` subscriptions, so pin the channels on `globalThis` after `Sentry.init()` in `server/plugins/sentry.ts` — `globalThis.__sentryPinnedChannels = ['mysql2:query', 'mysql2:execute', 'mysql2:connect', 'mysql2:pool:connect', 'orchestrion:mysql:query'].map(n => dc.tracingChannel(n))` — or use an equivalent `bun --preload pin.mjs` file if the Nitro plugin cannot be touched.

Works today:

- Per-request isolation, one scope and one trace per request
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation
- Outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers
- `mysql2` 3.20.0+ and `mysql` v2 database spans alike, once the tracing channels are pinned. No build step and no driver import order is required; every channel-based integration on Bun is exposed to the same bug, not only databases
- `Sentry.logger` log envelopes
- Errors from server functions wrapped in `withServerActionInstrumentation`, and errors thrown in a file API route once the h3 middleware below is added. The recorded verdict for errors is partial: page-render errors stay dark either way

Known limits:

- Errors thrown while a page component renders on the server are not reported, on Bun and on Node alike. File API route errors are reported only if `src/middleware.ts` wraps `next()` in a `try`/`catch` that calls `Sentry.captureException(error, { mechanism: { handled: false, type: 'solidstart.middleware' } })` and re-throws — `createMiddleware` accepts a raw h3 middleware array on SolidStart 2, so this composes with `sentryBeforeResponseMiddleware()`. The guide's own Verify step at `solidstart/index.mdx:444-453`, a `sentry-test.tsx` route throwing from `GET`, is exactly the case that produces no event without it.
- Server transactions are named from the raw URL (`GET /users/456`, source `url`) rather than the route pattern, on Bun and on Node alike, and under the `stream` default the segment collapses further to a bare `GET`. App code can fix the name: call `getRootSpan(getActiveSpan()).updateName(...)` and set `http.route` and `sentry.segment.name.source`, verified on both runtimes and both lifecycles.
- `bunHttpServerIntegration({ spans: false })` also isolates requests and continues traces but drops the `node:http` server span; the default is the parity choice. The `NITRO_PRESET=bun` plus `bunServerIntegration()` path was tried and rejected.
- `@sentry/bun` adds roughly 2.4 MB to the server bundle.
- `contexts.runtime.name` is `node` under Bun.

What to change:

- New page `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/frameworks/solidstart.mdx` with the `bun .output/server/index.mjs` start command, the full SolidStart 2 Vite config, the two `@sentry/bun` integrations with the runtime guard, the channel pin and the capability list.
- Add the route-naming workaround and the unreported-error notes to `guides/solidstart/index.mdx`, and correct the Verify step at `:444-453`, which currently demonstrates the one case that sends nothing.
- `guides/solidstart/` needs a SolidStart 2 setup for every runtime: the documented `app.config.ts` plus `withSentry` plus `vinxi` shape does not apply, and `sentrySolidStart` is otherwise undocumented.

heading: The page for Hono on Deno misses the wiring or the limits
title: Document the verified Hono on Deno setup and its outgoing fetch limit
body:
The Hono guide already claims Deno support: `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hono/index.mdx:12` lists Deno among the runtimes, `:88-89` gives the Deno peer dependency as `deno add npm:@sentry/deno`, and `:302-324` shows the Deno tab with `import { sentry } from "@sentry/hono/deno"`, `app.use(sentry(app, {...}))` and `Deno.serve(app.fetch)`. The page carries no runtime caveats around `:360`, and `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:1-230` never mentions `node_modules`, `nodeModulesDir`, the `@sentry/deno/import` hook or outgoing `fetch`.

Verified on Hono 4.13.7 with `@sentry/hono/deno` 10.67.0 on Deno 2.9.0: install `@sentry/hono` and `@sentry/deno` into a real on-disk `node_modules` with `npm install`, set `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}` in `deno.json`, put `import "@sentry/deno/import";` as the first line of the entry file when you want database and library spans, then wire the middleware exactly as the current snippet shows and run `deno run --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys main.ts`.

Works today:

- Unhandled route errors, with `transaction: "GET /error"` and mechanism `auto.http.hono.context_error`. Hono turns the throw into its own 500 response and the middleware's `responseHandler` reads `context.error`, so the event still arrives and the server span is marked `internal_error`.
- Parameterized names `GET /users/:id` with source `route`.
- Per-request isolation across concurrent requests.
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation.
- Database spans for `mysql` (requires the import hook line).
- Logs.

Known limits:

- Outgoing `fetch()` is not instrumented on Deno: no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers, so the downstream service starts a new trace. The default integrations of `@sentry/deno` carry `denoHttpIntegration()` for `node:http`/`node:https` and nothing that traces `fetch`; the breadcrumb integration patches `fetch`, so the call is still breadcrumbed while no span is started and no header is injected.
- `node:http`/`node:https` clients are traced normally.
- Without the import hook line, database and library spans are silently missing.

What to change:

- `guides/hono/index.mdx:88-89`: show the `deno.json` and the npm-based install, not `deno add` alone.
- `guides/hono/index.mdx` near `:302-324`: note the optional `@sentry/deno/import` first line and the permission flags.
- `guides/hono/index.mdx` near `:360`: add a Deno-only caveat for outgoing `fetch`, naming `node:http`/`node:https` as the clients that are traced.
- `guides/deno/index.mdx`: add an "Outgoing fetch requests" section stating the same limit.

heading: No page documents Express on Deno
title: Add an Express on Deno page covering the plain setup and the import-hook setup
body:
Nothing covers this combination: `grep -rni express docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/` and `grep -rni deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/express/` both return zero hits. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/express/index.mdx:4-5` declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.node` with `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`, and `:12` is a bare `<PlatformContent includePath="getting-started-node" />`, so the whole guide assumes `@sentry/node` on Node. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:1-230` names no framework.

Verified on Express 5.2.1 and Deno 2.9.0 in two shapes. Both start the same way: `npm install express@5 mysql@2` plus `@sentry/deno` into a real on-disk `node_modules`, and a `deno.json` with `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}`; the app runs with `deno run --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys app.ts`. Shape A is the plain one: an `instrument.ts` that calls `Sentry.init({ dsn, tracesSampleRate: 1.0 })` from `@sentry/deno` and is the first import of the app file. Shape B adds library instrumentation: the same file starts with `import "@sentry/deno/import";`, then imports a six-line JSON load hook, then inits. The load hook is `Module.registerHooks({ load(url, context, nextLoad) { const result = nextLoad(url, context); if (url.endsWith(".json") && result.format !== "json") result.format = "json"; return result; } })` from `node:module`, registered after the Sentry hook; without it Express never imports. No `integrations` entry is needed in either shape, because `expressIntegration()` is already in the Deno SDK's default set.

Works today:

- Both shapes: incoming requests produce `http.server` transactions, and `Sentry.logger` logs arrive.
- Shape B: parameterized names `GET /users/:id` with source `route`, plus a `handler /users/:id` child span.
- Shape B: unhandled route errors as events with mechanism `auto.http.express` and `transaction: "GET /error"`; Express still answers 500.
- Shape B: database spans for a module-scope `mysql@2` connection, as a child of the handler span.
- Shape B: per-request isolation across concurrent requests with distinct trace ids, and incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation. Both were measured on this shape only.
- Shape A error capture, with `setupExpressErrorHandler(app)` imported from `@sentry/server-utils`: route errors arrive with mechanism `auto.middleware.express`.
- Outgoing `fetch()`, with `fetchIntegration()` imported from `@sentry/cloudflare` and passed to `Sentry.init`: `http.client` spans with origin `auto.http.fetch` parented under the handler span, and `sentry-trace`/`baggage` on the wire, in both trace lifecycles. It means installing `@sentry/cloudflare` in a Deno app.

Known limits:

- Shape A names transactions `GET /users/42` with source `url` and produces no handler spans and no database spans.
- Shape A captures nothing for a thrown route error unless `setupExpressErrorHandler` is added: Express's default error handler swallows the throw and the SDK prints no warning, so the 500 is invisible in Sentry.
- `setupExpressErrorHandler` has to come from `@sentry/server-utils`; `@sentry/deno` does not re-export it.
- `import "@sentry/deno/import"` needs the companion JSON load hook because of denoland/deno#36240: with any module load hook registered, `require('*.json')` compiles as JavaScript, and Express dies at import time on `require('./codes.json')` inside `statuses`.
- Outgoing `fetch()` is not instrumented by default in either shape: the Deno SDK's default integrations trace only `node:http`/`node:https`, so without the integration above a handler's `fetch()` gets no span and sends no trace headers.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/frameworks/express.mdx` with the install, `deno.json`, both init shapes including the JSON load hook, the run command and the capability split above.
- Add a shared "Outgoing fetch requests" note to `guides/deno/index.mdx`.

heading: No page documents Fastify on Deno
title: Add a Fastify on Deno page: full instrumentation without the import hook
body:
There is no page for Fastify on Deno. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/fastify/index.mdx:4` declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.node`, `:5` `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`, and `:12-14` is only `<PlatformContent includePath="getting-started-primer" />` plus `getting-started-node`; `grep -rni deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/fastify/` returns zero hits. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:1-230` never mentions Fastify, any framework, `nodeModulesDir`, or the `@sentry/deno/import` hook.

Verified on Fastify 5.12.3 and Deno 2.9.0 with `@sentry/deno` 10.67.0: a `package.json` with `{"type":"module"}`, `npm install @sentry/deno fastify mysql2` into a real `node_modules`, `deno.json` with `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}` and an `imports` map, an `instrument.ts` that only calls `Sentry.init({ dsn, tracesSampleRate: 1.0 })`, imported as the very first line of `main.ts`, and `deno run --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys main.ts`. No build step is needed and the Fastify integration is on by default; `setupFastifyErrorHandler(app)`, which the Fastify guide still prescribes, is a deprecated no-op on the develop line and errors are captured without it.

Works today:

- Route errors, mechanism `auto.function.fastify`, with the server span marked `internal_error`.
- `GET /users/:id` with source `route` and `http.route` set, in both trace lifecycles.
- Per-request isolation and incoming trace continuation.
- Database spans for `mysql2` 3.20+, which publishes its own diagnostics channels, with no import hook and no bundler plugin.
- Logs.
- Outgoing `fetch()`, with `integrations: [winterCGFetchIntegration()]` imported from `@sentry/vercel-edge`: the `http.client` span and the `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers appear in both trace lifecycles, with the shipped integration running unmodified on Deno. It is an extra package to install next to `@sentry/deno`.

Known limits:

- Do not add `import "@sentry/deno/import"`: with it the process dies at import with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` from `ajv/dist/core.js:21`, which does `require("./refs/data.json")`, because Deno compiles JSON requires as JavaScript once a module load hook is registered (denoland/deno#36240).
- Outgoing `fetch()` is not instrumented by default: `@sentry/deno`'s default integrations trace only `node:http`/`node:https`, so without the integration above a `fetch()` gets no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers, in either trace lifecycle.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/frameworks/fastify.mdx` with the setup above and an explicit warning against the import hook.
- Put the outgoing `fetch` note, with the `winterCGFetchIntegration()` remedy, in `guides/deno/index.mdx` as a shared runtime section.

heading: No page documents Koa on Deno
title: Add a Koa on Deno page: instrumentation timing decides what you get
body:
No page covers Koa on Deno. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/koa/index.mdx:4` declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.node`, `:5` `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`, and `:12` is only `<PlatformContent includePath="getting-started-node" />`; `grep -rni deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/koa/` returns nothing, and `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:1-230` mentions no framework and no import hook.

Verified on Koa 3.2.1 with `@koa/router` 15.7.0 on Deno 2.9.0: `npm install` the app dependencies and `@sentry/deno` into a real `node_modules`, `deno.json` with `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}` and an `imports` map, an `instrument.ts` calling `Sentry.init()` from `@sentry/deno` that is evaluated before the Koa app module, and `deno run --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys main.ts`. Three shapes were exercised on top of that. (A) Bundle the server with esbuild and `sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild` (`format: 'esm'`, `external: ['@sentry/deno', '@sentry/server-utils']`, plus a `createRequire` banner; both externals and the banner are load-bearing) and run the bundle. (B) Skip the bundler and start with `deno run --import=./preload.ts main.ts`, where `preload.ts` first registers a `node:module` load hook that returns `.json` URLs with `format: "json"` and then imports `"@sentry/deno/import"`. (C) For database spans without either, import the Koa app module first, then register the hook in the entry body with `await import("@sentry/deno/import")`, then `await import("mysql")` and create the client with `mysql.createConnection`.

Works today:

- Automatic route-error capture with mechanism `auto.middleware.koa`, in shapes A and B, with no `app.on('error')` of your own; in shape C, register `app.on('error', err => Sentry.captureException(err))` yourself.
- Parameterized names `GET /users/:id` with source `route`, `http.route` set and koa `router` spans, in shapes A and B, in both trace lifecycles.
- Per-request isolation and incoming trace continuation.
- Database spans for `mysql` in shape C, on the request transaction.
- Logs, carrying the request trace id.

Known limits:

- With no build step and no hook, nothing Koa-specific is instrumented: transactions are `GET /users/42` with source `url`, the streamed server span is `GET` with no `http.route`, there are no koa spans, and a thrown route error is not captured at all.
- `import "@sentry/deno/import"` must not be a static import of the entry file. Deno instantiates the entry's whole static module graph, Koa included, before the first statement runs, so the hook registers after Koa is already in the module cache and never transforms it, and the same import kills the process anyway: Koa's `statuses` dependency does `require('./codes.json')`, and Deno compiles JSON as JavaScript while any module load hook is registered (denoland/deno#36240), so it aborts with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'`.
