The JSON load hook in shape B is what makes the flag form survive.
- Use `mysql.createConnection`, not `mysql.createPool`: pooled queries emit their db span as a root transaction of its own, on a different trace from the request.
- `@sentry/deno` exports no `setupKoaErrorHandler`, so the unbundled fallback is the hand-written `app.on('error')` listener, whose events carry a manual mechanism.
- `debug: true` prints "[instrumentation:koa] subscribing to channels" and "Integration installed: Koa" even when no hook is loaded and nothing is instrumented, so the debug log cannot be used to confirm the setup.
- Outgoing `fetch()` is not instrumented: no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage`, in both trace lifecycles. `node:http`/`node:https` requests are traced and propagated.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/frameworks/koa.mdx` with the setup, the three shapes, the database rule and the limits.

heading: No page documents Hapi on Deno
title: Add a Hapi on Deno page with the three verified wirings
body:
Neither guide covers the pair: `grep -rn -i hapi docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/` and `grep -rn -i deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hapi/` both return nothing. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hapi/index.mdx:4-5` declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.node` with `fallbackGuide: javascript.node` and `:12` is a bare `getting-started-node` include. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:1-230` covers error monitoring and tracing only, and never mentions `node_modules`, `nodeModulesDir` or the import hook.

Verified on `@hapi/hapi` 21.4.10 and Deno 2.9.0: `npm install @hapi/hapi` plus `@sentry/deno` into a real on-disk `node_modules`, `deno.json` with `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}` and an `imports` map, and `Sentry.init()` from `@sentry/deno` before the server is created. `hapiIntegration()` is already in the Deno SDK's default set, so no `integrations` entry is needed. Three shapes were verified. (A) Bundle the app with esbuild and `sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild` (`bundle: true`, `platform: 'node'`, `format: 'esm'`, `external: ['@sentry/deno','@sentry/server-utils']`, `loader: {'.json': 'json'}`, `createRequire` banner) and run `deno run --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys dist/main.js`, which yields error capture, parameterized route names, hapi router spans and database spans with no runtime hook. (B) Keep `deno run main.ts` and call `attachHapiErrorHandler(server)` from `@sentry/server-utils`, which works before or after `server.start()`. (C) Keep `deno run main.ts` and put `import "@sentry/deno/import"` plus a twelve-line JSON load hook (`Module.registerHooks` returning `{ format: 'json', source: readFileSync(...) }` for `.json` URLs) ahead of the app; the two registrations may come in either order, but both must precede the app import.

Works today:

- Route errors, mechanism `auto.function.hapi`, in shapes A and C; in shape B, mechanism from `attachHapiErrorHandler`.
- `GET /users/{id}` with source `route`, in shapes A and C, plus a `router` child span.
- Route names without any build step or hook, through a six-line `server.ext('onPreHandler')` that calls `updateName` on the root span and then sets `Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE` to `route` and `http.route` to `request.route.path`. The attribute must be set after `updateName`, which otherwise leaves the source `custom`.
- Per-request isolation and incoming trace continuation, with or without a build step or hook.
- Database spans for `mysql`, in shapes A and C, and logs in every configuration.

Known limits:

- Running the entry directly with `Sentry.init()` alone loses Hapi errors, because Hapi turns the throw into a Boom 500 and the transaction is recorded with status `internal_error` while no event is sent, and it names transactions `GET /users/42` with source `url` (`http.server GET` under the stream lifecycle).
- `import "@sentry/deno/import"` on its own aborts the app at import: `@hapi/validate` does `require('../package.json')` and Deno compiles JSON as JavaScript while a module load hook is registered (denoland/deno#36240). Registering the hook through `--import` fails the same way; the JSON load hook is the escape.
- `@sentry/deno` does not export `setupHapiErrorHandler`, so the call the Hapi guide prescribes throws on Deno; the shipped equivalent is `attachHapiErrorHandler` from `@sentry/server-utils`.
- Outgoing `fetch()` is not instrumented: no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage`, with and without the hook and in both trace lifecycles. `node:http`/`node:https` requests are traced and propagated.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/frameworks/hapi.mdx` with the three setups side by side and the limits.
- `platform-includes/getting-started-use/javascript.hapi.mdx:17,42`: `await Sentry.setupHapiErrorHandler(server)` does not exist on `@sentry/deno`. Scope that step to the Node SDK, or give the Deno equivalent.

heading: No page documents Oak on Deno
title: Add an Oak on Deno page: mount with Deno.serve(app.fetch)
body:
Oak appears nowhere in the docs: `grep -rin '\boak\b' docs/ platform-includes/` and `grep -rl '@oak/oak\|jsr:@oak' docs/` return nothing. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:1-230` names no framework and never mentions `Deno.serve`, only bare `deno run` at `:100` and `:119`; the Deno guide directory holds just `index.mdx` and two integration pages.

Verified on Oak 17.2.0 (`jsr:@oak/oak`) and Deno 2.9.0: `deno.json` with `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}` and imports for `@oak/oak` and `@sentry/deno`, `@sentry/deno` present in a real `node_modules`, plus `npm install path-to-regexp@6.3.0`, which Oak needs to boot under manual `nodeModulesDir`. Put `import "@sentry/deno/import";` as the first line of the instrument file, then `Sentry.init()`, and mount the app with `Deno.serve(app.fetch)`. Name routes with a middleware registered before `app.use(router.routes())` that reads `ctx.matched?.at(-1)?.path` and, inside `try { await next(); } finally { ... }`, calls `Sentry.updateSpanName(span, `${ctx.request.method} ${route}`)` and sets both `Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE` to `route` and `http.route` to the route. A `router.use((ctx, next) => { ...; return next(); })` registered before the routes is equivalent.

Works today:

- Route errors, mechanism `auto.http.deno`, on the `app.fetch` path.
- Per-request isolation and incoming trace continuation.
- `GET /users/:id` with source `route` and `http.route` set, via the naming middleware, on the success and the error path, in both trace lifecycles, and with prefixed routers (`GET /api/users/:id`).
- Database spans for `mysql` through the import hook, with the driver imported dynamically after init.
- Logs, correlated to the request trace.

Known limits:

- `app.listen()` runs handlers outside the request's async context: no active span, errors are never captured, and tags and trace ids leak between requests. Nothing in user code repairs it, so always mount with `Deno.serve(app.fetch)`.
- Naming code placed after `await next()` instead of in a `finally` block silently skips every request whose handler throws, so those keep the unparameterized name.
- Without the middleware, spans are named by HTTP method only (stream) or by the raw path with source `url` (static); there is no Oak integration in `@sentry/deno`.
- Oak types `app.fetch` as a Cloudflare handler, so `ctx.request.ip` is empty on Deno. The SDK still records the client address, which it takes from the `Deno.serve` connection info.
- Outgoing `fetch()` is not instrumented; `node:http` requests are.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/frameworks/oak.mdx`, leading with the mounting rule.

heading: No page documents Fresh on Deno
title: Add a Fresh 2 on Deno page: what the SDK does and does not instrument
body:
There is no Fresh page at all, and `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:1-230` names no framework; the Deno guide directory holds only `index.mdx` and `configuration/integrations/{breadcrumbs,contextlines}.mdx`, so the Cloudflare-style `guides/*/frameworks/` layout has no Deno counterpart.

Verified on Fresh 2 and Deno 2.9.0: scaffold with `deno run -A jsr:@fresh/init@^2`, set `"nodeModulesDir": "manual"` in `deno.json`, install `@sentry/deno` into that same `node_modules`, keep `import "@sentry/deno/import";` as the first line of `instrument.ts` and `instrument.ts` as the first import of `main.ts`. Fresh catches route errors itself, so add `integrations: [Sentry.captureConsoleIntegration({ levels: ['error'], handled: false })]` to `Sentry.init` to report them; if the app registers its own `app.onError("*")` handler, call `Sentry.captureException` inside it instead. For database spans, use `mysql@2` and list each driver in both `ssr.external` and `environments.ssr.build.rollupOptions.external` in `vite.config.ts`. Both `deno task dev` and the `deno serve _fresh/server.js` build were exercised.

Works today:

- Errors, via `captureConsoleIntegration`, or an explicit capture in the app's error handler, or `setErrorInterceptor` from `jsr:@fresh/core/internal`.
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation.
- Database spans for `mysql@2`, with the driver externalized as above.
- Logs.

Known limits:

- Routes are not named automatically; a middleware that reads `ctx.route` and calls `Sentry.updateSpanName` on the root span is required, otherwise transactions carry the raw path with source `url`.
- Per-request isolation is not reliable on Deno: awaiting a dynamic `import()` inside a request restores that request's store into the root async context, so tags, users, contexts and breadcrumbs set during one request appear on every later request. Mitigate with a first middleware that strips tags, contexts, extra, user, breadcrumbs and attachments off `Sentry.getIsolationScope()`. Do not use `Sentry.withIsolationScope(new Sentry.Scope(), ...)` for this: it cleans events but attributes each request's tags to the next transaction.
- `mysql2` cannot be used: under the import hook Deno compiles its `require('*.json')` as JavaScript (denoland/deno#36240) and the route 500s.
- Outgoing `fetch()` is not instrumented.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/frameworks/fresh.mdx` plus a `frameworks/index.mdx` listing the Deno frameworks.

heading: No page documents NestJS on Deno
title: Add a NestJS on Deno page: the boot workaround decides what you get
body:
No page covers NestJS on Deno. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nestjs/index.mdx:1-9` declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.nestjs`, `fallbackGuide: javascript.node` and category `server-node`, and `grep -rni deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nestjs/` returns zero hits. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:1-230` is a beta-flagged manual-setup page for `@sentry/deno` (Alert at `:12-16`) that names no framework.

Verified on NestJS 10 (`@nestjs/core` with `@nestjs/platform-express`, and re-run on `@nestjs/platform-fastify`) and `@sentry/nestjs` 10.67.0 on Deno 2.9.0: install the Sentry packages in a single `npm install` into a real on-disk `node_modules`, set `deno.json` to `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}` with `experimentalDecorators` and `emitDecoratorMetadata` in `compilerOptions`, keep the standard instrument file that calls `Sentry.init({ dsn, tracesSampleRate: 1.0 })` from `@sentry/nestjs` first, and register `SentryGlobalFilter` as `APP_FILTER` alongside `SentryModule.forRoot()`. `@sentry/deno` is neither used nor needed. One more line is mandatory, or the app does not boot on Deno, and the choice decides how much you get. Either add a six-line `Module.registerHooks({ load(url, context, nextLoad) { const result = nextLoad(url, context); return url.endsWith(".json") ? { ...result, format: "json" } : result; } })` from `node:module` in the instrument file, before the `@sentry/nestjs` import or right after `Sentry.init()` (both orders verified), and leave the SDK's diagnostics-channel injection on. Or turn the injection off with `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false` in `Sentry.init`, the public option for it, which the Next.js-on-Deno run used on the same runtime.

Works today:

- Handler errors, mechanism `auto.http.nestjs.global_filter`, linked to the request transaction.
- With the JSON load hook and injection left on: `GET /users/:id` with source `route` and `http.route` set, plus express middleware, `handler` and `function AppController.getUser` spans, on `@nestjs/platform-express` and on `@nestjs/platform-fastify`, in both trace lifecycles.
- Per-request isolation across concurrent requests, with distinct trace ids.
- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation.
- Database spans for `mysql2`, which ships its own diagnostics channels, with no hook and no bundler plugin.
- Logs.

Known limits:

- With injection off, transaction names are not parameterized: `/users/42` reports `GET /users/42` with source `url`, under span streaming the span is `GET` with no source attribute, and there are no express or nest middleware, handler or function spans.
- With injection on and no JSON load hook, the app does not start: `Sentry.init` registers module hooks on Deno unconditionally, Deno then compiles every `require('*.json')` as JavaScript (denoland/deno#36240), and Nest fails with "No driver (HTTP) has been selected" on platform-express and `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` on platform-fastify.
- With injection off, only drivers that publish their own diagnostics channels are instrumented; anything that needs the injected channels stays dark.
- Without `SentryGlobalFilter` as `APP_FILTER`, Nest swallows the error and only the failed transaction arrives. `SentryModule.forRoot()` registers `APP_INTERCEPTOR` only.
- Outgoing `fetch()` is not instrumented: no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers, because that instrumentation listens on undici's diagnostics channels and Deno's native fetch publishes none. `node:http` requests are traced and propagated.
- On Deno the SDK logs "@sentry/server-runtime-injection was bundled into your application" for an app that is not bundled, so that line is no signal of a misconfiguration.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/frameworks/nestjs.mdx` with the install, `deno.json`, init and filter wiring, both boot options with what each one costs, and a "Known limitations on Deno" section.

heading: No page documents Next.js on Deno
title: Add a Next.js on Deno page and document enableRuntimeChannelInjection
body:
`grep -rniE "deno" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nextjs/` returns zero hits across every subtree, and the reverse grep over `guides/deno/` returns zero for Next.js. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nextjs/index.mdx:4-9` declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.nextjs` with category `server-node`. `grep -rn "enableRuntimeChannelInjection" docs/` returns nothing repo-wide, so the option that makes this combination work is undocumented; `docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/options.mdx:755` is where the neighbouring `traceLifecycle` option lives.

Verified on Next.js 15.5.4 App Router and Deno 2.9.0: `deno.json` with `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}`, build and start with `deno run -A node_modules/next/dist/bin/next build` and `... next start`, the standard root `instrumentation.js` and `sentry.server.config.js`. Two deviations are required: set `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false` in `Sentry.init()`, and add `integrations: [winterCGFetchIntegration()]` from `@sentry/vercel-edge`, which is already installed with `@sentry/nextjs`. Keep the default webpack builder: the build-time instrumentation that carries part of the database story needs it.

Works today:

- Route handler errors, mechanism `auto.function.nextjs.route_handler`.
- `GET /users/[id]` with source `route`, plus nested Next.js spans.
- Per-request isolation and incoming trace continuation.
- Outgoing `http.client` spans with `sentry-trace`/`baggage`, via `winterCGFetchIntegration()`.
- Database spans for drivers with native diagnostics channels (`mysql2` >= 3.11, `ioredis` >= 5.11), plus drivers Sentry bundles and transforms at build time (`ioredis` below 5.11), as long as the app builds with webpack and keeps `buildTimeInstrumentation` on.
- Logs.

Known limits:

- Without `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false`, every request returns 500 with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'`, because Deno cannot `require()` a `.json` file while the module hook is installed (denoland/deno#36240).
- With it set, drivers that depend on that runtime hook produce no spans. `mysql` 2.x and `pg` stay in Sentry's default server-external packages, and only `ioredis` is on the list that gets un-externalized for build-time instrumentation, so there is no config knob that rescues them: forcing `mysql` 2.x to be bundled does produce the span but corrupts the driver, on Node as well as on Deno.
- Passing `--turbopack` on Next 15, or setting `buildTimeInstrumentation: false`, removes the build-time path and with it the `ioredis` spans.
- Error events carry no source context lines.
- `contexts.runtime` reports `{ name: "node" }` on Deno, so a Deno-hosted Next.js app is indistinguishable from a Node one in Sentry.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/frameworks/nextjs.mdx`.
- Document `enableRuntimeChannelInjection` in `common/configuration/options.mdx` near `:755`.

heading: No page documents React Router on Deno
title: Add a React Router on Deno page with the Deno entry.server and node:http server entry
body:
`docs/platforms/javascript/guides/react-router/` contains only `index.mdx`, `manual-setup.mdx` and `profiling/`, and `grep -rni deno` over it returns nothing; the reverse grep over `guides/deno/` also returns nothing. The guide is Node-shaped throughout: `index.mdx:9` categorises it `server-node`, `manual-setup.mdx:400-401` gives the only start commands and both are Node ones, and the "Limited Node support for OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation" Expandable at `:186-197` is the closest the guide comes to a runtime statement.

Verified on React Router 7.18.3 in framework mode with `@sentry/react-router` 10.67.0 on Deno 2.9.0: `npm install` the app packages and the Sentry packages into a real `node_modules`, `deno.json` with `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}`. `app/entry.server.tsx` must use the web-stream renderer, `renderToReadableStream` from `react-dom/server`, because Deno resolves `react-dom/server` through the `deno` export condition and there is no `renderToPipeableStream`; wrap it with `wrapSentryHandleRequest` and export `handleError = createSentryHandleError({ logErrors: true })`. The server entry is a hand-written `node:http` adapter whose first line is `import './instrument.server.mjs';` and which serves `createRequestHandler(build, 'production')` over `http.createServer`; build with `npx react-router build` and start it with `PORT=<port> deno run --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys server.mjs`. Add the Vite plugin as `import { sentryReactRouter } from '@sentry/react-router/vite'`. Use `mysql@2`, not `mysql2`.

Works today:

- Loader errors, mechanism `react-router`, surfaced by the `handleError` export.
- `GET /users/:id` with op `http.server` and source `route`.
- Per-request isolation and incoming trace continuation.
- Database spans for `mysql@2` with no extra instrumentation path: the SDK subscribes to the driver's diagnostics channel eagerly on Deno. The connection must be created inside the loader.
- Outgoing `fetch()`, with `fetchIntegration` imported from `@sentry/cloudflare` and registered in `instrument.server.mjs` behind a Deno-only guard, so a Node build does not emit a duplicate `http.client` span.
- Logs.

Known limits:

- The two start paths the guide prescribes do not work on Deno: `react-router-serve` goes through the `renderToPipeableStream` path Deno cannot load, and `NODE_OPTIONS='--import ./instrument.server.mjs'` is ignored by Deno. A bare `Deno.serve` handler produces neither the `http.server` span nor the isolation scope, so the `node:http` server entry above is the load-bearing piece.
- `mysql2` cannot be loaded once Sentry is initialized: its `require('../package.json')` throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` through the SDK's runtime require hook. Plain Deno imports it fine.
- With `mysql@2`, a module-scope pool detaches its query: the db span arrives as its own root transaction on a different trace while the request transaction has no children.
- Without the fetch integration above, an outgoing `fetch()` gets no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers, so the trace ends at the server. `node:http` requests are traced and propagated.
- Error events carry the raw path in their `transaction` field while the transaction itself carries the route pattern.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/frameworks/react-router.mdx` and cross-link it from `guides/react-router/manual-setup.mdx` near `:400-401` and from the Node-support Expandable at `:186-197`.

heading: No page documents TanStack Start on Deno
title: Add a TanStack Start on Deno page with the Deno entry and noExternals
body:
`grep -rni deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/tanstackstart-react/` returns nothing, and `grep -rni tanstack docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/` also returns nothing. The guide is Node-only by construction: `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/tanstackstart-react/manual-setup/index.mdx:9` tags it `server-node`, `:286` heads the recommended section "With `--import` Flag (e.g. Node.js Server)", and `:354-358` gives the start script as `node --import ./.output/server/instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`.

Verified with `@sentry/tanstackstart-react` 10.67.0 on Deno 2.9.0, running the Nitro `node` output: keep the documented app shape (`sentryTanstackStart()` in `vite.config.ts`, `wrapFetchWithSentry` in `src/server.ts`, the Sentry request and function middleware in `src/start.ts`, and `instrument.server.mjs` calling `Sentry.init`). Deno has no `node --import`, so add a two-line `.output/server/deno-entry.mjs` that imports `./instrument.server.mjs` then `./index.mjs`, and start it with `PORT=<port> deno run --allow-net ... deno-entry.mjs`. For parameterized names, pass `nitro({ noExternals: ['@sentry/tanstackstart-react'] })` in `vite.config.ts`, so the plugin can inject route patterns into the bundled SDK. Build with vite 8.x and the pristine config: vite 7.3.2 with nitro 3.0.260903-beta crashes rollup with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getVariableForExportName')` whether or not Sentry is involved, and a pre-plugin that externalises every `@sentry/*` import gets past that crash but silently removes the route parametrization. Confirm the injection landed before deploying with `grep -l 'users/$userId' .output/server/_libs/sentry__tanstackstart-react.mjs`.

Works today:

- Server route errors, mechanism `auto.middleware.tanstackstart.request`.
- Parameterized server route names (`GET /users/$userId`, source `route`), with `noExternals` set, in both trace lifecycles. A Node control run of the same output produced the same names.
- Per-request isolation and incoming trace continuation.
- Database spans for `mysql`, injected at build time by the Sentry Vite plugin.
- Logs.

Known limits:

- If the build externalizes `@sentry/tanstackstart-react`, transaction names stay raw, for example `GET /users/123` with source `url`. This is a build-config effect, not a Deno one: the same build produces url-source names under Node, and the SDK emits no warning when the route-pattern substitution did not happen.
- The build is version-sensitive: vite 7.3.2 with nitro 3.0.260903-beta fails in rollup with or without Sentry, and the externalising pre-plugin that works around it costs the route names.
- Outgoing `fetch()` is not instrumented on Deno: no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/frameworks/tanstack-start.mdx`.
- Add a Deno start-command variant in `guides/tanstackstart-react/manual-setup/index.mdx` near `:354-358`.

heading: No page documents Remix on Deno
title: Add a Remix on Deno page covering installGlobals and the build-time setup
body:
The Remix guide names no runtime other than Node: `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/remix/index.mdx:4-9` scopes the guide with Node categories and `:12-16` carries only the Remix 3 alert, while `platform-includes/getting-started-prerequisites/javascript.remix.mdx:1-7` requires just Remix 2.0.0+. Greps for `deno`, `installGlobals` and `enableRuntimeChannelInjection` over `docs/` and `platform-includes/` return zero; `orchestrion` returns two hits, both on `common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx` (`:689` and `:1297`), so the option and the plugin are documented nowhere outside the migration page.

Verified on Remix 2.17.5 with the Remix Vite plugin and a custom `node:http` server on Deno 2.9.0: install with npm under Node using `--legacy-peer-deps`, set `deno.json` to `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}`, add `sentryRemixVitePlugin()`, imported from `@sentry/remix/vite`, next to `remix()` in `vite.config.ts`, export `handleError = Sentry.sentryHandleError` from `app/entry.server.tsx`, and import `instrument.server.mjs` as the first line of the server entry with `Sentry.instrumentBuild(build)`. Call `installGlobals()` from `@remix-run/node` at the top of `app/entry.server.tsx`, which is what `remix reveal` generates: it replaces Deno's native `fetch` with the `node:http`-backed polyfill, and outgoing requests are then traced. For database spans there are two shapes. Either import the driver before `instrument.server.mjs`, which needs no instrumentation path at all because mysql2 3.20+ publishes its own diagnostics channels; or set `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false` and bundle the server entry with `sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild`, with `@remix-run/server-runtime` bundled, `@sentry/*` and `mysql2` external, and a `createRequire` banner on the ESM output.

Works today:

- Loader errors, mechanism `auto.function.remix.server`.
- `GET users/:id` with source `route`, plus nested loader spans.
- Per-request isolation and incoming trace continuation.
- Outgoing `http.client` spans with trace headers, after `installGlobals()`, in both trace lifecycles.
- Database spans for `mysql2`, through either shape above, and logs.

Known limits:

- Without `installGlobals()`, outgoing `fetch()` produces no span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers. `node:http` and `undici` clients are traced without it.
- `installGlobals()` called from the server entry must run after `import './instrument.server.mjs'`. Calling it before `Sentry.init()` silently drops every transaction and span envelope for the whole process while errors keep arriving. In `app/entry.server.tsx`, the position `remix reveal` generates, the ordering takes care of itself.
- Replacing the polyfill with a hand-written fetch integration is not a substitute: it propagates the headers but suppresses every server transaction and span for the process.
- The esbuild bundle needs the `createRequire` banner; without it the server dies with `Dynamic require of "@sentry/server-utils" is not supported`. Bundling `@sentry/*` instead of leaving it external fails the same way.
- Turning the runtime hook off without the bundler plugin silently removes every server span, and leaving it on makes Deno abort at startup on a CommonJS dependency that does `require('*.json')`.
- Express cannot be used as the Remix server on Deno; it fails at import.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/frameworks/remix.mdx` and link it from `guides/remix/frameworks/index.mdx`, which today lists only the Cloudflare pages.
- Name the supported runtimes in `guides/remix/index.mdx:4-9` and in the prerequisites include, and document `enableRuntimeChannelInjection` and the orchestrion build plugin outside the migration page.

heading: No page documents SolidStart on Deno
title: Add a SolidStart on Deno install page and record its instrumentation limits
body:
`grep -rni deno` over `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/` returns zero, `index.mdx:1-7` names no server runtime, and there is no `platform-includes/getting-started-prerequisites/javascript.solidstart.mdx`. The tracing verification step at `index.mdx:444-470` tells the reader to create `src/routes/sentry-test.tsx`, throw from it and expect an issue, which never arrives on SolidStart 2. `guides/deno/index.mdx:1-18` covers only the Deno SDK, not a node-server Nitro build run under Deno.

Verified on SolidStart 2.0.2 with Nitro 3 beta, Vite 8 and `@sentry/solidstart` 10.67.0: install with npm and `--legacy-peer-deps`, and put `solidStart({ appRoot: './src' })`, `sentrySolidStart()` imported from `@sentry/solidstart/vite`, and `nitro({ serverDir: './server' })` in `vite.config.ts`. Initialise in a Nitro startup plugin (`server/plugins/sentry.ts`) that calls `Sentry.init()`; no `--import` preload and no instrument file are needed, because the Sentry Vite plugin bakes the library instrumentation into the bundle. Build with `NODE_ENV=production npx vite build` on Node — the plugin skips its instrumentation pass in development, and that pass is what produces the database spans — then run the `node-server` output with `PORT=<port> HOST=127.0.0.1 deno run -A .output/server/index.mjs` on Deno 2.9.0. For error capture, register a try/catch middleware as the first entry of the array form of `createMiddleware` and call `Sentry.captureException` there.

Works today:

- Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation.
- Database spans for `mysql2`, injected at build time by the Sentry Vite plugin.
- Logs.
- Errors from API routes, with the middleware above; errors thrown inside `'use server'` actions are already captured by the shipped `withServerActionInstrumentation` wrapper, mechanism `auto.function.solidstart`.
- Parameterized names, with `setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute` from `@sentry/server-utils`: an `onBeforeResponse` middleware that rebuilds the pattern from `event.params` covers API routes, and a `useCurrentMatches()` call in the Router root covers SSR pages. Verified in both trace lifecycles.
- Outgoing `fetch()`, with `winterCGFetchIntegration()` from `@sentry/vercel-edge` in the Nitro startup plugin, gated on Deno so a Node build does not get duplicate spans. It bundles cleanly into the node-server output and is an extra install.

Known limits:

- Unhandled errors from API routes are not captured on their own: SolidStart answers 500 and no event is sent, on Deno and on Node alike, so the guide's own verification snippet reports nothing. The object form of `createMiddleware` cannot fix this, because neither of its lifecycles wraps the handler; the array form is required, with the existing `sentryBeforeResponseMiddleware()` spread in through a nested object-form call.
- The Nitro error hook cannot help either: SolidStart builds its own inner H3 instance whose default `onError` turns the throw into a 500, so `@sentry/nitro`'s `error` hook never fires and adding `@sentry/nitro` as a module changes nothing.
- The SDK does not name server transactions: SolidStart mounts one catch-all Nitro route, so without the middleware above names arrive as the raw path with source `url`. `setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute` is not re-exported from `@sentry/solidstart`, so the app has to depend on `@sentry/server-utils` directly, and only the segment span is renamed; the inner non-segment `http.server` spans stay `GET` under the stream lifecycle.
- Scope data set during one request is inherited by later requests in the process: the first `setTag` lands on the shared default isolation scope. Node with the same build is clean. The mechanism was not established for this stack.
- Outgoing `fetch()` is not instrumented without the integration above; `node:http`/`node:https` clients produce `http.client` spans with headers on Deno either way.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/install/deno.mdx`, correct the verification step at `index.mdx:444-470`, and add the two missing platform-includes.

heading: The page for Hono on Cloudflare Workers misses the wiring or the limits
title: Document Hono on Cloudflare Workers: compatibility_date and build-time database spans
body:
The Hono guide already treats Cloudflare Workers as a first-class tab: `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hono/index.mdx:12` names Cloudflare Workers as a supported runtime, `:65-78` tells Workers users to install `@sentry/cloudflare` as a peer dependency they never import, `:129-144` is the "Cloudflare Workers: Enable Node.js Compatibility" Expandable, and `:240-262` (the Cloudflare Workers tab of "Add the Sentry Middleware") shows the `sentry(app, {...})` wiring. Two gaps: the Expandable sets `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]` but never `compatibility_date`, and the guide's only database sentence, `:162`, is Node.js-only.

Verified on the develop line: `npm install @sentry/hono @sentry/cloudflare hono`, a `wrangler.jsonc` with `compatibility_date: "2026-05-01"` and `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]`, `app.use(sentry(app, { dsn, tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }))` as the first middleware, `export default app`, run with `npx wrangler dev`. For database spans the same app is built through Vite instead, which needs three more packages, `npm install vite @cloudflare/vite-plugin mysql@2`, and a `vite.config.ts` with `plugins: [cloudflare(), sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ autoInstrumentation: false })]` from `@sentry/cloudflare/vite`, with `autoInstrumentation: false` because the Hono middleware already applies `withSentry`.

Works today:

- Unhandled route errors, parameterized route names (`GET /users/:id`, source `route`), per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers, `Sentry.logger` logs.
- `db` spans from a `mysql` query, through the Vite build only.

Known limits:

- A Worker bundled by `wrangler dev`/`wrangler deploy` alone emits no database spans and logs no warning.
- No `middleware.hono` spans on Workers: the transaction's `spans[]` holds only the `db` and `http.client` children.

What to change on `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hono/index.mdx`:

- Extend the Expandable at `:129-144` to set `compatibility_date` alongside `nodejs_compat`, matching `platform-includes/getting-started-config/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:5`.
- Add a "Database spans on Cloudflare Workers" subsection after the "Add the Sentry Middleware" section (`:227-359`), before "### Report Unhandled Exceptions" at `:360`, stating that database instrumentation on Workers is build-time only, showing the Vite config above, and linking to `/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin/`.
- Say in the same subsection that a Workers transaction carries no `middleware.hono` spans, so readers do not go looking for them.
- Link that subsection from `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/hono.mdx`, the 8-line stub that today only redirects to the Hono guide, so a reader who starts on the Cloudflare side reaches the database note too.

heading: No page documents Express on Cloudflare Workers
title: Add an Express on Cloudflare Workers page built with the Sentry Cloudflare Vite plugin
body:
Nothing documents Express on Workers. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/express/index.mdx:4-9` pins `sdk: sentry.javascript.node` with `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`, and grepping the Express guide for "cloudflare" or "workerd" returns nothing. In the other direction, the Cloudflare framework list at `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23` has no Express entry and `httpServerHandler`, `cloudflare:node` and `enable_nodejs_http_server_modules` appear nowhere under `docs/` or `platform-includes/`.

Verified on the develop line: Express 5 on workerd with `compatibility_date: "2026-05-01"` and `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat", "enable_nodejs_http_server_modules"]`, served through `httpServerHandler` from `cloudflare:node` and wrapped with `Sentry.withSentry()` from `@sentry/cloudflare`. Build the Worker with Vite: `plugins: [cloudflare(), sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()]` from `@sentry/cloudflare/vite`, then `npx vite build && npx wrangler dev --config dist/<worker>/wrangler.json`. Keep `httpServerHandler({ port: 8080 })` at module scope but create the Express app and call `app.listen()` inside `fetch`, memoized on first request: with build-time instrumentation on, a module-scope `app.get(...)` kills the Worker at startup with "Disallowed operation called within global scope". On a plain `wrangler` build the same app needs two app-side lines instead: `setupExpressErrorHandler(app)` from `@sentry/server-utils` (an extra dependency, since `@sentry/cloudflare` does not re-export it, so the `Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler(app)` form the Express guide shows is `undefined` in a Worker), and `patchExpressModule(express, () => ({}))` from `@sentry/core/server` before the app is built.

Works today:

- Vite build: unhandled route errors (mechanism `auto.http.express`), parameterized route names with `http.route`, per-request isolation across `await`, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers, `db` spans from `mysql2` or `mysql` 2.x nested under the Express handler span, `Sentry.logger` logs.
- Plain `wrangler` build: isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans and logs unaided; unhandled route errors after `setupExpressErrorHandler(app)` (mechanism `auto.middleware.express`); route names and handler/router spans after `patchExpressModule(express, () => ({}))`.

Known limits:

- A Worker bundled by plain `wrangler dev`/`wrangler deploy` gets no route names, no handler spans and no database spans unless you add app-side wiring: `setupExpressErrorHandler(app)` from `@sentry/server-utils` (not re-exported by `@sentry/cloudflare`) for error capture, and `patchExpressModule(express, () => ({}))` from `@sentry/core/server` for handler spans and route names, the latter only under the stream trace lifecycle and on a deprecated API.
- Database spans have no plain-`wrangler` equivalent at all: the build-time instrumentation of the Vite plugin is what injects the channels, and a wrangler-bundled Worker emits none and logs no warning.
- `vite dev` cannot start Express on workerd; build first, then run wrangler against the build output.
- `mysql2` on workerd needs `disableEval: true` in the connection options.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/express.mdx` with the wiring above and link it from `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23`.
- Correct `guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx` to the shipped options `buildTimeInstrumentation` and `autoInstrumentation`, both defaulting to `true`: the prose at `:30` that presents `useDiagnosticsChannelInjection` as something you must enable, the two snippets at `:40-44` and `:78-82`, and the `SdkOption` blocks at `:150-166` that document `_experimental.autoInstrumentation` and `_experimental.useDiagnosticsChannelInjection` as defaulting to `false`.

heading: No page documents Fastify on Cloudflare Workers
title: Note that Fastify does not run on Cloudflare Workers
body:
Neither guide says anything about this combination. `grep -rni "cloudflare|workerd" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/fastify/` returns zero hits, `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/fastify/index.mdx:4-9` declares the guide Node-only, and the Cloudflare framework list at `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23` names no Node HTTP framework at all. A reader gets no signal either way and spends the time finding out.

The audit ran Fastify 5.12.3 on workerd via `wrangler dev` with `compatibility_date: "2026-05-01"` and `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat", "enable_nodejs_http_server_modules"]`, serving through `httpServerHandler` from `cloudflare:node`. No wiring made Fastify serve a request, so there is no setup to document and no Sentry capability could be exercised. A control test with a plain `node:http` server behind the same `httpServerHandler` config did serve requests, so the Cloudflare half of the shape is fine.

- Works today: nothing; Fastify never serves a request on Workers.

Known limits:

- Constructing the app at module scope throws "Disallowed operation called within global scope", because Fastify's boot generates random values and schedules work.
- Constructing it lazily on the first request then fails when any route is registered, because Fastify's router compiles matchers with `new Function` and Workers forbid runtime code generation, with no compatibility flag that lifts it.
- Fastify 4 behaves the same way, so downgrading does not help.
- Declaring a route schema is not an escape either: `ajv` (validation) and `fast-json-stringify` (response serialization) compile with `new Function` and hit the same wall.

What to change:

- Add a "Node HTTP frameworks on Workers" note near Known Limitations at `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:368`, stating that Fastify does not run on Cloudflare Workers and why, and that the Cloudflare half of the shape is not the problem: `enable_nodejs_http_server_modules` plus `httpServerHandler` serve requests fine, it is the frameworks that cannot be constructed at module scope.
- Add a one-line runtime note to `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/fastify/index.mdx`, scoped to Workers, making clear Fastify on Node.js is unaffected.

heading: No page documents Koa on Cloudflare Workers
title: Add a Koa on Cloudflare Workers page covering the Vite build and module-scope rule
body:
Nothing documents Koa on Workers. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/koa/index.mdx:1-12` is a 12-line stub declaring `sdk: sentry.javascript.node` with `fallbackGuide: javascript.node`, and grepping it for "cloudflare" or "workerd" returns nothing. `grep -rin koa docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/` returns nothing, `guides/cloudflare/frameworks/` has no `koa.mdx`, the framework list at `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23` omits Koa, and `httpServerHandler` and `enable_nodejs_http_server_modules` appear nowhere in the docs.

Verified on the develop line: `npm install @sentry/cloudflare koa @koa/router` plus `vite` and `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` for the build. Koa 3 with `@koa/router` on workerd, `compatibility_date: "2026-05-01"`, `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat", "enable_nodejs_http_server_modules"]`, served through `httpServerHandler` from `cloudflare:node` and wrapped with `Sentry.withSentry()` from `@sentry/cloudflare`. Build with Vite: `plugins: [cloudflare(), sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()]` from `@sentry/cloudflare/vite` at its defaults, then `vite build` and run wrangler against the emitted config. `httpServerHandler({ port: 8080 })` stays at module scope; `new Koa()`, every `app.use()`, the router wiring and `app.listen()` must run inside `fetch`, behind a memoized promise. The plugin registers the Koa error listener itself, so no hand-written `app.on('error')` is needed on this build.

On a plain `wrangler` build, where none of that instrumentation exists, two app-side lines keep the Worker from being silent: `app.on('error', err => Sentry.captureException(err))`, Koa's own idiom, and inside a handler `Sentry.updateSpanName(Sentry.getRootSpan(Sentry.getActiveSpan()), `${ctx.method} ${ctx._matchedRoute}`)`, all four exports from `@sentry/cloudflare`. That yields a captured error and a route-shaped name with source `custom` rather than `route`.

Works today:

- Vite build: unhandled errors captured automatically (mechanism `auto.middleware.koa`, `handled: false`, from the error listener the Koa integration attaches), parameterized route names with `http.route`, per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers, `db` spans from `mysql2` or `mysql` 2.x, `Sentry.logger` logs.
- Plain `wrangler` build: isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans and logs unaided; errors and a custom-source route name with the two app-side lines above.

Known limits:

- Without the Vite build there is no Koa instrumentation at all: unless you add the two lines above, errors are swallowed with no event and the transaction is named from the raw URL (`GET /users/42`, source `url`).
- The manual rename gives source `custom`, not `route`, and no database spans exist on a plain `wrangler` build.
- Creating the Koa app at module scope makes the Worker fail to start with "Disallowed operation called within global scope".
- `mysql2` on workerd needs `disableEval: true` in the connection options.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/koa.mdx` with the wiring above and link it from `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23`.
- Add the module-scope rule as a shared note on `guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx`.
- Include the plain-`wrangler` fallback on the new page, so readers who cannot build with Vite still get errors and a usable transaction name.

heading: No page documents Hapi on Cloudflare Workers
title: Add a Hapi on Cloudflare Workers page and document build-time instrumentation
body:
Nothing documents Hapi on Workers. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hapi/index.mdx:4-5` sets `sdk: sentry.javascript.node` with `fallbackGuide: javascript.node` and its whole body is one include at `:12`. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/` holds no `hapi.mdx` and the framework list at `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23` omits Hapi. Separately, `packages/server-utils/package.json:30-62` exports seven orchestrion entry points (`./orchestrion/config` plus six bundler entries: vite, rollup, webpack, webpack-loader, esbuild and bun), and the only mention of any of them in the docs is one line of the v10-to-v11 migration guide at `common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:1297`; no how-to page explains them.

Verified on the develop line: `@hapi/hapi` 21 on workerd with `compatibility_date: "2026-05-01"` and `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat", "enable_nodejs_http_server_modules"]`, served through `httpServerHandler` from `cloudflare:node` and wrapped with `Sentry.withSentry()` from `@sentry/cloudflare`. Build-time instrumentation is what makes the framework visible, by either of two public routes: `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` from `@sentry/cloudflare/vite` in a Vite build, or `sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild` when you pre-bundle the Worker yourself and point wrangler's `main` at the output (an esbuild banner that backs `require` with statically imported `node:` builtins is needed, or workerd fails at startup on `node:async_hooks`). With build-time instrumentation on, register routes and call `server.start()` inside the first `fetch`, never at module scope: the injected wrapper around `Server.prototype.route` starts a span, and the isolate then fails to boot with "Disallowed operation called within global scope". `hapiIntegration()` is not in the Cloudflare default integrations and is not re-exported by `@sentry/cloudflare`, so add it by hand from `@sentry/server-utils`.

Works today:

- Parameterized transaction names (`GET /users/{id}`, source `route`) with nested router and extension spans, per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers, `db` spans from a `mysql` query, `Sentry.logger` logs, all on a build-time-instrumented bundle.
- Route handler errors, after adding an `onRequest` extension that drops the premature `close` event: `server.ext('onRequest', (request, h) => { const res = request.raw.res; const on = res.on.bind(res); res.on = (e, l) => (e === 'close' ? res : on(e, l)); return h.continue; })`. With that in place `hapiIntegration()` captures the throw itself, with the transaction name and mechanism `auto.function.hapi`.
- On a plain `wrangler` build, parameterized names from a four-line `onPreResponse` extension: `Sentry.updateSpanName(root, `${request.method.toUpperCase()} ${request.route.path}`)` plus `root.setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, 'route')` on `Sentry.getRootSpan(Sentry.getActiveSpan())`, all exports of `@sentry/cloudflare`.

Known limits:

- Without the `onRequest` fix, nothing is captured: on workerd the `node:http` `ServerResponse` emits `close` before `finish` with `writableEnded` still false, hapi reads that as a client disconnect, answers 499 and never fires its `request`/`error` event. A `server.ext('onPreResponse')` that calls `Sentry.captureException` when `request.response.isBoom` is the fallback on builds without the instrumentation.
- A plain `wrangler` build emits no database spans and no router or extension spans, and names the transaction from the raw URL unless you add the `onPreResponse` rename; wrangler's own bundler takes no plugins.
- `mysql` 2.x works unchanged; `mysql2` needs `disableEval: true` in the connection options.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/hapi.mdx` with the wiring above and link it from `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23`.
- Add `guides/cloudflare/features/build-time-instrumentation.mdx` covering `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` for esbuild, rollup and webpack, and link it from the Vite plugin page.

heading: No page documents Oak on Cloudflare Workers
title: Add an Oak on Cloudflare Workers page covering the JSR install and withSentry wiring
body:
Oak is absent from the docs entirely. `grep -ril "oak" docs/platforms/javascript/ platform-includes/` returns nothing, there is no Oak guide on any runtime, `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/` contains only astro, hono, the two hydrogen pages, index, nextjs, nuxt, remix, sveltekit and tanstack-start, and the framework list at `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23` omits Oak.

Verified on the develop line: Oak 17.2.0 on workerd with `compatibility_date: "2026-05-01"` and `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]`. Oak's current line ships only to JSR, so install it through the JSR npm bridge (`@jsr:registry=https://npm.jsr.io` in `.npmrc`, then `npm install '@oak/oak@npm:@jsr/oak__oak@17.2.0'`); the plain npm package, `@oakserver/oak`, stops at 14.1.0. Install `@sentry/server-utils` explicitly alongside `@sentry/cloudflare`, in the same install command: without it the wrangler build fails to resolve `@sentry/server-utils/no-diagnostic-channels`. Oak's `Application.fetch` is already a Workers fetch handler, so no adapter is needed and `withSentry` is the whole wiring: `export default Sentry.withSentry((env) => ({ dsn: env.SENTRY_DSN, tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }), { fetch: (request, env, ctx) => app.fetch(request, env, ctx) })`. Run with `npx wrangler dev`; no bundler plugin is required.

Works today:

- Unhandled errors (Oak rethrows rather than swallowing), per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers, `db` spans from a `mysql` query under plain `wrangler dev`, `Sentry.logger` logs.

Known limits:

- There is no Sentry Oak integration, so the request span is named from the raw URL under `traceLifecycle: 'static'` and from the HTTP method alone under the default `'stream'`, never from the matched route pattern. One Oak middleware, given below, restores parameterized names with source `route` in both lifecycles.
- The server span is reported with status `ok` even when the handler threw.
- `mysql` 2.x works with no configuration; `mysql2` emits spans but its query fails on workerd unless you pass `disableEval: true` in the connection options, which this cell did not exercise.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/oak.mdx` with the JSR install, the wrangler config, the `withSentry` entry above, and a Works/limits summary matching the two bullet lists here.
- Add Oak to the framework list at `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23`.
- Show the route-name middleware on that page: registered before `router.routes()`, it reads `ctx.matched` inside a `try/finally` (so it also runs when a handler throws) and calls `Sentry.updateSpanName(root, routeName)`, `root.setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, 'route')` and `root.setAttribute('http.route', pattern)` on `Sentry.getRootSpan(Sentry.getActiveSpan())`, plus `Sentry.getIsolationScope().setTransactionName(routeName)` so error events carry the route too, all exports of `@sentry/cloudflare`. Use the exported `SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE` constant, not the legacy string `'sentry.source'`, which the SDK ignores; with the constant both trace lifecycles report source `route`.

heading: No page documents Fresh on Cloudflare Workers
title: Add a Fresh 2 on Cloudflare Workers page with the esbuild orchestrion build step
body:
Fresh is absent from the docs. There is no `guides/fresh/` directory, and the only "fresh" hits under `docs/platforms/javascript/` are the ordinary English word (for example `guides/cloudflare/agent-tracing/agents-sdk.mdx:43`). The Cloudflare framework list at `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23` names Astro, Hono, Hydrogen, Next.js, Nuxt, Remix, SvelteKit and TanStack Start and nothing else.

Verified on the develop line: Fresh 2 on workerd with `compatibility_date: "2026-05-01"` and `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]`. Fresh's own Vite plugin emits `_fresh/server.js` whose default export is already `{ fetch }`, so no Cloudflare adapter is needed. Keep `@sentry/cloudflare` and any database driver out of the Fresh SSR bundle via `environments.ssr.build.rollupOptions.external`, then write a separate wrangler entry that wraps Fresh's server with `Sentry.withSentry()` from `@sentry/cloudflare`. For database spans, bundle that wrangler entry yourself with esbuild plus `sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild`, and point wrangler's `main` at the output. That esbuild build needs a banner defining a `globalThis.require` backed by static `node:*` imports, or workerd dies at the first query with "Dynamic require of 'diagnostics_channel' is not supported".

Route names take one middleware in `main.ts`, registered before `app.fsRoutes()`: in a `finally` around `ctx.next()`, call `rootSpan.updateName(`${ctx.req.method} ${ctx.route}`)`, then `rootSpan.setAttribute("http.route", ctx.route)` and `rootSpan.setAttribute(Sentry.SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE, "route")`, on `Sentry.getRootSpan(Sentry.getActiveSpan())` from `@sentry/cloudflare`. The order matters: the source has to be set after the rename, because both `span.updateName()` and `Sentry.updateSpanName()` mark the name `custom`. The `finally` matters too, because Fresh's error boundary sits outside user middleware, so a throwing route would otherwise keep the unparameterized name.

Works today:

- Per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers, `Sentry.logger` logs, and `db` spans through the esbuild orchestrion build.
- Parameterized route names (`GET /users/:id`, source `route`) in both trace lifecycles, with the `main.ts` middleware above.

Known limits:

- Nothing a route handler, middleware or page component throws reaches Sentry on its own: Fresh's default error handler catches it and returns a 500, leaving only the request span marked `internal_error`. Adding `Sentry.captureConsoleIntegration({ levels: ["error"] })` to the `withSentry` options turns Fresh's own `console.error(error)` into an event, at the cost of reporting every other `console.error`.
- Out of the box there are no route names: the request span is named from the URL (`static`) or the HTTP method alone (`stream`). Fresh does call `getActiveSpan()?.updateName()` and set `http.route` through `@opentelemetry/api`, but `@sentry/cloudflare` registers no OpenTelemetry global, so those calls land on a no-op tracer.
- `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` does not belong in Fresh's `vite.config.ts`: there is no Cloudflare worker environment for it to instrument, and adding it there is worse than a no-op, it injects the channels and then breaks the driver under workerd through Vite's CJS interop (`createRequire(import.meta.url)` with unresolvable module ids).
- `mysql` 2.x is the driver this ran on; `mysql2` is instrumented but its query fails on workerd unless you pass `disableEval: true`, which this cell did not exercise.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/fresh.mdx` with the wiring above and link it from `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23`.
- Add the missing-worker-environment caveat to `guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx:13-18`, stating that in a Vite build with no Cloudflare worker environment the plugin breaks bundled drivers rather than doing nothing.

heading: No page documents NestJS on Cloudflare Workers
title: Add a NestJS on Cloudflare Workers page using the esbuild orchestrion plugin
body:
Nothing documents NestJS on Workers. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nestjs/index.mdx:5-9` sets `fallbackGuide: javascript.node` with `server-node` categories and carries no runtime caveat. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/` has no `nestjs.mdx`, the framework list at `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23` omits Nest, `httpServerHandler` appears nowhere under `docs/` or `platform-includes/`, and `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` appears exactly once, in the v10-to-v11 migration guide at `common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:1297`, with no how-to page behind it.

Verified on the develop line: NestJS 11 with `@nestjs/platform-express` on workerd, `compatibility_date: "2026-05-01"`, `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat", "enable_nodejs_http_modules", "enable_nodejs_http_server_modules"]`, served through `httpServerHandler` from `cloudflare:node` and wrapped with `Sentry.withSentry()` from `@sentry/cloudflare`. Nest must be booted lazily inside `fetch`, not at module scope. Bundle the Worker with esbuild plus `sentryOrchestrionPlugin()` from `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild` and point wrangler's `main` at the output. Three esbuild details decide whether the bundle boots at all: a banner whose `createRequire` shim strips the `node:` prefix (workerd's `createRequire` cannot resolve `node:`-prefixed builtins, and `node:process` additionally needs an alias returning `globalThis.process`), aliases stubbing `class-validator`, `class-transformer`, `@nestjs/microservices*` and `@nestjs/websockets/socket-module`, and leaving `mainFields`/`conditions` alone, because preferring ESM hands Express the ESM build of `is-promise` and the Worker dies on the first request. Error capture uses exactly the Node wiring: install `@sentry/nestjs` next to `@sentry/cloudflare` and register `SentryModule.forRoot()` in `imports` and `SentryGlobalFilter` from `@sentry/nestjs/setup` as an `APP_FILTER` provider.

Works today:

- Unhandled controller errors through `SentryGlobalFilter` (mechanism `auto.http.nestjs.global_filter`, `handled: false`), parameterized route names with middleware and handler spans, per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers, `db` spans, `Sentry.logger` logs.
- Expected `HttpException`s stay unreported (a `NotFoundException` yields status `not_found` and no event), the same behavior as on Node.
- Error capture needs no bundler plugin: `SentryGlobalFilter` works on a plain `wrangler` build too, since `@sentry/nestjs/setup` depends only on `@nestjs/*` and `@sentry/core`.

Known limits:

- Plain `wrangler` bundling gives no route names and no database spans: those need the orchestrion esbuild build.
- `mysql2` on workerd needs `disableEval: true` in the connection options, and the connection must be opened inside the request handler rather than at module scope.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/nestjs.mdx` with the wiring above and link it from `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23`.
- Put the `disableEval` and connection-placement rules in a shared Workers database-driver note.

heading: The page for Next.js on Cloudflare Workers misses the wiring or the limits
title: Document outgoing fetch and database spans for Next.js on Cloudflare Workers
body:
`docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/nextjs.mdx` is the only page for this combination and is 56 lines long. `:6` says the SDK supports Next.js on Workers "but requires additional configuration", `:14` points at OpenNext, `:15` at the plain Next.js install guide, `:28-38` sets `nodejs_compat`, `:40-54` sets a minimum `compatibility_date`, and `:56` closes with "You should start seeing error events, traces, and logs appear in Sentry." That is the entire body of advice. `disableEval` appears nowhere in the docs, and `@sentry/cloudflare` is never mentioned on the page.

Verified on the develop line: Next.js 15 App Router via `@opennextjs/cloudflare`, `compatibility_date: "2026-05-01"`, `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]`, with `src/instrumentation.ts` exporting `register` and `onRequestError = Sentry.captureRequestError`, `sentry.server.config.ts` calling `Sentry.init`, and a CommonJS `next.config.js` wrapped with `withSentryConfig` from `@sentry/nextjs/config`. The config file has to be CommonJS: `import { withSentryConfig } from '@sentry/nextjs'` in an ESM `next.config.mjs` fails with "Named export 'withSentryConfig' not found", because the exports map puts the CJS `node` condition ahead of `import`. Outgoing HTTP needs one addition: install `@sentry/cloudflare` explicitly, it is not a transitive dependency, and add `fetchIntegration()` from it to the `integrations` array in `sentry.server.config.ts`; that one integration covers `node:http` calls as well as global `fetch`.

Works today:

- Unhandled route handler errors, parameterized route names (`GET /api/users/[id]`, source `route`), per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, `Sentry.logger` logs.
- Outgoing `fetch` and `node:http` spans with `sentry-trace`/`baggage` propagation, once `fetchIntegration()` from `@sentry/cloudflare` is added.
- `db` spans from `mysql2`, with `disableEval: true` in the connection options.

Known limits:

- Only drivers that publish their own diagnostics channels produce database spans; `mysql` 2.x produces none on Workers. The visible symptom at init is the SDK logging "Failed to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks, so channel-based integrations will not record spans" with `TypeError: port1.on is not a function`. Listing the driver in `serverExternalPackages` is not an escape hatch: it produces spans but breaks the driver with `PROTOCOL_INCORRECT_PACKET_SEQUENCE`.
- `sendDefaultPii` is gone on the v11 line; leaving it in `sentry.server.config.ts` fails the `next build` type check.

What to change on `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/nextjs.mdx`:

- Add an "Instrument Outgoing HTTP Requests" section after `:54` with the `@sentry/cloudflare` install and the `fetchIntegration()` snippet.
- Add a "Database Spans" section covering `disableEval: true` and the driver limit.

heading: The page for Nuxt on Cloudflare Workers misses the wiring or the limits
title: Document server route naming for Nuxt on Cloudflare Workers
body:
The combination is documented. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/nuxt.mdx:1-11` is a "Nuxt on Cloudflare" page that names Nitro's `cloudflare_module` preset at `:6` and pulls in the shared include at `:8-11`. The Cloudflare branch of that include is `platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.nuxt.mdx:255-316`: the wrangler config at `:259-262`, the warning to delete an existing `sentry.server.config.ts` at `:270-273`, the `sentryCloudflareNitroPlugin` server plugin at `:280-287` and the `nitroApp` variant at `:300-310`. What no page describes is how the request span is named on Cloudflare: `grep -rn -i "route name|segment name" guides/cloudflare/ platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.nuxt.mdx` returns zero hits.

Verified on the develop line: Nuxt 4.2 with the `cloudflare_module` preset, `compatibility_date: "2026-05-01"`, `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]`, and `server/plugins/sentry.ts` registering `sentryCloudflareNitroPlugin` from `@sentry/nuxt/module/plugins`. Six of seven capabilities worked with that wiring, with no bundler plugin and no extra Sentry step, but two `nuxt.config.ts` settings that no page mentions were needed to get there: `nitro.cloudflare: { nodeCompat: true, deployConfig: false }`, and `nitro.alias: { 'readable-stream': 'node:stream' }` for the bundled `mysql` driver to boot under unenv. Install only `@sentry/nuxt` and `@sentry/cloudflare`: adding `@sentry/nitro` pulls `nitro@3` in next to Nuxt 4's nitropack. Verification has to run on a build, since the SDK is inert under `nuxt dev` (orchestrion is skipped in dev and there is no workerd): `nuxt build`, then `wrangler dev`.

Works today:

- Unhandled server route errors through Nitro's error hook, parameterized route names for routes such as `server/api/users/[id].ts` (`GET /api/users/:id`, source `route`, with `http.route`), per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers, `db` spans with no manual bundler step, `Sentry.logger` logs.

Known limits:

- A server route with no parameters gets no `http.route` attribute, so its span is named by HTTP method alone under the default `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` and from the request URL, with source `url`, under `'static'`. Parameterized routes such as `server/api/users/[id].ts` are unaffected.
- Nothing is reported under `nuxt dev` at all; the instrumentation exists only in a built Worker.

What to change on `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/nuxt.mdx`:

- Replace the bare include passthrough with a page that keeps the include and adds a "Server Route Names" section stating the parameterless-route limit above, in both trace lifecycles.
- Note that database spans need no extra _Sentry_ configuration on the Cloudflare presets, and give the two Nitro settings they do need: `nitro.cloudflare: { nodeCompat: true, deployConfig: false }` and, for the `mysql` driver, `nitro.alias: { 'readable-stream': 'node:stream' }`.
- Show the ship-today fix for parameterless routes in the same section: a second Nitro plugin, registered next to the Sentry one, that hooks `beforeResponse`, reads `event.context.matchedRoute.path` and sets `http.route` on the root span (`Sentry.getRootSpan(Sentry.getActiveSpan())` from `@sentry/cloudflare`) when it carries none.

heading: The page for SvelteKit on Cloudflare Workers misses the wiring or the limits
title: Document route naming and database-span setup for SvelteKit on Cloudflare Workers
body:
The combination is documented. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/sveltekit.mdx:1-9` is a "SvelteKit on Cloudflare" page that renders the shared include; the Cloudflare branch is `platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.sveltekit.mdx:299-347`, with the `sequence(initCloudflareSentryHandle({...}), sentryHandle())` snippet at `:310-343`, `handleErrorWithSentry` at `:340-342`, "Configure Vite" at `:351-376` with `sentrySvelteKit()` at `:369`, and the wrangler config at `:378-387`. Two things the run needed are absent: `grep -rn noExternal docs/platforms/javascript platform-includes` returns zero hits, and no page describes how the segment span is named on Cloudflare.

Verified on the develop line: SvelteKit 2.70 with `@sveltejs/adapter-cloudflare` 5, `compatibility_date: "2026-05-01"`, `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]`, `sentrySvelteKit()` from `@sentry/sveltekit/vite` before `sveltekit()`, and `src/hooks.server.ts` exactly as the include shows. `vite build`, then `wrangler dev`.

Works today:

- Unhandled errors through `handleErrorWithSentry` (mechanism `auto.function.sveltekit.handle_error`), per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers, `Sentry.logger` logs.
- `db` spans from the build-time transform `sentrySvelteKit()` already installs, with no extra configuration on a pnpm install.

Known limits:

- The transaction/segment span is named from the raw URL under `traceLifecycle: 'static'` and by HTTP method alone under the default `'stream'`; the SvelteKit route id and `http.route` only reach a child span. This hits every route except `/`, not just parameterized ones, because the Cloudflare wrapper keeps only a name whose source is already `route`.
- SvelteKit's native tracing (`kit.experimental.tracing.server`) makes this worse rather than better: on Cloudflare it removes the route-named `http.server` span entirely, leaving the route only as an attribute on a `function` span.
- On a flat `node_modules` (npm or Yarn) the build fails until `ssr: { noExternal: ['@sentry/core', '@sentry/conventions', '@opentelemetry/api'] }` is added to `vite.config.js`.

What to change on `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/sveltekit.mdx`:

- Keep the include and add a "Route Names on Cloudflare Workers" section stating the naming limit above and showing the verified fix: one user-land `handle` inserted between `initCloudflareSentryHandle` and `sentryHandle` in the `sequence`, which takes `getRootSpan(getActiveSpan())` from `@sentry/sveltekit`, calls `updateName` on it with ``${event.request.method} ${event.route.id}`` and sets `sentry.segment.name.source` to `route` plus `http.route`. Use `updateName` and the source attribute, not `Sentry.updateSpanName`, which stamps the source `custom`. It works in both trace lifecycles.
- Add a "Database Spans" section stating that no extra setup is needed on pnpm and giving the `ssr.noExternal` entry for npm and Yarn installs.

heading: No page documents React Router on Cloudflare Workers
title: Add a React Router 7 on Cloudflare Workers page
body:
No page documents React Router framework mode on Workers. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/react-router/` holds only `index.mdx`, `manual-setup.mdx` and `profiling/`, and a case-insensitive grep for "cloudflare" across it returns zero hits. In the other direction, `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/` has no `react-router.mdx` and the framework list at `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23` omits React Router. The nearest page, `guides/cloudflare/frameworks/hydrogen-react-router.mdx:186-215`, is Shopify Oxygen-specific and prescribes different wiring.

Verified on the develop line: React Router 7.18 in framework mode with SSR, `compatibility_date: "2026-05-01"`, `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]`. Install `@sentry/react-router` and `@sentry/cloudflare` (a separate install), and pin `@react-router/node` to `^7` next to `react-router` 7: nothing on Workers uses it, but `@sentry/react-router`'s peer range otherwise makes npm hoist 8.3.1 and the install aborts with `ERESOLVE`. `react-router.config.ts` needs `ssr: true` and `future: { v8_viteEnvironmentApi: true }`, without which the build dies in `[commonjs--resolver]` with `id.endsWith is not a function`, a message that names neither plugin. `vite.config.ts` combines `cloudflare({ viteEnvironment: { name: 'ssr' } })`, `reactRouter()` and `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` from `@sentry/cloudflare/vite`. `app/entry.server.tsx` exports a `handleError` that calls `Sentry.captureException`, written by hand because `createSentryHandleError` lives only on the node entry: `@sentry/react-router/cloudflare` re-exports `../client`, `wrapSentryHandleRequest` and `injectTraceMetaTags` and nothing else. `wrapSentryHandleRequest` supplies the route names, and `injectTraceMetaTags` is what hands the browser its trace.

Works today:

- Loader errors, parameterized route names (`GET /users/:id`, source `route`), per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers, `db` spans from `mysql` through the Vite plugin's build-time instrumentation, `Sentry.logger` logs.

Known limits:

- Without the hand-written `handleError` export, React Router routes the throw into the ErrorBoundary and no event is sent; `createSentryHandleError` is not available on the Cloudflare entry.
- Building with `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ buildTimeInstrumentation: false })` removes all database spans.
- `mysql` 2.x is the driver this ran on; `mysql2` queries fail on workerd unless you pass `disableEval: true` in the connection options, which this cell did not exercise.
- Only the server runtime was exercised; the client half of `@sentry/react-router` was not part of this run.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/react-router.mdx` with the package set, wrangler config, Vite configuration and worker entry above.
- Add React Router to the framework list at `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23` and a Cloudflare pointer to `guides/react-router/index.mdx`.

heading: The page for TanStack Start on Cloudflare Workers misses the wiring or the limits
title: Add a "Configure Vite" step to the TanStack Start on Cloudflare page
body:
`docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/tanstack-start.mdx:1-281` covers this combination and is linked from `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:23`. `:10` scopes the page to Cloudflare Workers built with `@cloudflare/vite-plugin`, `:16-47` covers the install, `:50` states that the server entry must be wrapped with `Sentry.withSentry` from `@sentry/cloudflare`, `:59-100` shows the custom server entry with `wrapFetchWithSentry` from `@sentry/tanstackstart-react` inside `Sentry.withSentry(...)`, `:102-123` the `"main": "src/server.ts"` wrangler change, `:125` the client configuration, `:184` server-side error capture, `:221` source maps and `:232` verification. The page has no Vite configuration section at all: `sentryTanstackStart` appears nowhere on it, and the only two "vite" mentions are incidental, at `:10` and `:258`. It also never states which versions the setup was exercised against.

Verified on the develop line: TanStack Start (React) v1.136 with file-based routing, React 19, `compatibility_date: "2026-05-01"`, `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]`, wrangler 4.129.0. The page's wiring was exercised as shown, plus one step the page never mentions: `sentryTanstackStart()` from `@sentry/tanstackstart-react/vite` in `vite.config.ts`. Plugin order matters: `cloudflare({ viteEnvironment: { name: 'ssr' } })` first, `tanstackStart()`, then `sentryTanstackStart()`. `src/start.ts` registers `sentryGlobalRequestMiddleware` and `sentryGlobalFunctionMiddleware` first in their arrays, and `src/router.tsx` must export `getRouter`, not `createRouter`, or the client build fails. Run `vite build`, then `wrangler dev` against the emitted config.

Works today:

- Unhandled route handler errors, parameterized route names (`GET /users/$id`, source `route`, with `http.route`), per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers, `db` spans, `Sentry.logger` logs.

Known limits:

- Without `sentryTanstackStart()` in `vite.config.ts`, two capabilities disappear at once: route names fall back to the raw URL (`GET /users/123`, source `url`), because that plugin defines `__SENTRY_ROUTE_PATTERNS__`, which `wrapFetchWithSentry` reads, and database spans vanish, because the same plugin runs `sentryOrchestrionPlugin`.
- `vite dev` produces no database spans on this stack at all: the orchestrion plugin returns early when `NODE_ENV` is `development`. Use `vite build` plus `wrangler dev`.
- Only the server runtime was exercised; the client half of the SDK was not part of this run.

What to change on `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/tanstack-start.mdx`:

- Add a "Configure Vite" step to the Configure section showing the full plugin chain in order, `cloudflare({ viteEnvironment: { name: 'ssr' } })`, then `tanstackStart()`, then `sentryTanstackStart()`, and stating that without the last one route names fall back to source `url` and database spans are not recorded.
- Say in that step that `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` should not be added to a TanStack Start app, since the TanStack plugin chain plus the explicit `withSentry` in `src/server.ts` already covers it, and that database spans need `vite build`, not `vite dev`.
- Add a tested-versions note near `:10` recording the combination above.

heading: No page documents SolidStart on Cloudflare Workers
title: Add a SolidStart on Cloudflare Workers page wiring the Nitro output with withSentry
body:
Nothing documents this combination in either direction. `grep -rn -i cloudflare docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/` returns zero hits across `index.mdx`, `install/`, `features/` and `profiling/`. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/` has no `solidstart.mdx` and the framework list at `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23` omits SolidStart. The generic Workers entry pattern the run relied on is documented only at `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:111`, with no SolidStart context.

Verified on the develop line: SolidStart 1.3 with the `cloudflare-module` Nitro preset, `compatibility_date: "2026-05-01"`, `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]`. `@sentry/solidstart` itself does not run on Workers, so keep it for the browser and wire the server side by hand: set `server: { preset: 'cloudflare-module', rollupConfig: { external: ['@sentry/cloudflare'] } }` in `app.config.ts` so Nitro does not inline a second SDK copy, then write a `worker.mjs` that wraps the built Nitro handler with `Sentry.withSentry()` from `@sentry/cloudflare` and point wrangler's `main` at that wrapper. Add a Nitro server plugin registered through `server.plugins` that forwards Nitro's `error` hook to `Sentry.captureException`, otherwise thrown server errors never become events. Nitro emits no wrangler config for the `cloudflare-module` preset, so write `wrangler.jsonc` by hand: `main` pointing at the wrapper, plus an assets entry for `.output/public` with its `ASSETS` binding. Do not skip `rollupConfig.external`: without it Nitro inlines a second `@sentry/cloudflare`, and the failure is silent rather than loud, because `Sentry.setTag` and `Sentry.captureException` in a route handler then run against an uninitialised client while the wrapper's request transactions keep arriving and make the setup look healthy.

Works today:

- Server errors through the Nitro error hook, per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers, `Sentry.logger` logs, and browser errors with `Sentry.init` from `@sentry/solidstart` in `src/entry-client.tsx`.

Known limits:

- Server transactions never carry the file-route pattern: under `traceLifecycle: 'static'` the name is the raw request URL with source `url`, and under the default `'stream'` the path is gone altogether and the span is named bare `GET`. There is no Sentry SolidStart router integration on this runtime.
- Errors thrown while a page renders on the server stay uncaptured even with the Nitro error plugin, because SolidStart streams the render through a detached pipe.
- There is no server-to-client trace continuation: nothing injects a `sentry-trace` meta tag into the SSR HTML.
- Database spans were not exercised, and no Sentry database instrumentation path exists for this vinxi/Nitro/rollup build shape.

What to change:

- Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/solidstart.mdx` with the wiring above and the limits.
