- Show the route-name fix on that page: `src/middleware.ts`, registered with `middleware: './src/middleware.ts'` in `app.config.ts`, that builds a radix3 router from the `vinxi/routes` file-route table, looks the request path up in it, and on `Sentry.getRootSpan(Sentry.getActiveSpan())` from `@sentry/cloudflare` calls `updateName` with the matched pattern and sets the segment name source to `route`.
- Link it from `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23` and from `guides/solidstart/index.mdx`.

heading: GlobalHandlers page renders on the Cloudflare guide; @sentry/cloudflare has no such export
title: Exclude Cloudflare from the GlobalHandlers integration page
body:
`docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/integrations/globalhandlers.mdx:4-18` lists a `notSupported` set that omits `javascript.cloudflare`, so the page renders on the Cloudflare guide. A Cloudflare reader sees `_Import name: Sentry.globalHandlersIntegration_` at `:27` and "This integration is enabled by default" at `:29` — even though the page's own alert at `:23` says it "only works in the Browser and Deno runtimes".

On develop, `globalHandlers` appears nowhere in `packages/cloudflare/src`, so `Sentry.globalHandlersIntegration` is `undefined` when imported from `@sentry/cloudflare`. Deno is the runtime the alert is right about: `packages/deno/src/index.ts:163` on develop (`:160` at the pin) exports it and `packages/deno/src/sdk.ts:45` installs it by default.

`javascript.cloudflare` is not the only gap in that list: `javascript.vercel-edge` is missing from it too, and `globalHandlers` appears nowhere in `packages/vercel-edge/src` either.

What to change:

- Add `javascript.cloudflare` to the `notSupported` list in `globalhandlers.mdx`.
- While the list is open, walk the other non-browser JavaScript guides and add the ones that are missing, starting with `javascript.vercel-edge`.
- Leave the Deno rendering as is, since the export and the default both exist there.

heading: trpcMiddleware page lists javascript.deno, but @sentry/deno does not export it
title: Remove javascript.deno from the trpcMiddleware supported list
body:
`docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/integrations/trpc.mdx:24` lists `javascript.deno` under `supported`, so the tRPC page renders on the Deno guide and instructs the reader to call `Sentry.trpcMiddleware`. The page's alert at `:32` repeats the claim in prose: "This integration only works inside server environments (Node.js, Bun, Deno)".

On develop, `trpcMiddleware` appears nowhere in `packages/deno/src`. The Deno entry point re-exports only `wrapMcpServerWithSentry` from `@sentry/core/server` (`packages/deno/src/index.ts:104`), with `instrumentPostgresJsSql` now coming from `@sentry/server-utils` at `:105`; at the pin both names were on `:104`. Either way `Sentry.trpcMiddleware` is `undefined` for a Deno user following the page. The two neighbouring runtimes do export it — `packages/bun/src/index.ts:156` on develop (`:154` at the pin) and `packages/cloudflare/src/index.ts:109` — and their entries in the same list are accurate, though the alert never names Cloudflare.

What to change:

- Delete the `- javascript.deno` line from the `supported` frontmatter in `trpc.mdx`.
- Fix the alert at `:32` in the same edit: drop Deno from the runtime list and add Cloudflare, otherwise the page keeps the wrong claim in prose.
- Keep `javascript.bun` and `javascript.cloudflare`, which match the shipped exports.

heading: Thirteen database and library integration pages are hidden from the Deno guide
title: Show the database and library integration pages on the Deno guide
body:
Thirteen integration pages under `docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/integrations/` gate themselves to a `supported` allowlist that includes `javascript.bun` but not `javascript.deno`: `mysql.mdx:24`, `mysql2.mdx:24`, `postgres.mdx:24`, `redis.mdx:24`, `mongo.mdx:24`, `graphql.mdx:24`, `mongoose.mdx:23`, `knex.mdx:23`, `dataloader.mdx:23`, `kafka.mdx:23`, `genericpool.mdx:23`, `prisma.mdx:23` and `firebase.mdx:9`. All thirteen are invisible on the Deno guide.

On develop, `packages/deno/src/index.ts:119-147` (`:118-144` at the pin) re-exports twelve of these integrations from `@sentry/server-utils`, so all thirteen are usable on Deno. `packages/deno/src/sdk.ts:48` spreads `getTracingIntegrations()` (`packages/server-utils/src/integrations/index.ts:31-58` on develop, `:31-56` at the pin), which installs eleven of them by default: graphql, mongo, mongoose, mysql, mysql2, redis, postgres, prisma, genericPool, kafka and firebase. `dataloaderIntegration` and `knexIntegration` are re-exported but opt-in — the user adds them to `integrations`, on Deno exactly as on Node — which the comment at `packages/deno/src/index.ts:114-117` states in prose. Prisma is the one that is on by default without being re-exported from `@sentry/deno`.

Twelve of the thirteen pages also carry an alert reading "This integration only works in the Node.js and Bun runtimes" (`mysql.mdx:30`, `knex.mdx:29`, `dataloader.mdx:29`, `prisma.mdx:29` and so on); `firebase.mdx` is the one without an alert.

What to change:

- Add `- javascript.deno` to the `supported` list on all thirteen pages.
- Rewrite the "This integration only works in the Node.js and Bun runtimes" alert on the twelve pages that carry it, so the prose matches the platform keys; adding the key alone moves the wrong claim onto the Deno guide.
- On `knex.mdx` and `dataloader.mdx`, state that the integration is opt-in on Deno as on Node: it is importable from `@sentry/deno` but not in the default set.
- On `prisma.mdx`, state that Deno installs it by default but does not re-export it individually.

heading: ExtraErrorData page says the data lands in extra; it is written to contexts.<ErrorName>
title: Correct where ExtraErrorData writes on the integration page
body:
`docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/integrations/extraerrordata.mdx:3` and `:8` both describe the integration as one that "attaches them to the event as extra data". The page renders on the Bun, Deno and Cloudflare guides via `platform-includes/configuration/extra-error-data/javascript.{bun,deno,cloudflare}.mdx`, so readers on all three go looking for the values under Additional Data.

On develop the integration writes a context instead. `packages/core/src/integrations/extraerrordata.ts:70` sets `contexts[exceptionName] = normalizedErrorData` and returns `{ ...event, contexts }` at `:73-76`; `event.extra` is never touched. `exceptionName` is the error's `name`, falling back to its constructor name (`:55`), so the payload shows up as `contexts.<ErrorName>` in the issue view — the header reads `TypeError` for a `TypeError`, not `ExtraErrorData`. The line numbers are the same at the pin and on develop.

What to change:

- Reword the `description` frontmatter and the body sentence to say the properties are attached as a context named after the error.
- Name the location explicitly as `contexts.<ErrorName>`, note that the section header in the issue view carries the error name, and drop the "extra data" phrasing.

heading: rewrite-frames snippets for Bun, Deno and Cloudflare are TypeScript types inside a JavaScript call
title: Replace the invalid rewriteFrames options snippets with runnable code
body:
The rewrite-frames includes for all three runtimes show a call that cannot run. `platform-includes/configuration/rewrite-frames/javascript.bun.mdx:6-17`, `javascript.deno.mdx:6-17` and `javascript.cloudflare.mdx:6-17` pass `Sentry.rewriteFramesIntegration` an object literal whose members are TypeScript type annotations — `root: string;`, `prefix: string;`, `iteratee: (frame) => frame;` — inside a fence tagged ```javascript with `tabTitle: JavaScript`.

Copied as shown, this throws a SyntaxError in every runtime: `string` is an undefined identifier being used as a value, and the semicolons are not valid inside an object literal. The integration itself works and is exported everywhere the include renders — `packages/bun/src/index.ts:196` on develop (`:194` at the pin), `packages/deno/src/index.ts:79` and `packages/cloudflare/src/index.ts:82` — so only the snippet is at fault.

The Cloudflare snippet has a second problem: it wraps the options in a bare `Sentry.init({ ... })` at `:4`, which is not how `@sentry/cloudflare` is configured. That guide's entry points are `withSentry` for Workers and `sentryPagesPlugin` for Pages.

What to change:

- Rewrite the three snippets as a runnable call with concrete values, for example a real `root` path and `prefix` string.
- Move the per-option descriptions out of the object literal into an Options section.
- Put the Cloudflare example in a `withSentry` or `sentryPagesPlugin` options object instead of `Sentry.init`, and keep the `___SDK_PACKAGE___` import placeholder in the Deno snippet.

heading: Bun feature flag page offers only the generic integration; @sentry/bun exports five providers
title: Enable the provider feature flag pages for Bun
body:
`platform-includes/feature-flags/evaluation-tracking-index/javascript.bun.mdx:1` offers Bun readers only "the generic `featureFlagsIntegration`". The four provider pages each exclude Bun explicitly: `launchdarkly.mdx:7`, `openfeature.mdx:7`, `statsig.mdx:7` and `unleash.mdx:7` list `javascript.bun` under `notSupported`.

On develop `@sentry/bun` re-exports all of them. `packages/bun/src/index.ts:175-182` at the pin (`:177-184` on develop) exports `featureFlagsIntegration`, `launchDarklyIntegration`, `growthbookIntegration`, `buildLaunchDarklyFlagUsedHandler`, `openFeatureIntegration`, `OpenFeatureIntegrationHook`, `statsigIntegration` and `unleashIntegration` from `@sentry/node`. The Deno and Cloudflare exclusions are correct: Deno exports only `featureFlagsIntegration` (`packages/deno/src/index.ts:95`), Cloudflare that plus `growthbookIntegration` (`packages/cloudflare/src/index.ts:100-101`), both unchanged on develop.

Growthbook is a separate piece of work: it ships on Bun and Cloudflare but has no page anywhere under `docs/`, `platform-includes/` or `includes/`, so it needs a new page rather than a frontmatter edit.

What to change:

- Remove `javascript.bun` from the `notSupported` lists on the four provider pages.
- Link those pages from the Bun evaluation-tracking include.
- File the growthbook page separately, covering Bun and Cloudflare.

heading: waitUntil() section covers spans only; errors inside ctx.waitUntil() are never captured
title: Document that errors inside ctx.waitUntil() are not captured
body:
The Cloudflare guide's `waitUntil()` section at `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:376-424` is titled "Spans in `waitUntil()`" and covers span capture only: the static lifecycle snapshotting the transaction at `:382`, `traceLifecycle: "stream"` at `:384-386`, and `forceTransaction: true` at `:388`. Errors are never mentioned, and the sample at `:393-420` shows deferred work with no note about failure.

An error thrown or a promise rejected inside `ctx.waitUntil(promise)` is not captured. The SDK's `waitUntil` handling is flush and invocation bookkeeping: `packages/cloudflare/src/client.ts:285` hands the promise to the invocation's `waitUntil` and nothing else, and `captureException` has no occurrence in `packages/cloudflare/src/flush.ts`. There is no error-capture path on that plumbing, on either trace lifecycle.

The fix belongs in the app, so the page can show it: `ctx.waitUntil(work().catch((e) => Sentry.captureException(e)));`.

What to change:

- Add a sentence stating that errors thrown or rejected inside `ctx.waitUntil()` are not captured, on either trace lifecycle.
- Show the app-side fix, `ctx.waitUntil(work().catch((e) => Sentry.captureException(e)));`, next to the existing sample.
- Retitle the section so it does not read as complete `waitUntil` coverage.

heading: Workflows page never says step errors are captured only on the final retry attempt
title: Document Cloudflare Workflows step error capture on the final attempt
body:
`docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/workflows.mdx` is 56 lines and covers `trace_id` derivation from `instanceId` (`:11-15`), the sampling decision (`:17-23`) and a warning about creating spans outside `step.do()` (`:25-30`). It never says what happens to an error thrown inside a step, so a reader cannot tell whether a retried failure appears once or many times.

On develop, `packages/cloudflare/src/workflows.ts:152-153` (`:151-153` at the pin; `:150` is the `catch`) calls `captureException` only when `isFinalAttempt`, with `mechanism: { handled: true, type: 'auto.faas.cloudflare.workflow' }`, and then rethrows at `:154`, so the engine still sees the failure and retries. `isFinalAttempt` is computed at `:114-121` on develop (`:113-120` at the pin) as `!hasStepContext || attempt > retryLimit`: when the Workflows engine passes both `attempt` and `config.retries.limit`, only the attempt past the limit reports and intermediate retries send nothing; when no step context is supplied, every attempt is captured.

What to change:

- Add a section on step error capture to `workflows.mdx`.
- State that a failing `step.do()` reports once, on the final attempt, where the engine supplies `attempt` and `config.retries.limit`, and that every attempt reports where it does not.
- Name the mechanism `auto.faas.cloudflare.workflow` and say the error is rethrown, so retries and the workflow's own failure handling are unchanged.

heading: Release health and session APIs render on the Cloudflare guide; @sentry/cloudflare exports none of them
title: Gate the release health and session APIs away from the Cloudflare guide
body:
`docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/releases.mdx:30-43` markets Release Health and links to Session APIs, and `docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/apis.mdx:922-941` documents `startSession` (`:927`), `endSession` (`:931`) and `captureSession` (`:935-941`). Neither file has `supported` or `notSupported` frontmatter, and the Sessions block carries no `PlatformSection` gate, so both render on the Cloudflare guide as if `Sentry.startSession()` were available there.

It is not. `packages/cloudflare/src/index.ts` exports none of the three, so importing them from `@sentry/cloudflare` yields `undefined`. The same file does export the `Session` type at `:12`, so editor autocomplete suggests sessions exist while the functions do not. Bun (`packages/bun/src/index.ts:33-35`) and Deno (`packages/deno/src/index.ts:87-89`) export all three, which is why the pages read correctly on those guides.

Gating is the change to make. The Cloudflare client does inherit the session plumbing — `packages/cloudflare/src/client.ts:24` extends `ServerRuntimeClient`, and core implements `captureSession` at `packages/core/src/client.ts:399` and `sendSession` at `:596` — but no Workers run in the audit exercised those functions through `@sentry/core`, so the page should not send readers down that path on the strength of the source alone.

What to change:

- Gate the Sessions section in `apis.mdx` and the Release Health block in `releases.mdx:30-43` away from `javascript.cloudflare`.
- If the sections stay ungated, state plainly on the Cloudflare rendering that `@sentry/cloudflare` exports none of `startSession`, `endSession` and `captureSession`.
- Say that the exported `Session` is a type only, so its presence in autocomplete does not mean the APIs are there.

heading: The verify step of all four guides is written around the transaction envelope that v11 stops sending
title: Rewrite the tracing verify step for the stream lifecycle on the Node, Bun, Deno and Cloudflare guides
body:
The tracing verify step tells the reader to wrap work in `Sentry.startSpan({ op: "test", name: "My First Test Transaction" })`: `platform-includes/getting-started-verify/javascript.node.mdx:38-53`, `guides/bun/index.mdx:156-172`, `guides/deno/index.mdx:176-190` and `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:313-335`. The sentence that follows each one sends the reader to Sentry "to view the collected data" (`getting-started-node/javascript.mdx:120`, `bun/index.mdx:188`, `deno/index.mdx:207`, `cloudflare/index.mdx:364`) and expands the `quick-start-locate-data-expandable` include, which points at the Traces page. The only place the word "Transaction" appears is the sample name inside the snippet.

Observed on `develop`, on all four runtimes with the documented wiring: no `transaction` envelope is sent at all. The manual span arrives as a child item inside a `span` envelope together with the server span, for example `["http.client GET 127.0.0.1", "test My First Test Span", "http.server GET"]`, because `packages/core/src/client.ts:243` normalizes any `traceLifecycle` other than `'static'` to `'stream'`. On the released line there is no such normalization, so `'static'` is the default and a transaction is sent: the pages are correct for the version they serve today and become wrong with v11.

What to change, in the v11 docs update:

- On each of the four verify steps, describe what arrives: a trace with a server segment span and the manual span as its child, no transaction.
- Rename the sample from "My First Test Transaction" to a span name.
- Link the stream lifecycle page, and note that `traceLifecycle: "static"` restores the transaction envelope for readers who look for it.
- Fix the ten `platform-includes/performance/enable-stream-mode/javascript.*.mdx` files whose closing line calls `traceLifecycle` `'static'` "(the default)": node `:36`, cloudflare `:62`, hono `:51`, deno `:24`, and bun, nextjs, nestjs, nitro, gcp-functions and elysia at `:25`.
- Rewrite `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:382-388`, which frames the static lifecycle as the current model and stream as the opt-in.
- Apply the same rewrite to the framework verify includes: `platform-includes/getting-started-verify/javascript.express.mdx:30` and `:40` name "My First Test Transaction", and the Express run received the span as an `op: test` child of the `http.server` segment inside a span envelope, never a transaction envelope (QS-express, variants import and express5); `getting-started-verify/javascript.fastify.mdx:24-30` and `:40` and `guides/fastify/tracing/instrumentation/automatic-instrumentation.mdx:3` say the same and the Fastify run saw the same (QS-fastify, every variant); `getting-started-verify/javascript.koa.mdx:29` and `:35-46` and `guides/koa/tracing/instrumentation/automatic-instrumentation.mdx:3` likewise (QS-koa, every variant), as do `getting-started-verify/javascript.hapi.mdx:34` and `:47` and `guides/hapi/tracing/instrumentation/automatic-instrumentation.mdx:3` (QS-hapi, every variant), and `getting-started-verify/javascript.connect.mdx:30` and `:36-47`, `guides/connect/tracing/instrumentation/automatic-instrumentation.mdx:3` and `includes/node-automatic-instrumentation.mdx:1-3` (QS-connect, every variant that starts), and `getting-started-verify/javascript.hono.mdx:30` plus the `getting-started-config/javascript.hono.mdx:21` and `:57` comment about 100% of transactions (QS-hono, every variant); the Hono guide page itself already says spans at `guides/hono/index.mdx:184`; the NestJS verify include is covered by DOC-Q57; the Google Cloud Functions config include says 100% of transactions at `platform-includes/getting-started-config/javascript.gcp-functions.mdx:19` and its `tracing/instrumentation/automatic-instrumentation.mdx:3` explains transactions, while the invocation arrives as a `function.gcp` segment with the test span as its child (QS-gcp-functions, variant http-tracing).

heading: The Cloudflare Vite plugin instruments nothing, without warning, when it resolves a different default-named wrangler config
title: Say on the Vite plugin page that a wrangler config resolved to the wrong file instruments nothing
body:
`guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin.mdx` documents the probing order at `:68` and gives `wranglerConfigPath` its own option entry at `:130-148`, described as the setting for a config at a custom path. What no page says is what happens when the config is not at a custom path but simply not the one the reader means: with several wrangler files in the project, the plugin resolves the first default-named `wrangler.json`, `wrangler.jsonc` or `wrangler.toml` at the Vite root, reads the entry point and classes from that file, and instruments nothing for the Worker actually being built. Nothing is logged, because the plugin only warns when no config parses at all.

Observed on `develop` with a Worker whose source has no `withSentry` call, built in a directory holding more than one wrangler config: before `wranglerConfigPath` was passed, the run produced an empty sink, an uncaught error in the worker log and no trace-propagation headers. With `wranglerConfigPath` set and an `instrument.server.ts` next to the wrangler `main`, the built Worker delivered the same errors, spans, headers and logs as a hand-written `withSentry`, with no experimental flag.

What to change:

- On the Vite plugin page, state that `wranglerConfigPath` is required whenever the project holds more than one wrangler config, not only when the config sits at a custom path, and that a config resolved to the wrong file instruments nothing while the build still succeeds.
- Say how to tell: with auto-instrumentation working, the built entry contains a `withSentry` wrapper; without it there is no wrapper and no plugin output.
- Remove the `_experimental.useDiagnosticsChannelInjection` flag from `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:77-92`; it is not needed on `develop` (also DOC-C4).

heading: Without a framework, server spans are named by method or URL on every runtime, and no guide says where a route name comes from
title: State on the four guides that route names need a framework integration or a routes map
body:
The four guides end their verify step without saying anything about how server spans are named: `getting-started-node/javascript.mdx:120`, `guides/bun/index.mdx:188`, `guides/deno/index.mdx:207`, `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:364` each send the reader to Sentry "to view the collected data" and expand an include that points at the Traces page. Nothing on the way there says where a route name comes from, so a reader who sees `GET` has no page to check.

Observed on `develop` with the base setup: a plain `node:http` server on Node names every segment span `GET` and sets no `sentry.source`; `Deno.serve` names every span `GET` with source `url`, a `URLPattern` route included; `withSentry` on Workers names every span `GET` with source `url`; only `Bun.serve` with a `routes` map produces `GET /users/:id` with source `route`, and falls back to `GET` for an unrouted path. On Bun and Cloudflare the error event carries no `transaction` field, so an issue shows no route either; on Node the same event does carry `transaction: "GET /debug-sentry"`. Route names appear once a framework integration is in place, as the framework matrix records.

What to change, in the v11 docs update:

- On each guide, state that the base setup names server spans by method (or URL under the static lifecycle) and that route names come from a framework integration, or on Bun from the `Bun.serve` routes map.
- Link the framework pages for the runtime from that sentence.
- On the Bun and Cloudflare guides, drop the claim that issues are grouped by transaction until the SDK sets the field. The Node guide can keep it: the Node error event does carry the transaction name.

heading: The browser CDN tab names the tracing bundle while its snippet adds replayIntegration()
title: Match the CDN bundle named on the browser config page to the integrations its snippet uses
body:
`platform-includes/getting-started-config/javascript.mdx:116` names `bundle.tracing.min.js` in the CDN tab, and the same snippet adds `Sentry.replayIntegration()` at `:130` and `:133`.

Observed with that combination on the develop CDN build: the console shows `warning: You are using replayIntegration() even though this bundle does not include replay.`, `Replay` still appears in the installed integrations, no event carries a `replayId` tag, and no replay envelope is ever sent. With `bundle.tracing.replay.min.js` the same page records the replay.

What to change:

- Name `bundle.tracing.replay.min.js` in the CDN tab, or remove `replayIntegration()` and the replay sample rates from the CDN variant of the snippet.
- State that a bundle without replay turns `replayIntegration()` into a no-op with a console warning only.

heading: Sentry.logger is a silent no-op on the CDN bundles, and no page says which bundle carries logs
title: State on the logs pages which browser CDN bundles include Sentry.logger
body:
The logs quick start (`includes/logs/javascript-quick-start-verify-logs-splitlayout.mdx:13`) tells every browser reader to call `Sentry.logger.info(...)`; the CDN install tab of the browser guide names `bundle.tracing.min.js`. Neither says that the CDN bundles ship a stub logger.

Observed on develop: with the npm package and the CommonJS build the log item arrives. With `bundle.tracing.min.js` and with `bundle.tracing.replay.min.js` no log envelope is produced and nothing warns; in the bundle `Sentry.logger` and `Sentry.metrics` are objects whose methods are empty functions. The v10-to-v11 page mentions the metrics half only (`common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:1398`).

What to change:

- On the logs pages that render for the browser, say that `Sentry.logger` is a no-op on the CDN bundles that do not include logs, and name the bundle that does.
- Add the same sentence next to the CDN tab of the browser config page.

heading: On React 19 the reactErrorHandler root hooks silence the ErrorBoundary features the page describes
title: Say on the React error boundary page how reactErrorHandler and ErrorBoundary interact on React 19
body:
`guides/react/features/error-boundary.mdx:21-53` shows a React 19 root with `onCaughtError: Sentry.reactErrorHandler()` next to `Sentry.ErrorBoundary`, then documents `beforeCapture` tags (`:151`) and `captureReactException` with the linked component stack (`:173`).

Observed with the page's own `main.jsx`: every boundary error is captured first by the root hook (mechanism `auto.function.react.error_handler`, `handled: false`), and the boundary's own capture, the `beforeCapture` tags and `captureReactException` are dropped by the dedupe integration, five times `Not capturing exception because it's already been captured`. On a plain `createRoot` without the hooks the boundary path works as described: `auto.function.react.error_boundary`, `handled: true`, `tags.section` set, component stack linked.

Related, on the guide itself: `guides/react/index.mdx:163-167` passes a callback to `onUncaughtError: Sentry.reactErrorHandler((error, errorInfo) => {...})`; the render error that unmounted the whole root then arrives with `handled: true`, because passing a callback marks the error as handled, while the callback-less `onCaughtError` hook reports boundary-caught errors as `handled: false`.

What to change:

- State that with `onCaughtError` set, the ErrorBoundary's `beforeCapture` and `captureReactException` never run, and tell readers who rely on them to leave `onCaughtError` out or to tag inside its callback.
- Say what the `handled` flag means for each hook, and drop the `console.warn` callback from the `onUncaughtError` snippet or explain its effect.

heading: The data-collection include claims a built-in password denylist that does not cover Redux or Pinia state
title: Scope the built-in denylist claim on the data-collection include to request data
body:
`platform-includes/getting-started-data-collection/javascript.mdx:8` says the SDK always filters sensitive values whose keys match a built-in denylist, such as `auth` or `password`, and sends `[Filtered]` instead.

Observed after the Redux step of the React guide (`includes/platforms/configuration/integrations/redux.mdx:39-113`, `platform-includes/configuration/redux-init/javascript.mdx:1-21`): `contexts.state.state.value.password`, the `redux_state.json` attachment and the `redux.action` breadcrumb data all carry `password: "hunter2"` in clear on every error event. The denylist applies to the request-data categories that `dataCollection` covers, not to state the app attaches.

The Vue Pinia page has the same gap: `guides/vue/features/pinia.mdx:34` says the SDK tries its best to filter out PII such as user passwords, and with `createSentryPiniaPlugin()` the password arrived in clear in `contexts.state` (type `pinia`) and in the `pinia_state_all_stores_*.json` attachment on every event (QS-vue, variant pinia).

What to change:

- Scope the sentence to the request data the `dataCollection` categories cover.
- On the Redux page, point at `stateTransformer` and `actionTransformer` for secrets in state; on the Pinia page drop the password sentence and point at `stateTransformer`.

heading: The React component monitoring page names Profiler span ops that the SDK no longer emits
title: Rename the Profiler span ops on the React component monitoring page
body:
`guides/react/features/component-monitoring.mdx:34-46` and `:66-72` say the Profiler generates spans with the ops `ui.react.mount`, `ui.react.render` and `ui.react.update`, attached to the current active transaction.

Observed with `withProfiler(App)`: spans named `<App>` arrive with the ops `ui.mount`, `ui.update` and `ui.render` (attribute `ui.component_name: App`, origin `auto.ui.react.profiler`), as children of the pageload segment span. The v10-to-v11 page records the rename at `common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:454`; this page does not.

What to change:

- Rename the three ops on the page, and say the spans attach to the active root span rather than a transaction.

heading: The Vue component tracking page states the wrong default hooks and the wrong span ops
title: Correct the Vue component tracking page: default hooks, span ops and the duplicate-key snippet
body:
`guides/vue/features/component-tracking.mdx:71` says the default set of tracked hooks is `['activate', 'mount', 'update']`. The develop build's `DEFAULT_HOOKS` is `['activate', 'mount']` (`build/esm/constants.js`); two prop updates produced no `ui.update` span until `hooks` was passed, and `hooks` is additive, `mount` cannot be turned off.

`:19-23` names the ops `ui.vue.render` and `ui.vue.[hook]`. Observed: `ui.render` named `Application Render`, and `ui.mount`, `ui.update`, `ui.unmount` named `Vue <Name>` plus `Vue <Root>`. Only the v10-to-v11 page (`common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:454`) records the rename.

`:28-48` puts `trackComponents: true` and the component-name array in one object literal as an "or"; as printed the array wins, esbuild warns `Duplicate key trackComponents`, and the untracked component gets no span.

What to change:

- State the default as `['activate', 'mount']` and say `hooks` adds to it.
- Rename the ops and add the span names.
- Split the boolean and the array form into two snippets.

heading: The Express and Connect tracing verify snippets hang on Express 4 and Connect 3
title: Make the async tracing verify snippets work on Express 4 and Connect 3, or state what they need
body:
`platform-includes/getting-started-verify/javascript.express.mdx:36-47` replaces the `/debug-sentry` route with an `async` handler that throws inside `Sentry.startSpan`. On express 4.22.2 the request never gets a response (the client timed out, status 000) and the error arrives as `auto.node.onunhandledrejection`, not through the Express error path; the request segment reports status `ok` with `http.response.status_code: 200` although nothing was sent. On express 5.2.1 the same snippet answers 500 and the error is captured as `auto.http.express`. The guide names no Express major; the registry's `express` is 5. The Connect include `getting-started-verify/javascript.connect.mdx:36-47` has the same shape and the same result on connect 3.7.0: no response, the error as `auto.node.onunhandledrejection`, and the segment closed with status `ok` when the client gave up (QS-connect, variant no-handler).

What to change:

- Say that the async snippet needs Express 5, or add a `try/catch` that calls `next(err)` so it works on Express 4 and on Connect as well.

heading: The esm-without-import page says a first-line import cannot instrument frameworks; Express, Fastify, Hapi and Hono are fully instrumented that way
title: Correct the first-line import limitation on the esm-without-import page for v11
body:
`common/install/esm-without-import.mdx:28-30` says that with a direct first-line import only native Node.js APIs can be instrumented and the SDK will not capture framework-specific data. Observed on develop: `import "./instrument.mjs"` as the first line of the Express app produced exactly the `--import` output, with middleware and handler spans, route-named segments (`GET /users/:id`, source `route`) and `auto.http.express` error events; the Node run's Express check saw the same, and the Fastify run got the same hook and handler spans and `auto.function.fastify` events from a first-line import (QS-fastify, variant self-import). Koa is the counter-example: its first-line import produced url-named `GET` segments and no router or middleware span (QS-koa, variant self-import), so the page should name what is covered and what is not instead of a blanket warning. Hapi behaves like Fastify: the first-line import produced the same items as `--import`, every Hapi span, route name and error (QS-hapi, variant self-import). Hono too: `sentry(app)` patches the app instance at registration time, and the first-line import produced the same route-named segments, middleware spans and errors as `--import` (QS-hono, variant self-import).

What to change:

- Replace the blanket warning with what is affected on v11 (packages imported before the instrument file), and say that Express, Fastify, Hapi and Hono are covered while Koa is not; the NestJS copy of the page, `guides/nestjs/install/esm-without-import.mdx:18-20`, needs the same qualification, since the guide's default CommonJS build gets full Nest and Express spans from a first-line import (QS-nestjs, variant cjs).

heading: The Angular custom error handler page never shows how to register the subclass, and the obvious way does not bootstrap
title: Show a working provider for a subclassed SentryErrorHandler on the Angular error handler page
body:
`guides/angular/features/error-handler.mdx:62-82` says to extend Sentry's `ErrorHandler` as in the example and shows no registration. Registered as `{ provide: ErrorHandler, useClass: CustomErrorHandler }`, the app never bootstraps: `NG0201` in production, and in development `DEPRECATED: DI is instantiating a token "CustomErrorHandler" that inherits its @Injectable decorator but does not provide one itself` followed by `NG0402`, because the inherited factory injects the unprovided `errorHandlerOptions` token. `{ provide: ErrorHandler, useValue: new CustomErrorHandler() }` boots and reports errors through the subclass.

What to change:

- Show the provider as `useValue: new CustomErrorHandler()` (or a factory that passes the options), and say why `useClass` fails.

heading: The Angular component tracking page names span ops the SDK no longer emits
title: Rename the component tracking span ops on the Angular page
body:
`guides/angular/features/component-tracking.mdx:18` and `:56` say the trace directive and `TraceClass` add spans called `ui.angular.init`; `:78` says `TraceMethod` spans are called `ui.angular.[methodname]`. Observed: op `ui.mount` named `<header>`, `<Header>` or `<unnamed>` (origins `auto.ui.angular.trace_directive` and `auto.ui.angular.trace_class_decorator`), and op `function` named `<Login.ngOnChanges>` with `code.function.name: ngOnChanges` for the method decorator, all under the pageload segment. Only `common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:455` records the rename.

What to change:

- Rename the ops to `ui.mount` and `function`, and state the `<name>` span naming and the `code.function.name` attribute.

heading: The Fastify error handler page documents an options object that develop silently ignores
title: Move shouldHandleError to fastifyIntegration on the Fastify error handler page
body:
`guides/fastify/features/error-handler.mdx:29-48` passes `{ shouldHandleError(error, request, reply) }` to `setupFastifyErrorHandler(app, ...)`. On develop the function is a deprecated one-parameter no-op: the options object is ignored, the callback never ran and `/error-404` stayed uncaptured. `fastifyIntegration({ shouldHandleError })` works, ran the callback four times with the final status codes on Fastify 5, and captured the 404.

What to change:

- Document `shouldHandleError` on `fastifyIntegration({ ... })` and mark `setupFastifyErrorHandler(app)` as a deprecated no-op.

heading: The Fastify integration page's supported versions exclude Fastify 5 and include 3.0
title: Correct the supported Fastify versions on the integration page
body:
`common/configuration/integrations/fastify.mdx:31` says `fastify ^3.0.0 || ^4.0.0`. Fastify 5.12.3 is fully instrumented on develop (route-named segments, handler and middleware spans, `auto.function.fastify` error capture), the built types say the integration supports `>= 3.21.0 < 6`, and `common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:112` drops Fastify 3.0 through 3.20.

What to change:

- Change the range to `^3.21.0 || ^4.0.0 || ^5.0.0`.

heading: The Svelte component tracking page names old span ops, the wrong trackUpdates default, and no Svelte 5 runes caveat
title: Correct the Svelte component tracking page: span ops, the trackUpdates default and the runes-mode limit
body:
`guides/svelte/features/component-tracking.mdx:68` and `:72` call the spans `ui.svelte.init` and `ui.svelte.update`; the build sends `ui.mount` and `ui.update`, named `<Navbar>`, `<MyAwesomeComponent>` and so on, with origin `auto.ui.svelte`.

`:55-57` and `:87-89` say `trackUpdates` is optional and defaults to `true`; the shipped default is `false` in both `withSentryConfig` and `trackComponent`, and `withSentryConfig(config)` produced mount spans only, no update span after re-renders.

`:72-74` describe update spans over the `beforeUpdate` to `afterUpdate` cycle. On Svelte 5 a runes-mode component (`$props`) records no update span even with `trackUpdates: true`: the lifecycle hooks throw, the SDK swallows it and warns `Cannot track component updates ... Svelte 5 in Runes mode` only with `debug: true`; update spans arrived for the legacy-mode component only, and only while a span was active.

What to change:

- Rename the ops to `ui.mount` and `ui.update` and add the `<ComponentName>` span name.
- State that `trackUpdates` defaults to `false`.
- Say that on Svelte 5 update spans need legacy-mode components and that runes-mode components are skipped with a debug warning.

heading: The migration page says setupKoaErrorHandler is no longer needed; with a direct import it still is
title: Qualify the Koa error handler claims on the migration and esm-without-import pages
body:
`common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:715-719` says Koa errors are captured by the integration now, so `setupKoaErrorHandler(app)` is no longer needed. True with `--import`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `--require` and a CommonJS `require`: five events with `auto.middleware.koa` and no handler call, with and without tracing. With the direct first-line import that `common/install/esm-without-import.mdx:53-63` documents, the orchestrion callback channel never fires and without the call no Koa error reaches Sentry at all: only the sentinel arrived and Koa logged the errors to stderr. That page says only that framework spans are lost.

What to change:

- Say on both pages that with a direct first-line import Koa error capture still requires `Sentry.setupKoaErrorHandler(app)`, next to the span loss.

heading: The Koa integration page names the wrong mechanism, the wrong enablement rule and the wrong version range
title: Rewrite the Koa integration page around the diagnostics-channel instrumentation
body:
`common/configuration/integrations/koa.mdx:21` says the integration captures spans using `@opentelemetry/instrumentation-koa`. That package is not installed (not a dependency of `@sentry/node` or `@sentry/server-utils`); every Koa span has origin `auto.http.koa` from the SDK's own `orchestrion:koa:use` channel, which needs the SDK loaded before `koa` through `--import`, `NODE_OPTIONS` or `require`. A first-line ESM import yields url-named `GET` segments and no router or middleware span.

`:19` says the integration is enabled when performance monitoring is enabled; with no `tracesSampleRate` it is still installed (23 default integrations include Koa) and its auto-registered error listener captured all five errors. `:54` lists `koa ^2.0.0`; koa 3.2.1 is fully instrumented and the build's range is `>=2.0.0 <4`. `:29-50` show `ignoreLayersType` as the only option, and there is no status filter: `ctx.throw(404, ...)` and `ctx.throw(503, ...)` both arrive as unhandled events, while Express and Fastify have `shouldHandleError`.

What to change:

- Describe the diagnostics-channel mechanism and its loading requirement, say the integration is always on and creates spans only with tracing, list `koa ^2.0.0 || ^3.0.0`, and say that every error Koa emits is reported, with `ignoreErrors` or `beforeSend` as the filter.

heading: The Hapi integration page names the wrong mechanism, the wrong enablement rule and no option, and its table row says it captures no errors
title: Rewrite the Hapi integration page and its table row
body:
`common/configuration/integrations/hapi.mdx:21` says the integration captures spans using `@opentelemetry/instrumentation-hapi`; that package is not installed, and every span has origin `auto.http.hapi` from the SDK's own diagnostics-channel instrumentation of `@hapi/hapi/lib/server.js`. `:19-27` say the integration is enabled when performance monitoring is enabled and show no option; with no `tracesSampleRate` it is still installed and captured the same four errors (`auto.function.hapi`), and `hapiIntegration({ shouldHandleError(error, request) })` exists and is invoked, which neither this page nor `common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:722` (Express and Fastify only) documents. The integrations table include `platform-includes/configuration/integrations/javascript.hapi.mdx:12` leaves the Errors column empty for `hapiIntegration`, although it is what captures Hapi errors on develop.

One limit the page should state: Hapi emits its request error channel only for 500 responses (`@hapi/hapi/lib/request.js:511-515`), so `Boom.notFound` and `Boom.serverUnavailable` thrown from handlers never reach Sentry even with `shouldHandleError: () => true`; plain throws and `Boom.badImplementation` are captured.

What to change:

- Describe the diagnostics-channel mechanism, say the integration is always on and captures errors with or without tracing, add the `shouldHandleError` option and the 500-only limit, tick the Errors column in the table row, and list `hapiIntegration` at migration `:722`.

heading: The Solid guide's DEV guard skips init under vite dev, so its verify step sends nothing
title: Say on the Solid guide that the verify step needs a production build because of the DEV guard
body:
`guides/solid/index.mdx:79-80` wraps `Sentry.init` in `if (!DEV)`, and the verify step at `:173-179` and `:207-210` tells the reader to open the page and click the button. Under the development export condition (a Vite dev server) `DEV` is truthy, `Sentry.init` never runs, `getClient()` is undefined and the clicks send nothing; the boundary fallback renders without capture. A production build sends both verify errors, the boundary error, logs, replay and the trace.

What to change:

- Say in the verify step that the guard means a production build (`vite build` plus `vite preview`) is needed, or drop the guard for the verify step.

heading: The Solid guide's tracing setup produces no navigation spans without withSentryRouterRouting
title: Add withSentryRouterRouting to the Solid guide's tracing snippet
body:
`guides/solid/index.mdx:76` and `:89` add `solidRouterBrowserTracingIntegration()` and present that as the tracing setup. The integration forces `instrumentNavigation: false` and creates navigation spans only through `withSentryRouterRouting`, which the guide never mentions: around a plain `<Router>` two route changes produced zero navigation spans and both pageloads were named `Pageload` with source `url`; with the wrapped Router (`features/solid-router.mdx:20-45`) the pageload is `/router/users/:id` with source `route` and navigations carry `params.id`.

What to change:

- Add the `withSentryRouterRouting(Router)` line next to the integration in the init snippet, or link the Solid Router feature page there.

heading: The Connect verify route never reaches Sentry: v11 captures no Connect errors automatically
title: Say on the Connect guide that errors need an error-handling middleware, and show it
body:
`platform-includes/getting-started-verify/javascript.connect.mdx:7` and `:13-15` say that `app.use("/debug-sentry", (req, res) => { throw new Error(...) })` creates an issue. On the app that starts (the handler line removed, DOC-Q52), the request answers 500 from Connect's `finalhandler`, Connect prints the stack, and no event reaches Sentry in any variant, with or without tracing; thrown and `next(err)` errors (404, 503, 500) are all swallowed. The guide also renders no capture-errors step, because `getting-started-capture-errors` has no Connect include (DOC-Q31). The only Connect error that arrived was the unhandled rejection of the async tracing snippet (DOC-Q27).

What to change:

- Add an error-handling middleware `(err, req, res, next)` that calls `Sentry.captureException(err)` before `next(err)` as the prerequisite of the verify route, and state that v11 captures no Connect errors on its own.

heading: The Hono tracing verify snippet uses Sentry without importing it, and the package root exports nothing
title: Add the runtime import to the Hono tracing verify snippet
body:
`platform-includes/getting-started-verify/javascript.hono.mdx:36-47` tells the reader to call `Sentry.startSpan` in the `/debug-sentry` route. No Hono snippet imports `Sentry` into the app file: `guides/hono/index.mdx:264-267` imports only `{ sentry }`, and `:71` says `@sentry/node` is not imported directly. Pasted verbatim the route throws `ReferenceError: Sentry is not defined`, captured as the error, with no test span. `import * as Sentry from "@sentry/hono"` does not help: the package root exports nothing, and the route throws `TypeError: Sentry.startSpan is not a function`. With `import * as Sentry from "@sentry/hono/node"` the snippet works.

What to change:

- Add the per-runtime import (`@sentry/hono/node`, `/cloudflare`, `/bun`, `/deno`) to the tracing verify snippet, and say that the package root exports nothing.

heading: The install pages' Hono config snippets initialize from @sentry/node, which the guide forbids
title: Point the Hono config snippets on the CommonJS, ESM and ESM-without-import pages at @sentry/hono/node
body:
`guides/hono/index.mdx:168` says to import from `@sentry/hono/node`, not `@sentry/node`. The install pages render the opposite: `platform-includes/getting-started-config/javascript.hono.mdx:2` and `:38` (through `common/install/commonjs.mdx:25`), `common/install/esm.mdx:25` and `common/install/esm-without-import.mdx:39` initialize from `@sentry/node`. Following them, the build prints `[Sentry] Sentry was not initialized with @sentry/hono/node` and tags every event and span `sentry.javascript.node` instead of `sentry.javascript.hono`; the data itself arrives. With `@sentry/hono/node` the warning disappears and the SDK name is right.

What to change:

- Point the four Hono config snippets at `@sentry/hono/node`.

heading: No NestJS error reaches Sentry until SentryGlobalFilter is added, and the guide says the opposite
title: Say on the NestJS guide that SentryGlobalFilter is required for any HTTP error to be captured, and move it before Verify
body:
`platform-includes/getting-started-capture-errors/javascript.nestjs.mdx:1` says Sentry captures by default the unhandled exceptions that no error filter catches. With the guide's setup up to `guides/nestjs/index.mdx:102-117` (`SentryModule.forRoot()`, no filter) the unhandled controller error produced no event: Nest's built-in exception handler catches everything, and nothing reaches Sentry until `SentryGlobalFilter` or `@SentryExceptionCaptured()` is added. `:2` says HttpExceptions are not captured by default; that holds for 404, 503 and a bare `HttpException` with status 500 alike, the filter has no status threshold and no option, and `shouldHandleError` exists only for Express and Fastify.

What to change:

- State that Nest's default exception handler swallows every error, so the filter or the decorator is required for any HTTP error, move that step before Verify, and say that 5xx HttpExceptions are included with no option to change it.

heading: The Nest integration page names the wrong mechanism, the wrong enablement rule and Nest.js 4 as supported
title: Rewrite the Nest integration page around the diagnostics-channel instrumentation
body:
`common/configuration/integrations/nest.mdx:19-21` says the integration is enabled with performance monitoring and captures spans using `@opentelemetry/instrumentation-nestjs-core`. That package is not installed (only `@opentelemetry/api` is); the Nest integration is installed with and without tracing (24 of 24 integrations in the errors-only run), and every Nest span comes from the SDK's own diagnostics-channel instrumentation (`auto.http.nestjs`, `auto.middleware.nestjs`). `:31` says Nest.js 4.0.0 or later is supported; the build injects into `@nestjs/core` 8 through 12 and the package peer range starts at 8.

What to change:

- Describe the built-in instrumentation of `@nestjs/core`, `@nestjs/common`, `@nestjs/schedule`, `@nestjs/event-emitter` and `@nestjs/bullmq`, say it is always installed, and list Nest.js 8 through 12.

heading: The Node prerequisites include says Node 18 while the v11 packages declare a higher engines range
title: Update the Node prerequisite include to the engines range the v11 packages declare
body:
`platform-includes/getting-started-prerequisites/javascript.node.mdx:7`, rendered by every Node guide, says Node version 18.0.0 or above. `@sentry/nestjs` 10.67.0 declares `engines.node` as `>=20.19.0 <22.0.0 || >=22.12.0 <23.0.0 || >=23.2.0`; Node 18 was not run in any quick start. `@sentry/elysia`, `@sentry/bun` and `@sentry/node` declare the same range, and `guides/elysia/index.mdx:25` says Bun or Node.js 18+ (QS-elysia). `@sentry/nitro` declares it too, and `guides/nitro/index.mdx:24` says Node.js 18.19.0+ (QS-nitro). Check the remaining server packages before rewording.

What to change:

- State the engines range the packages declare, or the lowest supported line, instead of 18.0.0.

heading: The WebAssembly guide promises debug IDs and images that need a build_id section and a streaming loader it never mentions
title: Say on the WebAssembly guide what the integration needs: a build_id section, a URL-keeping loader and uploaded debug files
body:
`guides/wasm/index.mdx:65` says the integration provides Debug IDs, Debug Files, Code IDs, Code Files and memory addresses. With a module that has no `build_id` custom section (nothing in the guide's install or Rust steps adds one; `wasm-split` does) the event carries only `instruction_addr` and `platform: native` on the wasm frame, no `addr_mode` and no `debug_meta`: the registry skips modules without `build_id`. With the section present the full set arrives (`addr_mode: rel:0`, a `debug_meta.images` entry of type `wasm` with code_id, code_file, debug_file and debug_id). The page never mentions `wasm-split`, `build_id`, DWARF or the debug file upload.

Loading also matters and the page (`:160`, `:176-179`) is silent on it: a module loaded with `WebAssembly.instantiate(bytes)` after `fetch().arrayBuffer()` is named `wasm://wasm/<hash>` by Chrome, so even with `build_id` no image matches and no `addr_mode` or `debug_meta` is attached; `instantiateStreaming` and `compileStreaming` keep the URL and match.

What to change:

- State at `:65` that the module must carry a `build_id` section (`wasm-split`) and that the DWARF debug file has to be uploaded, link the debug files docs, and add that symbolication needs a loader that keeps the module URL.

heading: The Elysia verify route is added after listen() and is never served on Node
title: Chain the Elysia verify route before .listen() on the guide
body:
`guides/elysia/index.mdx:177-184` says to add the `/debug-sentry` route to the app, after a config snippet (`:124-126`) that ends in `.listen(3000)`. Under `@elysiajs/node` a route added after `.listen()` answers 404: `My first Sentry error!` is never thrown, and the only event is `Error: NOT_FOUND`, which looks like success. Chained before `.listen()` the route creates the issue (`auto.http.elysia.on_error`, transaction `GET /debug-sentry`, request data).

What to change:

- Show the verify route chained before `.listen()`, or say that routes must be defined before `listen`, and drop the "add the following route" framing.

heading: The Elysia guide says client errors are not captured by default; unmatched routes and status() throws are
title: Correct the default error filter description on the Elysia guide
body:
`guides/elysia/index.mdx:139` says client errors (3xx and 4xx) are not captured by default. The default filter reads `context.set.status`, which is 200 for Elysia's `NotFoundError` (an unmatched route, 404 to the client) and 500 for anything thrown through `status(4xx, ...)`: both are captured, `Error: NOT_FOUND` once per process because Elysia reuses one instance, and a `status()` throw as `'ElysiaCustomStatusResponse' captured as exception with keys: code, response`. Only `set.status = 4xx` before a throw is skipped. The guide's own `shouldHandleError` snippet (`:146-151`) suppresses them.

What to change:

- State that unmatched routes and `status()`-thrown responses are captured by default, that `status()` throws arrive as non-Error objects, and point at `shouldHandleError` as the filter.

heading: The Mastra guide documents only the community exporter, and combining it with the SDK's built-in integration duplicates every span
title: Document the built-in mastraIntegration route on the Mastra pages and say the exporter must not be combined with it
body:
`guides/mastra/index.mdx:17-19`, `:47` and `:85-91` and `common/agent-tracing/mastra.mdx:55` present `@mastra/sentry` as the way to send Mastra data to Sentry, and tell apps that already call `Sentry.init` to confirm that the two setups are compatible. On develop `@sentry/node` ships a default `mastraIntegration` (Mastra is among the 46 installed integrations) that instruments `@mastra/core` on its own under `--import`: `gen_ai.invoke_agent`, `gen_ai.chat` and `gen_ai.execute_tool` spans with token usage, no exporter needed. With both present the SDK prints `Remove @mastra/sentry from your Mastra exporters`, installs every integration twice (92), replaces the app client with the exporter's, and duplicates every gen_ai span. The exporter also pins the `@sentry/node` version (`@mastra/sentry` 1.2.16 requires `^10.68.0`), which neither page says.

What to change:

- Document the built-in route (`Sentry.init` plus `--import`, no `@mastra/sentry`) for apps that already initialize Sentry, state that the exporter and the integration must not be combined, and say that `@mastra/sentry` decides the `@sentry/node` version.

heading: The AWS Lambda ESM tab creates instrument.mjs and the load step points at instrument.js
title: Give the AWS Lambda load step the file name its ESM tab creates
body:
`guides/aws-lambda/install/npm.mdx:125` (and `install/layer.mdx:88`) creates `instrument.mjs` in the ESM tab, and the load step at `npm.mdx:161` (`layer.mdx:111`) says `NODE_OPTIONS="--import ./instrument.js"`. With only `instrument.mjs` present the preload fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and the function never starts; `--import ./instrument.mjs` works.

What to change:

- Give the load step CommonJS and ESM tabs with `--import ./instrument.js` and `--import ./instrument.mjs`.

heading: The Lambda wrapper page documents options that the v11 automatic wrapping overrides
title: Say on the Lambda wrapper page that v11 wraps the handler automatically with default options
body:
`guides/aws-lambda/configuration/lambda-wrapper.mdx:13-37` says timeout warnings, `flushTimeout` and `timeoutWarningLimit` are set through the `wrapHandler` options. On develop `awsLambdaIntegration` rewrites `_HANDLER` to a shim that wraps the exported handler with default options: with `captureTimeoutWarning: false` on the user's `wrapHandler` a `Possible function timeout` warning event still arrived. `wrapHandler` in user code is redundant for both install options and only changes the mechanism to `auto.function.aws_serverless.handler`; on its own, without the runtime redirect, it yields an error event but no span.

What to change:

- State that the automatic instrumentation applies default wrapper options, and document how to opt out of `awsLambdaIntegration` so the `wrapHandler` options take effect.

heading: The Effect verify step promises an issue for a failed effect, and nothing captures it
title: Show the capture a failed effect needs on the Effect guide
body:
`guides/effect/index.mdx:280` and `:289-293` say that adding `yield* Effect.fail(new Error("Sentry Test Error"))` and running it with the layer creates an issue. No error event arrived in any variant (errors-only, tracing, launch, v3 and v4): the `@sentry/effect` build contains no `captureException` call, `defaultIntegrations` is forced to `false` so the Node error integrations are off and only `SpanStreaming` is installed, and the SDK's own e2e app captures failures by hand with `Sentry.captureException(Cause.squash(cause))`. Run with `Effect.runPromise` and no catch, the failure crashes the process and sends nothing; `NodeRuntime.runMain` exits 1 and sends only the sentinel.

What to change:

- Show a `catchAllCause` or `tapErrorCause` that calls `Sentry.captureException(Cause.squash(cause))`, say that failed effects are not captured on their own, and show the run call next to it.

heading: The Nitro guide's error and span claims do not match the build
title: Correct the Nitro error-capture and span claims
body:
`guides/nitro/index.mdx:273` says the error hook captures unhandled errors and skips 3xx and 4xx HTTPErrors: true on nitro 3.0.260415-beta; on 3.0.260903-beta every handler error is captured twice (`auto.http.nitro.onTraceError` plus `auto.function.nitro.captureErrorHook`) and the 404 HTTPError is reported. `:203-214` and `:228-249` say the verify route's `Error("My first Sentry error!")` creates the issue; the event's outermost exception is `HTTPError: My first Sentry error!`, Nitro's 500 wrapper, with the thrown Error as a chained cause, so the issue is titled HTTPError. `:289` says middleware spans use `op: 'middleware.nitro'`; the h3 spans have op `middleware` and are named after the route (`middleware GET /api/users/:id`), never after the middleware. `:286` says the SDK creates transactions for incoming requests; only span items arrive. `:291` says 4xx HTTPErrors do not mark the span errored; the `/error-404` segment arrives with status `error` and status code 404.

What to change:

- Scope the error-hook claim to the verified Nitro versions and note the newer betas' duplicates, tell the reader the issue is titled HTTPError with the original error chained, change the op to `middleware` with route naming, say request spans instead of transactions, and drop or restrict the 4xx claim.

heading: Guide hygiene: no Bun version requirement, npm install in the Hono guide, v7 tracing wording
title: Fix Bun guide hygiene: version floor, Hono install command, v7 wording
body:
`guides/bun/index.mdx:12` pulls the `getting-started-prerequisites` include, but no `javascript.bun.mdx` variant of it exists, so the page falls back to `_default.mdx` and states no Bun version floor. `guides/hono/index.mdx:84-85` installs the Bun SDK with `npm install @sentry/bun`, while the Bun guide uses `bun add`. `platform-includes/performance/automatic-instrumentation-intro/javascript.bun.mdx:1` still says the SDK "provides a `Tracing` integration", which is v7 wording.

What was observed: CI runs the Bun SDK against Bun 1.3.14 (`.github/workflows/build.yml:522`), which is the version the SDK is verified on.

What to change:

- Add `platform-includes/getting-started-prerequisites/javascript.bun.mdx` stating the Bun version the SDK is tested against (1.3.14), in the shape of `platform-includes/getting-started-prerequisites/javascript.deno.mdx:7` ("Deno version >= `2.0.0`").
- Change the Bun install tab in `guides/hono/index.mdx:84-85` to `bun add @sentry/bun`.
- Delete the "provides a Tracing integration" sentence from `platform-includes/performance/automatic-instrumentation-intro/javascript.bun.mdx`.

heading: The Deno v7-to-v8 migration include files are copies of the Bun ones
title: Rewrite the three Deno v7-to-v8 migration includes that are copies of the Bun ones
body:
The Deno v7-to-v8 migration includes are Bun text. `platform-includes/migration/javascript-v8/important-changes/javascript.deno.mdx:9` says "Sentry Bun SDK" and, at `:34-48`, claims OpenTelemetry-powered auto-instrumentation with bullets for Express (`:38`), Fastify (`:39`), Hapi (`:40`) and Nest (`:46`). `platform-includes/migration/javascript-v8/integrations-package-removal/javascript.deno.mdx:3-5` names `@sentry/bun`. `platform-includes/migration/javascript-v8/other-changes/javascript.deno.mdx:3` says "your Bun SDK" and links `./v8-opentelemetry`, whose `supported:` list does not include `javascript.deno`, so the link renders dead on the Deno guide.

What was observed: the v8 Deno SDK did not have the OpenTelemetry-powered framework auto-instrumentation the include describes, and the package under discussion on these pages is `@sentry/deno`.

What to change:

- In `important-changes/javascript.deno.mdx`, replace "Sentry Bun SDK" at `:9` with "Sentry Deno SDK" and delete the OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation list at `:34-48`, including the Express (`:38`), Fastify (`:39`), Hapi (`:40`) and Nest (`:46`) bullets.
- In `integrations-package-removal/javascript.deno.mdx:3-5`, replace `@sentry/bun` with `@sentry/deno`.
- In `other-changes/javascript.deno.mdx:3`, replace "your Bun SDK" with "your Deno SDK" and remove the `./v8-opentelemetry` link, which is not shown for Deno.

heading: The guide shows only the npm: specifier, never deno add or an import map, and events name a registry that does not ship the package
title: Show deno add and an import map in the Deno guide's install step
body:
`guides/deno/index.mdx:38-46` says to "Import the Sentry Deno SDK directly from the npm registry", and every snippet on the page renders `npm:@sentry/deno` from the `___SDK_PACKAGE___` placeholder (the literal specifier is not in the file). `guides/hono/index.mdx:88-89` is the only page showing `deno add npm:@sentry/deno`. The Deno `featureflags` and `enable-stream-mode` includes hardcode `@sentry/deno` and `npm:@sentry/deno` instead of the `___SDK_PACKAGE___` placeholder.

What was observed: every Deno e2e app uses a `deno.json` import map and the bare `@sentry/deno` specifier, which is also the form the `@sentry/deno/import` hook requires. Events reported by the SDK carry `sdk.packages[0].name = "denoland:sentry"`.

What to change:

- In the install step at `guides/deno/index.mdx:38-46`, add `deno add npm:@sentry/deno` and show the resulting `deno.json` import map entry.
- Use the bare `@sentry/deno` specifier in the snippets that follow, since that is the form the hook import needs, and keep `npm:@sentry/deno` documented as the no-import-map alternative.
- Replace the hardcoded package names in the Deno `featureflags` (`:2`) and `enable-stream-mode` (`:11`) includes with `___SDK_PACKAGE___`.
- While in `enable-stream-mode/javascript.deno.mdx`, note that `:24` calls `traceLifecycle: 'static'` "the default", which holds for the released line only; DOC-Q1 tracks that sentence across all ten runtime variants of the include.

heading: Four Cloudflare options have no SdkOption entry, and the deprecated enableRpcTracePropagation block outlives the option
title: Add the four missing Cloudflare SdkOption entries and drop the deprecated enableRpcTracePropagation block
body:
Four `@sentry/cloudflare` options have no `SdkOption` entry in `common/configuration/options.mdx`: `cacheClient`, `enableOpenTelemetrySetup`, `durableObjectSqlSpanAllowlist` and `durableObjectStorageSpanAllowlist`. Three of them appear nowhere in `docs/` or `platform-includes/`; `enableOpenTelemetrySetup` appears six times, all inside `common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx`, none of them an options entry.

What was observed: the SDK declares all four in `packages/cloudflare/src/client.ts` - `enableOpenTelemetrySetup` at `:324`, `durableObjectSqlSpanAllowlist` at `:384`, `durableObjectStorageSpanAllowlist` at `:409` and `cacheClient` at `:451`, on the same lines at `6f2da7483d` and at develop head. `rpcTracePropagationBindings` is declared at `:360` and now has its own entry at `options.mdx:580-592`; the deprecated `enableRpcTracePropagation` entry at `options.mdx:594-600` documents an option v11 removes (`MIGRATION.md:1418-1431`, `:1624-1637` at develop head).

What to change:

- Add `SdkOption` entries to `common/configuration/options.mdx` for `cacheClient`, `enableOpenTelemetrySetup`, `durableObjectSqlSpanAllowlist` and `durableObjectStorageSpanAllowlist`.
- In the v11 docs update, remove the deprecated `enableRpcTracePropagation` block at `common/configuration/options.mdx:594-600`; the `rpcTracePropagationBindings` entry at `:580-592` replaces it.

heading: No page lists which bindings produce spans, and the list changed twice this year
title: Add a bindings table to the Cloudflare features/index.mdx
body:
No Cloudflare page lists which Worker bindings produce spans. `guides/cloudflare/features/index.mdx` is a 13-line PageGrid. `agent-tracing/workers-ai.mdx` covers Workers AI, D1 is described as a manual wrapper in `features/d1.mdx`, and `common/tracing/instrumentation/caches-module.mdx` and `queues-module.mdx` are shown for Cloudflare while describing Redis and manual spans only.

What was observed in `instrumentEnv.ts` at `6f2da7483d`: D1 bindings are instrumented automatically with span op `db.query`; R2 is instrumented (`instrumentR2.ts:26-48`) with `object.*` ops; Queues producers are instrumented with the span name `send <binding>` (`instrumentQueueProducer.ts:20`) and the `queue.publish` op (`:28`); `env.AI.run` produces `gen_ai.*` spans; Durable Object namespaces and service bindings get trace-propagation headers and RPC metadata, with RPC instrumented and headers not; the rate limiter binding is not instrumented at that commit. Workers KV, Vectorize, Hyperdrive, Analytics Engine, the Cache API and Assets are not instrumented. The `d1`, `r2`, `queue` and `ratelimit` integration suites pin these.

What to change:

- Add a bindings table to `guides/cloudflare/features/index.mdx` with columns: binding, instrumented, span op, where it is documented, using the rows above.
- State plainly that Workers KV, Vectorize, Hyperdrive, Analytics Engine, the Cache API and Assets produce no spans.
- Adjust the `supported:` lists so the caches and queues common pages are not shown as Cloudflare binding documentation.

heading: Snippet hygiene across the Cloudflare includes
title: Fix snippet errors across the Cloudflare includes and framework pages
body:
Several Cloudflare includes show code that does not match the package or the guide's own contract. `platform-includes/tracing/traces-sampler/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:4` calls `Sentry.browserTracingIntegration()`. `platform-includes/tracing/sample-rate/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:1-7` and the `capture-console` (`:1-8`) and `dedupe` (`:1-8`) configuration includes show a bare `Sentry.init(...)`. `platform-includes/configuration/contextlines/javascript.cloudflare.mdx` exists but `contextlines.mdx` lists `cloudflare` under `notSupported`, so it never renders. `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:38-40` and `:356-360` contain a `logs` onboarding block that is not in the button list. `frameworks/nextjs.mdx:40` and `getting-started-config/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:5` state compatibility dates of 2025-08-16 and 2024-09-23 without saying which applies to whom. `frameworks/hydrogen-remix.mdx:59` contains a literal `YOUR_DSN_HERE`.

What was observed: `@sentry/cloudflare` does not export `browserTracingIntegration` on the released line, at `6f2da7483d` or at develop head; the guide's configuration contract is `withSentry` or `sentryPagesPlugin`; the 2025-08-16 date is OpenNext's `https.request` floor. Bun and Deno have guide-local `contextlines` overrides, so only the Cloudflare include is unreachable.

What to change:

- Replace `browserTracingIntegration()` in the traces-sampler include.
- Rewrite the bare `Sentry.init(...)` snippets as `withSentry` / `sentryPagesPlugin`.
- Remove `cloudflare` from `notSupported` in `contextlines.mdx` or delete the unreachable Cloudflare include, leaving the Bun and Deno includes in place.
- Add `logs` to the onboarding buttons.
- Say on each page which compatibility date applies.
- Replace `YOUR_DSN_HERE` with `___PUBLIC_DSN___`.

heading: "Tracing is enabled by default" on all three runtimes contradicts the guides
title: Fix "Tracing is enabled by default" in the Bun, Deno and Cloudflare enable-tracing includes
body:
`platform-includes/performance/enable-tracing/javascript.bun.mdx:1`, `javascript.deno.mdx:1` and `javascript.cloudflare.mdx:1` each read "Tracing is enabled by default in the Sentry <Runtime> SDK." The guides for those runtimes, and `platform-includes/performance/enable-automatic-instrumentation/javascript.bun.mdx:1` and `javascript.cloudflare.mdx:1`, tell the user to set `tracesSampleRate` or `tracesSampler`.

What was observed: `hasSpansEnabled` in `packages/core/src/utils/hasSpansEnabled.ts:23-36` records spans only when `tracesSampleRate` or `tracesSampler` is set, on every runtime. On Bun there is a second gate on top of it: `getPerformanceIntegrations` in `packages/bun/src/sdk.ts:38-44` returns no performance integrations while `hasSpansEnabled` is false. The Deno and Cloudflare SDKs have no such gate and always install the tracing integrations, so the general reason the sentence is wrong is the sampling option, not the integration set.

What to change:

- Replace the first sentence in all three includes with a statement that tracing is enabled by setting `tracesSampleRate` or `tracesSampler` in `Sentry.init`, and that no spans are recorded when neither is set.
- Keep the wording consistent with the `enable-automatic-instrumentation` includes for Bun and Cloudflare, which already require the option. There is no Deno variant of that include, so Deno falls back to `javascript.mdx`.

heading: The page for Astro on Cloudflare Workers is correct
title: Confirm tested versions and database spans on the Astro on Cloudflare page
body:
`docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/astro.mdx:1-142` already covers this combination and `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/index.mdx:24-25` routes Cloudflare users to it. The substance lives in two Cloudflare-gated sections of `platform-includes/getting-started-complete/javascript.astro.mdx`, `:57-85` and `:89-174`: installing both `@sentry/astro` and `@sentry/cloudflare` at `:59-84`, the wrangler config at `:89-96`, the custom entry point with `"main": "./sentry.server.config.ts"` at `:109-114` plus `Sentry.withSentry((env) => ({...}), handler)` around `@astrojs/cloudflare/entrypoints/server` at `:127-142`, and registering `sentry()` alongside `cloudflare()` in `astro.config.mjs` at `:148-174` (the snippet itself at `:158-168`). `astro.mdx:12` requires Astro 6.0.0 or above and `:13` requires `@astrojs/cloudflare` v13 or above.

Verified on the develop line: Astro 7.3.1 with `@astrojs/cloudflare` 14.3.0, `compatibility_date: "2026-05-01"`, `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]`, `npx astro build` then `npx wrangler dev --config dist/server/wrangler.json`. Both halves of the documented wiring were required and neither worked alone, exactly as the page prescribes; no separate Cloudflare Vite plugin was added.

Works today:

- Unhandled route errors (mechanism `auto.middleware.astro`), parameterized route names with `http.route` and source `route`, per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers, `db` spans with no configuration beyond the documented setup, `Sentry.logger` logs.

Known limits:

- Only the server runtime was exercised; the client half of `@sentry/astro` was not part of this run.

What to change on `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/astro.mdx`:

- Widen the tested-version statements: Astro 7.3.1 on `:12` and `@astrojs/cloudflare` 14.3.0 on `:13`, both on `compatibility_date` `2026-05-01`.
- Add one line stating that database spans need no setup beyond registering `sentry()` in `astro.config.mjs`, rather than leaving it unmentioned.
- Say why wrangler's `main` points at `./sentry.server.config.ts` and not at a `dist` path: `@astrojs/cloudflare` v14 runs `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` during `astro build` and resolves `main` at config time, so a `dist` path fails the build before the file exists.

heading: OpenTelemetry pages gated to Bun; Deno sets up a tracer by default and Cloudflare opts in
title: Add Deno and Cloudflare to the OpenTelemetry overview and API pages
body:
The three OpenTelemetry pages gate themselves to a `supported` allowlist that includes `javascript.bun` but neither `javascript.deno` nor `javascript.cloudflare`: `docs/platforms/javascript/common/opentelemetry/index.mdx:11`, `custom-setup.mdx:9` and `using-opentelemetry-apis.mdx:9`. Deno and Cloudflare readers never see the section.

Both runtimes support the setup on develop, with different defaults. `packages/deno/src/sdk.ts:114` calls `setupOpenTelemetryTracer()` when `options.enableOpenTelemetrySetup ?? true`, so a Deno app gets a Sentry OpenTelemetry tracer provider unless it passes `enableOpenTelemetrySetup: false`, and spans created through `@opentelemetry/api` reach Sentry with no extra configuration. `packages/cloudflare/src/sdk.ts:23` sets `options.enableOpenTelemetrySetup ??= false` and installs the tracer at `:27-29` only when the option is `true`. Bun, already on the list, is off by default too: it delegates to `@sentry/node`, where `packages/node/src/sdk/index.ts:253` applies `options.enableOpenTelemetrySetup ?? false`.

`custom-setup.mdx` is the exception and should stay gated for now. Its body is written around `skipOpenTelemetrySetup` (`:35`, `:122`, `:132`), `SentryContextManager` (`:35`, `:53`), `SentrySpanProcessor` (`:53`, `:66`) and `SentrySampler` (`:53`), none of which exist on develop, and the include it pulls for JavaScript readers is written against the same removed API. There is no `javascript.deno.mdx` or `javascript.cloudflare.mdx` under `platform-includes/performance/opentelemetry-setup/`, so the two guides would fall back to `javascript.mdx` and get a page that cannot be followed.

What to change:

- Add `- javascript.deno` and `- javascript.cloudflare` to the `supported` lists in `opentelemetry/index.mdx` and `using-opentelemetry-apis.mdx`, after checking those two bodies for Node-only wording.
- State the differing defaults: Deno sets up the tracer unless `enableOpenTelemetrySetup: false`, Cloudflare only with `enableOpenTelemetrySetup: true`, Bun off unless it is turned on.
- Leave `custom-setup.mdx:9` as it is until that page and the `performance/opentelemetry-setup` includes are dealt with.

heading: Bun and Deno v7 migration tables map to inboundFiltersIntegration and debugIntegration, both removed
title: Fix removed integration names in the Bun and Deno v7 migration tables
body:
The v7 deprecation tables map old class names to functions that no longer exist. `platform-includes/migration/javascript-v8/v7-deprecation/javascript.bun.mdx:5` and `javascript.deno.mdx:5` point `new InboundFilters()` at `inboundFiltersIntegration()`, and `:10` in both points `new Debug()` at `debugIntegration()`. The same tables list `sessionTimingIntegration()` at `:14` and `nativeNodeFetchIntegration()` at `:24`.

On develop, `inboundFiltersIntegration`, `debugIntegration` and `sessionTimingIntegration` appear in no `packages/*/src` at all. The filtering integration is now `eventFiltersIntegration` (`packages/bun/src/index.ts:96` on develop, `:94` at the pin; `packages/deno/src/index.ts:72`, unchanged), a rename the migration guide already records at `docs/platforms/javascript/common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:1406`.

`nativeNodeFetchIntegration` is a different case. It still exists, is exported by `@sentry/node` (`packages/node/src/index.ts:2`) and is a default integration there (`packages/node/src/sdk/index.ts:63`); what is wrong is that neither `@sentry/bun` nor `@sentry/deno` re-exports it, so on these two pages the `new Undici()` row names something the reader cannot import.

The Deno table lists eight further names that `@sentry/deno` does not export: `consoleIntegration` (`:15`), `nodeContextIntegration` (`:16`), `modulesIntegration` (`:17`), `onUncaughtExceptionIntegration` (`:18`), `onUnhandledRejectionIntegration` (`:19`), `spotlightIntegration` (`:21`), `anrIntegration` (`:22`) and `httpIntegration` (`:25`). The same rows are correct in the Bun table: `@sentry/bun` re-exports all of them (`packages/bun/src/index.ts:75`, `:78`, `:79`, `:82`, `:83`, `:87`, `:89` and `:148` at the pin; `modulesIntegration` `:89`, `nodeContextIntegration` `:91` and `spotlightIntegration` `:150` on develop).

What to change:

- Point the `InboundFilters` row at `eventFiltersIntegration()` in both tables.
- Drop the `Debug` and `SessionTiming` rows from both tables.
- Drop the `Undici` row from both tables, or say that `nativeNodeFetchIntegration` lives in `@sentry/node` and is not re-exported by these two SDKs.
- Prune the Deno table to what `@sentry/deno` exports: remove the `Console`, `Context`, `Modules`, `OnUncaughtException`, `OnUnhandledRejection`, `Spotlight`, `Anr` and `Http` rows. Leave the Bun table's equivalents.

heading: Durable Objects page omits the webSocketMessage, webSocketClose and alarm spans the SDK creates
title: Document the Durable Object WebSocket and alarm instrumentation
body:
`docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/durableobject.mdx` documents two things: storage spans at `:33-37` and RPC trace propagation at `:39-41`. The intro at `:8` says the wrapper instruments Durable Objects but never lists which handlers produce telemetry, so a reader debugging a WebSocket or alarm workload has nothing to go on.

On develop, `packages/cloudflare/src/instrumentations/instrumentDurableObjectHandlers.ts:44-129` wraps five handlers by default: `fetch` (`:44`), `alarm` (`:66`), `webSocketMessage` (`:85`), `webSocketClose` (`:102`) and `webSocketError` (`:119`), each producing one span per invocation.
