The last four go through `wrapMethodWithSentry` with `origin: 'auto.faas.cloudflare.durable_object'` (`:78`, `:95`, `:112`, `:129`), and that origin is used both as the span's `sentry.origin` attribute and as the `mechanism.type` of exceptions the wrapper captures (`packages/cloudflare/src/wrapMethodWithSentry.ts:72-76` and `:168-176`). `fetch` runs through the request wrapper instead: its span is an `http.server` span with origin `auto.http.cloudflare`, while errors thrown inside it carry mechanism `auto.faas.cloudflare.durable_object` (`packages/cloudflare/src/wrapRequestHandlerWithInit.ts:30-33`). The WebSocket error handed to `webSocketError` is captured with its own mechanism, `auto.faas.cloudflare.durable_object_websocket` (`:135`).

The `alarm` span is an `op: function` span named `alarm` that starts a new trace carrying `sentry.previous_trace` and a span link back to the `setAlarm` span. Two neighbouring facts belong on the page as well: `stub.fetch()` produces no `http.client` span, and under the stream lifecycle the Durable Object request span is named `GET` with the URL as an attribute.

What to change:

- Add a section listing the instrumented handlers: `fetch`, `alarm`, `webSocketMessage`, `webSocketClose`, `webSocketError`.
- Say what each produces — one span per WebSocket message, one per close, one per alarm firing.
- Distinguish origin from mechanism: spans from the four non-`fetch` handlers carry `sentry.origin: auto.faas.cloudflare.durable_object`, and errors thrown in them arrive with `mechanism: auto.faas.cloudflare.durable_object`.
- Note the alarm's new trace and its link back to `setAlarm`, that `stub.fetch()` produces no `http.client` span, and that the request span is named `GET` with the URL as an attribute in stream mode.

heading: Deno guide never mentions deno serve, which is instrumented like Deno.serve
title: Add deno serve to the Deno guide run commands
body:
The Deno guide shows only two ways to start an app: `deno run --allow-net=___ORG_INGEST_DOMAIN___ index.ts` at `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:100` and `deno run --allow-read=./src index.ts` at `:119`. The string `deno serve` appears nowhere under `docs/`, `platform-includes/` or `includes/`, so a reader using the default-export server form has no confirmation that the SDK covers it.

An `export default { fetch }` entrypoint started with `deno serve` is instrumented exactly like `Deno.serve`. The DenoServe integration proxies `Deno.serve` (`packages/deno/src/integrations/deno-serve.ts:80-93` on develop, `:75-88` at the pin), which is what `deno serve` calls internally. `--parallel` re-executes the entry module once per worker thread, so a 16-worker run performs 16 `Sentry.init` calls in one process; a recorded run of 55 requests produced exactly 55 spans, one per request, and per-request tags stayed inside their own worker in all ten checks.

One caveat belongs next to the note: an entry written as the guide shows it, without the `import "@sentry/deno/import"` hook line, still reports errors and `http.server` spans under `deno serve`, but produces no library spans — the module-scope mysql query lost its `db` span.

What to change:

- Add a `deno serve` note to the Deno guide alongside the existing run commands.
- State that a default-export `fetch` handler is instrumented the same way as `Deno.serve`.
- Note that `--parallel` initializes once per worker without duplicate events and without scope data crossing workers.
- Say that the entry still needs `import "@sentry/deno/import"` for library spans.

heading: Cloudflare Pages middleware snippet does not say the root middleware also spans static asset requests
title: Note that the root Pages middleware also spans static asset requests
body:
The Cloudflare Pages setup at `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:161-205` tells the reader to register `sentryPagesPlugin` as the first entry in `onRequest` inside `functions/_middleware.js` (snippet at `:174`). `includes/cloudflare-pages-middleware-intro.mdx` instructs creating that file in the `functions` directory at the project root. Neither says which requests the middleware then handles.

A root `functions/_middleware.js` runs on every Cloudflare Pages request, static asset requests included. Under the default stream lifecycle each asset fetch produces its own `http.server` span envelope alongside the app's function routes, which changes both the trace volume and what the reader sees in the performance view; the same requests become transactions only with `traceLifecycle: "static"`. The naming is worth stating too: the root request span is named `GET /` and every other path is named bare `GET`, with the path carried in the `url.path` attribute.

What to change:

- Add a note to the Pages setup section stating that a root middleware runs on every request, static assets included.
- Say what arrives per request under the default stream lifecycle: one `http.server` span envelope, named `GET /` for the root and `GET` for every other path, with `url.path` as an attribute.
- Point readers at scoping the middleware to a subdirectory, for example `functions/api/_middleware.js`, when they want only their function routes instrumented.

heading: The documented Bun path logs two warnings about missing channel injection that no page explains
title: Explain the channel-injection warnings on the Bun guide
body:
Following the "Apply Instrumentation to Your App" step at `guides/bun/index.mdx:82-105` as written, `bun --preload ./instrument.ts app.ts` (the command at `:100`) with `debug: true` prints `No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping.` at startup and `[Sentry] No diagnostics-channel injection detected. Channel-based integrations will not record spans. Make sure the diagnostics channels are injected via the runtime --import hook or a bundler plugin before the instrumented modules load.` after the first request. Neither line is mentioned on the Bun guide or the troubleshooting pages, and the guide names no bundler plugin (DOC-B1).

Observed on `develop` with bun 1.4.2: the warnings are correct. The first comes from `packages/server-runtime-injection/src/register.ts:160` (`:201` at develop head), the second from `packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/detect.ts:38-42`; both go through `debug.warn`, so they print only with `debug: true`. Runtime instrumentation (`Bun.serve`, fetch, errors, logs) works on the documented path, and library instrumentation needs the `Bun.build` with `sentryBunPlugin()`. A reader who sees the warning has no page that says which of the two it refers to.

What to change:

- Quote both lines on the Bun guide next to the run command at `:100`, say that they print only with `debug: true` and that runtime instrumentation is unaffected, and link the plugin build step from DOC-B1 as the fix for library spans.

heading: Node guide: the --require flag prints an undocumented "no longer supported" banner, and the ordering warning is stricter than develop
title: Update the Node getting-started page for --require and for first-line ESM imports
body:
`platform-includes/getting-started-node/javascript.mdx:93-96` shows `node --import ./instrument.mjs app.mjs`, and `:55` warns that importing the instrument file later than first means auto-instrumentation and modules like database monitoring may not work. Nothing on the page mentions `--require`.

Observed on `develop` with Node v26.5.0: `node --require ./instrument.cjs app.mjs` still delivers the same errors, spans, headers and logs, but its first stderr line is `[Sentry] Initializing the SDK via the Node --require flag is no longer supported, because Node re-runs --require preloads on its module loader thread. Use --import instead`, printed from `packages/node/src/sdk/index.ts:126-133` whenever `getEntryPointType() === 'require'`, unconditionally and not behind `debug`. A first-line `import "./instrument.mjs"` in the entry file gives the same telemetry as the flag, including Express route names and handler spans, because the injection hook is registered while `@sentry/node` evaluates. `NODE_OPTIONS="--import ./instrument.mjs"` is identical to the flag.

What to change:

- Add one sentence that `--require` is no longer supported for initializing the SDK and prints a banner, with the `--import` replacement. Keep it narrow: `common/install/late-initialization.mdx:34,37,106,132` recommends `node --require @sentry/node/preload app.js`, which no longer resolves on develop, because the `preload` entry point was removed from every server SDK (see DOC-Q26); the warning against `--require` can therefore stand without that exception.
- Soften the ordering warning at `:55`: a first-line ESM import of the instrument file is equivalent to `--import`; the warning applies to imports that are not first.
- Surface `NODE_OPTIONS` as an equivalent form on this page; it is already documented at `common/install/esm.mdx:44-48`.

heading: Cloudflare guide: wrangler dev stack traces have no context lines and point at the dev bundle, while source maps are presented as optional
title: Say on the Cloudflare guide that readable stack traces need the source maps step
body:
`guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:240` introduces source maps as an optional improvement. The verify step at `:267-280` says the thrown error produces an issue, with no word on what the stack trace looks like; the Pages variant at `:297-301` has the same problem.

Observed on develop under `wrangler dev`: the error event arrives with `hasContextLine: false`, every frame in `.wrangler/tmp/dev-*/index.js`, and no runtime version. The same app on Node, Bun and Deno ships context lines and source paths. The segment span of the throwing route also reports status `ok` although the Worker answered 500 (SDK-side, tracked separately).

What to change:

- Move the source maps step before the verify step, or state in both verify snippets (`:267-280` for Workers, `:297-301` for Pages) that the first issue shows bundle frames without source lines until source maps are uploaded.
- Show what the issue looks like without source maps, so the reader does not take it for a broken setup.

heading: The documented tracePropagationTargets value drops trace headers on 127.0.0.1
title: Say on the browser config page that the sample tracePropagationTargets matches localhost only
body:
`platform-includes/getting-started-config/javascript.mdx:46` sets `tracePropagationTargets: ["localhost", /^https:\/\/yourserver\.io\/api/]` and presents it as the value for local development.

Observed on develop: the same page served on `http://localhost` sends `sentry-trace` and `baggage` on its fetch; served on `http://127.0.0.1` it creates the `http.client` span but sends no headers, because the string `"localhost"` does not match the IP form.

What to change:

- Say that the sample matches the string `localhost` only, and show `127.0.0.1` or a regular expression for readers whose dev server is reached by IP.

heading: The verify flow discards the session replay when the error fires within the first five seconds
title: Tell browser readers to wait before triggering the verify error if they expect a replay
body:
`platform-includes/getting-started-config/javascript.mdx:50-55` sets `replaysOnErrorSampleRate: 1.0` and says that the replay is captured for every session with an error; the verify step tells the reader to click the button.

Observed on develop, clicking the button right after load: the error event carries a `replayId` tag, and the replay is dropped with `[Replay] Session duration (0s) is too short, not sending replay.` An error thrown later in the same session produced the `replay_event` with `replay_type: buffer`.

What to change:

- Add one sentence to the verify step: a replay is sent only when the session is at least five seconds old (`minReplayDuration`), so wait before clicking, and the issue will still show a replay id before the replay exists.
- Apply the same sentence to the React guide at `guides/react/index.mdx:344-346`, where the first verify click behaved the same way (QS-react, variant base); the Angular manual-setup run saw the same drop (QS-angular, variant base).

heading: The React guide's routing snippet uses the deprecated V7-suffixed API
title: Move the React guide routing snippet to the version-agnostic React Router API
body:
`guides/react/index.mdx:242-264` wires tracing with `Sentry.reactRouterV7BrowserTracingIntegration({ useEffect, useLocation, ... })` and `wrapCreateBrowserRouterV7`. It works (pageload and navigation segments named `/users/:userId`), but the develop build marks both, and every other `*V6` and `*V7` export, `@deprecated` in `build/types/index.d.ts` in favor of `reactRouterBrowserTracingIntegration` and `wrapCreateBrowserRouter`, which `guides/react/features/react-router/v8.mdx:7-66` documents and which behaved the same on react-router 7.18.3 and 8.3.1. There is no runtime warning. The `@sentry/react/react-router` subpath with a hook-less `reactRouterBrowserTracingIntegration()` is undocumented.

What to change:

- Switch the guide snippet to the version-agnostic API and mention the `@sentry/react/react-router` subpath.

heading: The React verify step promises transactions and shows a test span that ends before its error
title: Rewrite the React verify step for the stream lifecycle and fix the test span
body:
`guides/react/index.mdx:99` says `tracesSampleRate: 1.0` captures 100% of transactions, the verify text at `:336-338` promises page load traces and the test span, and the React Router pages promise pageload and navigation transactions (`features/react-router/index.mdx:16`, `v7.mdx:163`, `v8.mdx:165`, `features/tanstack-router.mdx:14`). Observed under the default lifecycle: only `span` envelope items, a pageload segment named `Pageload` (the route pattern once a router integration is set up) with its children, and no transaction envelope in any run.

The tracing test at `:374-389` wraps the error in `Sentry.startSpan` with a synchronous callback: the span ends at 0 ms with status `ok`, and the error fires 99 ms later from the `setTimeout` (mechanism `auto.browser.browserapierrors.setTimeout`), marking the pageload segment `error` instead.

What to change:

- Say traces and root spans instead of transactions, and that the pageload span is named `Pageload` until a router integration supplies the route.
- Make the span callback `async` and await the delay before throwing, or say the error is captured on its own.

heading: The React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, Solid and WebAssembly guides' config sends no sessions because it sets no release
title: Say on the React, Vue, Angular, Svelte, Solid and WebAssembly guides that release health sessions need a release
body:
`guides/react/index.mdx:73-117` presents `instrument.js` as the complete configuration. It sets no `release`, and the SDK then discards every session with `Discarded session because of missing or non-string release`: zero session envelopes in nine runs, although the `BrowserSession` integration is installed. The browser guide's config include sets a release at `platform-includes/getting-started-config/javascript.mdx:21`; the React guide renders its own snippet without one. The Vue guide's `main.js` at `guides/vue/index.mdx:71-126` has the same gap: every run logged `Discarded session because of missing or non-string release` and sent no session envelope (QS-vue, variant base). The Angular manual-setup snippet at `guides/angular/manual-setup.mdx:109-164` behaves the same (QS-angular, every variant). So does the Svelte guide's `main.js` at `guides/svelte/index.mdx:69-122` (QS-svelte, variant base). The Solid guide's `index.jsx` at `guides/solid/index.mdx:73-133` is the fifth (QS-solid, variant base), and the WebAssembly guide's init at `guides/wasm/index.mdx:70-100` the sixth (QS-wasm, every variant).

What to change:

- Add `release` to the six snippets, or a one-line note that sessions need it.

heading: The Vue guide and feature pages promise transactions that the stream lifecycle never sends
title: Rewrite the Vue guide and its feature pages for the stream lifecycle
body:
`guides/vue/index.mdx:103-104`, `features/vue-router.mdx:6` and `:60`, and `features/component-tracking.mdx:7` and `:19` speak of transactions, parameterized transaction names and spans in your transactions. Observed under the default lifecycle: only `span` envelope items, pageload and navigation segments named by the route name (`user`, `home`, source `custom`) or by the parameterized path with `routeLabel: "path"` (`/users/:id`, source `route`), `Pageload` without a router, and no transaction envelope in any run.

What to change:

- Say root spans and traces, name the two `routeLabel` shapes, and say the data appears in the trace view.

heading: The Vue guide's late-init and multiple-apps snippets do not run as printed
title: Fix the late-initialization and multiple-apps snippets on the Vue pages
body:
`guides/vue/index.mdx:203-219` calls `createApp({ template: "
hello
" })` without importing `createApp`, and the `template` option renders nothing (``, no production warning) on the default runtime-only `vue` export; it works only with the `vue/dist/vue.esm-bundler.js` alias. With those two fixes `addIntegration(vueIntegration({ app }))` adds Vue as the twelfth integration and the late app's error carries `contexts.vue`. `guides/vue/features/multiple-apps.mdx:13-21` calls `Vue.createApp(App)` with no import; a default import of `vue` fails on Vue 3, `import * as Vue from "vue"` works, and then all three apps report errors as `auto.function.vue.error_handler` with `contexts.vue`. What to change: - Import `createApp` and use a render function or an SFC root, or note the full-build alias. - Show the import line on the multiple-apps page.

heading: The Vue verify error looks different in a development build
title: Say on the Vue guide that the component context of the verify error appears in production builds
body:
`guides/vue/index.mdx:273-298` tells the reader to click the button and find the error. In a development build the error is captured first by `BrowserApiErrors` without `contexts.vue`, the Vue error handler's capture is dropped as already captured, and Vue prints `Unhandled error during execution of app errorHandler`. In a production build the same click is captured once as `auto.function.vue.error_handler` with the component name and props.

What to change:

- Add a sentence that the component context and the clean console appear in production builds, and that the dev-mode warning is expected.

heading: The Express, Fastify, Koa and Hapi guides teach deprecated error handler calls
title: Drop the deprecated setup*ErrorHandler calls from the Express, Fastify, Koa and Hapi getting-started snippets
body:
`platform-includes/getting-started-use/javascript.express.mdx:15` and `:34` add `Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler(app)` after all routes. On develop the export is marked `@deprecated` in the build (`server-utils/build/types/integrations/express/error-handler.d.ts:17-20`), takes only `app`, and prints no notice at runtime. The variants without the call captured the same events on express 4 and 5 (`auto.http.express`, `handled: false`, 5xx only), and `expressIntegration({ shouldHandleError })` is what changes the filter, as `common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:715-746` describes. The Fastify tab does the same at `platform-includes/getting-started-use/javascript.fastify.mdx:11` and `:28`: `setupFastifyErrorHandler(app)` is a deprecated empty function on develop, the variants without it captured the same events on Fastify 4 and 5, and nothing is printed at runtime (QS-fastify, variants no-handler and fastify4-no-handler). The Koa tab at `getting-started-use/javascript.koa.mdx:11` and `:28` places `setupKoaErrorHandler(app)` before `app.listen()`: the deprecated call adds an `app.on('error')` listener that pre-empts Koa's default one, so Koa's stderr error logging silently disappears while capture is identical without the call under `--import` (QS-koa, variants import and no-handler; the direct-import exception is DOC-Q45). The Hapi tab at `getting-started-use/javascript.hapi.mdx:17` and `:42` tells readers to `await Sentry.setupHapiErrorHandler(server)` before `server.start()`; the export is deprecated and a no-op on develop, the listener is auto-registered on the start channel, and every no-handler variant captured the identical four events (QS-hapi, variants no-handler, self-import-no-handler and errors-only-no-handler).

What to change:

- Remove the four calls from the getting-started snippets and point at `expressIntegration({ shouldHandleError })` and `fastifyIntegration({ shouldHandleError })` for filtering.

heading: No integration page documents expressIntegration and its options
title: Add an expressIntegration page to the integrations directory
body:
`docs/platforms/javascript/common/configuration/integrations/` documents connect, fastify, hapi, koa and nest, and nothing describes `expressIntegration` for Express users. On develop `expressIntegration({ ignoreLayers, ignoreLayersType, shouldHandleError })` exists, and `shouldHandleError` works: the migration page's callback made `/error-404` captured next to the 5xx defaults. The options are described only at `common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:722-748`.

What to change:

- Add `configuration/integrations/express.mdx` next to `fastify.mdx` and `koa.mdx`, covering the three options and the 5xx-only default.

heading: Express, Fastify, Koa and Connect guide hygiene: an empty include, orphaned includes and an unreachable logs section
title: Fix the empty capture-errors include and the orphaned includes on the Express guide
body:
`platform-includes/getting-started-node/javascript.mdx:102` renders `getting-started-capture-errors`, a directory with no `javascript.mdx` and no `_default.mdx`, so the Express, Fastify, Koa and Connect guides render nothing there; for Connect that missing step is the only place an error middleware could be shown (DOC-Q53). `platform-includes/getting-started-add-top-level-import/javascript.express.mdx` is referenced by no page, and so is `getting-started-add-top-level-import/javascript.fastify.mdx`, the only Fastify snippet whose import resolves; `getting-started-add-top-level-import/javascript.koa.mdx` is orphaned too, and it is the only Koa snippet that creates the router the verify step needs (DOC-Q44); `getting-started-add-top-level-import/javascript.connect.mdx` is orphaned as well, and so is `getting-started-capture-errors/javascript.hono.mdx`, whose one sentence points at the `honoIntegration` the migration page records as removed (`v10-to-v11/index.mdx:993`, `:1369`); the option it names, `shouldHandleError`, lives on `sentry(app, { ... })` and works there (QS-hono, variant should-handle-error). The logs section of `getting-started-verify/javascript.express.mdx:56-60` is unreachable, because the guide's onboarding options (`getting-started-verify/javascript.mdx:9-11`) do not include logs, although `Sentry.logger.info` works on the guide's setup (one log item per variant).

What to change:

- Add the missing include or drop the reference; delete or wire the orphaned include; add logs to the Express onboarding options or remove the unreachable section.

heading: The Angular manual-setup page promises transactions and shows a test span that ends before its error
title: Rewrite the Angular manual-setup verify and tracing text for the stream lifecycle
body:
`guides/angular/manual-setup.mdx:140-141`, `features/component-tracking.mdx:14` and `platform-includes/performance/enable-automatic-instrumentation/javascript.angular.mdx:3` speak of transactions, and `manual-setup.mdx:424-449` (and `index.mdx:77`) says the button starts a trace that measures the time until the error is thrown. Observed: only `span` envelope items, pageload and navigation segments named after the parameterized route with a trailing slash (`/users/:id/`) with a `Router` child; no transaction envelope. The example span ends after 0 ms, and the `setTimeout` throw 99 ms later is captured by `GlobalHandlers` as `auto.browser.global_handlers.onerror`, not by the Angular `ErrorHandler`, and marks the pageload segment `internal_error`; the same on zoneless Angular 22 and with zone.js loaded.

What to change:

- Say root spans and traces, show the `/users/:id/` and `Router` names, and make the verify callback async and await the timeout inside the span.

heading: Angular page hygiene: a deprecated bootstrap package, a missing logs option and a stray line
title: Fix the Angular pages' deprecated bootstrap call, the missing logs onboarding option and the stray export
body:
`guides/angular/features/component-tracking.mdx:139-159` and `manual-setup.mdx:166-220` bootstrap with `platformBrowserDynamic()` from `@angular/platform-browser-dynamic`; it works (`ui.angular.bootstrap`, 8 ms) but the package is deprecated on Angular 22 (`@deprecated` in its types, npm notice to use `@angular/platform-browser`). `manual-setup.mdx:84-91` offers no logs onboarding option, so the logs verify step at `:457-461` never renders although `Sentry.logger.*` delivers a log envelope. `features/error-handler.mdx:26` ends the App Config snippet with a stray `export class AppModule {}`.

What to change:

- Use `platformBrowser()` from `@angular/platform-browser`, add `logs` to the onboarding options, and drop the stray line.

heading: The Fastify integration page describes the wrong mechanism and none of the behaviour a user sees
title: Rewrite the Fastify integration page around the diagnostics-channel instrumentation and its options
body:
`common/configuration/integrations/fastify.mdx:21` says the integration captures spans using `@opentelemetry/instrumentation-fastify`; neither `@sentry/node` nor `@sentry/server-utils` depends on it, and the build subscribes to Fastify's `fastify.initialization` and `tracing:fastify.request.handler:error` diagnostics channels itself. The page (`:3`, `:17-27`) says the integration adds performance instrumentation and shows no option, while every error event in every working variant carries `auto.function.fastify` and the integration takes `shouldHandleError` with the default `reply.statusCode >= 500 || reply.statusCode <= 299`.

Two behaviours the page should name: on Fastify 4 the reply status is not yet set when the filter runs, so a thrown `{ statusCode: 404 }` error is captured on 4.29.1 and dropped on 5.12.3; and Fastify 4 prints `[FSTDEP017] DeprecationWarning` once for an unrouted request, because the instrumentation falls back to `request.routerPath`. The span tree is also undocumented: a segment `GET /users/:id`, a request handler span and a route-handler span both named `handler /users/:id`, and one middleware span per instance hook named `fastify - onRequest` and the like.

What to change:

- Replace the OpenTelemetry sentence with the diagnostics-channel mechanism, add the error capture, the `shouldHandleError` option and its default, the Fastify 4 status timing, the `FSTDEP017` note and the span tree.

heading: The Svelte pages promise transactions, show a 0 ms test span and print a placeholder that is a syntax error
title: Rewrite the Svelte verify and tracing text for the stream lifecycle and fix the compilerOptions placeholder
body:
`guides/svelte/index.mdx:96-97` says `tracesSampleRate` captures 100% of transactions and `features/component-tracking.mdx:6` and `:66` say component spans join the ongoing transaction; develop sends span envelope items (a pageload segment named `Pageload` with `url.path`, plus children) and no transaction item in any run. `index.mdx:247` says the updated button measures the execution of your code; the `startSpan` callback returns after scheduling a `setTimeout`, so the span lasts 0 ms and the error is thrown 99 ms later outside it (`auto.browser.browserapierrors.setTimeout`).

`features/component-tracking.mdx:23` and `:40` print `compilerOptions: {...}` as a stand-in for the user's options; copied as printed it is `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '}'`.

What to change:

- Say root spans and traces, make the verify callback async and await the timer, and use the `// ...` placeholder convention of the other guides.

heading: Solid pages: TypeScript in a javascript fence on the TanStack Router page and transactions wording
title: Fix the TanStack Router snippet fence and the transactions wording on the Solid pages
body:
`guides/solid/features/tanstack-router.mdx:20` opens a `javascript` block whose `:29-33` is a TypeScript `declare module` section; saved as `.jsx` it fails to parse (`Missing semicolon (12:7)`). `:14` promises pageload and navigation transactions, `guides/solid/index.mdx:97-98` says `tracesSampleRate` captures 100% of transactions and `:207-210` says the button starts a trace; under the default lifecycle no transaction item arrives, the pageload is a span segment named `Pageload` and the example span is its child.

What to change:

- Label the fence `typescript` or move the `declare module` block into a TypeScript-only note; say spans and traces instead of transactions, and that the button adds a span to the pageload trace.

heading: Hono guide details: unmatched requests under GET /*, the "no options" sentence, the filter's status source, the node-server dependency
title: Add the missing details to the Hono guide: catch-all naming, middleware options, error filter semantics and the node-server dependency
body:
Four things a Node reader hits that the guide does not say. Requests that match no route are named `GET /*` with `http.route: /*` and source `route`, because the `sentry()` middleware itself matches `/*`, so every 404 lands in one route-labelled segment. `guides/hono/index.mdx:235` says the Node middleware takes no options, while `sentry(app, { shouldHandleError })` is accepted on Node and `features/error-handler.mdx:52-77` works (a 401 became captured). `:362` says exceptions are captured from Hono's `onError`; capture reads the thrown error's status after `next()` regardless of `onError`, so a user `onError` that rewrites a 401 into a 500 does not make it captured, and Hono's default `onError` keeps printing every captured error to stderr. `@sentry/hono/node` imports `@hono/node-server/conninfo`, so `@hono/node-server` is required on Node although no install step names it; and `:214` runs `node --import ./instrument.mjs app.js` while the app tab at `:264` is named `app.ts`.

What to change:

- Mention the `GET /*` grouping, say "no init options" instead of "no options", state that filtering reads the thrown error's status, name `@hono/node-server` in the install step, and align the file names.

heading: NestJS guide details: the module adds nothing observable, transactions wording, doubled Express spans
title: Say what SentryModule does on the NestJS guide, fix the transactions wording and describe the span sets
body:
`guides/nestjs/index.mdx:97-117` presents `SentryModule.forRoot()` as a required step; the run without it was identical in every check (event transaction name, route-named segments, spans), because the module only registers an interceptor that sets a transaction name the HTTP instrumentation already set. `guides/nestjs/tracing/instrumentation/automatic-instrumentation.mdx:3` promises transactions; no transaction envelope was sent, every request is a span envelope, and the included `node-automatic-instrumentation.mdx` never mentions Nest. `common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:392` and `:436-441` describe the Nest handler spans correctly, but each request also carries the Express instrumentation's spans (`urlencodedParser`, `jsonParser`, two identical `handler` spans with origin `auto.http.express`) and a `Create Nest App` segment at start-up, which no page mentions.

What to change:

- Say what the module does or mark it optional, reword transactions to spans and list the Nest spans, and mention that Nest-on-Express apps get both span sets and a start-up segment.

heading: Elysia includes and details: a browser paragraph, old ops, a function-name claim, a missing run command
title: Rewrite the Elysia instrumentation include for v11 and add the Node run details
body:
`platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:1` is a BrowserTracing paragraph; `:5-7` name the ops `request_handler.elysia` and `middleware.elysia`, say transactions use parameterized names, and say named handlers show their function name. Observed on Node: ops `handler` and `middleware`, no transaction under the default lifecycle, route-named segments, and no `code.function.name` on any span although the handler is a named function; `common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:392` makes the same function-name claim for Elysia. The SDK also emits middleware spans for its own hooks (`sentryOnRequest`, `sentryOnAfterHandle`, `sentryOnError`), 11 to 12 spans per request, and children that end before route resolution carry `sentry.segment.name: GET`.

`guides/elysia/index.mdx:105-127` presents `index.ts` as the Node setup and never says how to start it; `node index.ts` runs it but prints `MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON` unless package.json has `"type": "module"`. The Bun tab is the default expanded tab; run under Node it dies at `.listen()` with `WebStandard does not support listen`.

What to change:

- Drop the browser paragraph, use the `handler` and `middleware` ops, say spans and segments, remove the function-name sentence until Node emits the attribute (and qualify migration `:392`), document the span count, and add the run command with the `"type": "module"` note.

heading: The Mastra agent-tracing page lists attributes the exporter does not emit, and neither page names the defaults or the trace shape
title: Correct the attribute list, the defaults and the trace shape on the Mastra pages
body:
`common/agent-tracing/mastra.mdx:140-172` lists `gen_ai.system`, `gen_ai.request.messages`, `gen_ai.request.temperature`, `gen_ai.tool.type` `function`, `gen_ai.tool.input`, `gen_ai.tool.output` and `gen_ai.agent.instructions`. The build sends `gen_ai.provider.name`, `gen_ai.input.messages` and `gen_ai.output.messages`, `gen_ai.tool.type` `tool`, `gen_ai.tool.call.arguments` and `gen_ai.tool.call.result`, and `gen_ai.system_instructions`; no temperature; and `gen_ai.request.stream` is `true` for non-streaming calls. `guides/mastra/index.mdx:83` and `agent-tracing/mastra.mdx:61` say the exporter reads `SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT` and `SENTRY_RELEASE`; when unset it passes environment `production` and release `''`, and the empty release makes the SDK discard every session with a warning.

Two things about the trace neither page says: the model's HTTP calls arrive as separate `http.client` root segments (`auto.http.node_fetch`) in the same trace, not as children of `gen_ai.chat`; and on the built-in route each tool call yields two `gen_ai.execute_tool` spans (one under the agent span from `client_tool_call`, one under the chat span), so tool counts double.

What to change:

- Replace the attribute list with the names the exporter emits, name the defaults and tell users to set `SENTRY_RELEASE`, and describe the trace shape.

heading: GCP Functions guide details: callback handlers lose the function span, HTTP functions split into two traces, no run step, no logs option, drifting export names
title: Add the missing details to the Google Cloud Functions guide: promise-form handlers, the two-trace split, a local run step, the logs option and consistent export names
body:
The Background and CloudEvent Issues snippets (`platform-includes/getting-started-config/javascript.gcp-functions.mdx:71-75`, `:110-114`, `guides/gcp-functions/index.mdx:110-112`) wrap a callback-style handler that throws: the error is captured (`auto.function.serverless.gcp_event` and `gcp_cloud_event`, with `gcp.function.context`), but the callback path never ends the function span, so no `function.gcp` span arrives; the promise-form Tracing snippets end it correctly. For HTTP functions every invocation yields two segments in two traces, `Serverless function execution` (`function.gcp`) and the Node `http.server` `GET`, with the error linked to the function trace only, which `automatic-instrumentation.mdx:7` does not say.

The guide never says how to run a function locally (`index.mdx:24`, `:82-90`); run with `npx @google-cloud/functions-framework --target=helloHttp` the segment has no `faas.name`, because the SDK reads `FUNCTION_TARGET` or `K_SERVICE`, which Cloud Run sets and the framework does not. `index.mdx:32-34` offers no logs onboarding option, so the logs verify include at `:176-180` never renders although `Sentry.logger.info` works with the unmodified config. The export names drift between the config and verify steps (`helloEvents` against `helloBackground` and `helloEvent`), so the entry point has to change with each paste.

What to change:

- Use the promise form in the Background and CloudEvent Issues snippets, state that HTTP functions produce two root spans, add a local run step with the `FUNCTION_TARGET` note, add `logs` to the onboarding options, and use one export name per tab.

heading: AWS Lambda details: an inconsistent verify tab, a broken anchor, request data absent, awslambda-auto outside Lambda, transactions comment
title: Add the missing details to the AWS Lambda pages
body:
`guides/aws-lambda/index.mdx:42-54`: the CommonJS verify tab has no `wrapHandler` while the ESM tab wraps, and both install options wrap the handler through the `_HANDLER` redirect anyway, so the tabs should match the npm page's no-code-changes promise. `configuration/lambda-wrapper.mdx:9` links `../../install/layer#alternative-initialize-the-sdk-in-code`, a heading that does not exist (the section is Option B: Manual Setup, `layer.mdx:62`). The data-collection include rendered at `install/npm.mdx:170` says user data, HTTP bodies and query parameters are sent; the Lambda error event carries no `request` at all, only the span has `url.full`. `install/npm.mdx:74` presents `NODE_OPTIONS="--import @sentry/aws-serverless/awslambda-auto"` as all the setup needed; outside the Lambda runtime it throws `LAMBDA_TASK_ROOT environment variable is not set` before user code. `npm.mdx:107-108` says 100% of transactions; the invocation is a `function.aws` span item, never a transaction.

What to change:

- Align the verify tabs, fix the anchor, say that Lambda request data is limited to `url.full` on the span, note that `awslambda-auto` needs the Lambda environment, and reword the comment to spans.

heading: Effect guide details: a missing install, an unshown file, the span op, log annotations, the integrations that are off
title: Add the missing details to the Effect guide
body:
`guides/effect/index.mdx:43-53` installs `@sentry/effect` only, then `:81` and `:86` import `NodeRuntime` from `@effect/platform-node` and `HttpLive` from `./Http.js`; the install pulls no `@effect/*` package and `Http.js` is never shown. `:301`, `:307` and `:322-324` call the custom span a transaction with `{ op: "test" }`; it arrives as a span item with `sentry.op: function` and `op` as an ordinary attribute. `:355-367` annotate logs with `Effect.annotateLogs`; the three log items arrive with `sentry.*` and `server.address` only, the annotations show in the console logger alone. `:61` and `:71` say the layer initializes Sentry for Node; with `defaultIntegrations` forced off, no Http, Console, global error handler, LinkedErrors or ContextLines integration is installed.

What to change:

- Name `@effect/platform-node` in the install step and show a minimal `Http.ts`, say the Effect span op is `function`, note that log annotations are not forwarded, and say that the Node auto-instrumentation and global handlers are off unless `defaultIntegrations` is set.

heading: Nitro guide details: source maps deleted without a token, an untyped option, the dev double init, $fetch
title: Add the missing details to the Nitro guide
body:
`guides/nitro/index.mdx:162` says `withSentryConfig` generates hidden source maps, uploads them and deletes the `.map` files; with no auth token the plugin warns it will not upload and still deletes every `.map` file from `.output`, leaving a build without source maps. `:277-282` set `enableNitroErrorHandler: false` in `Sentry.init`; the option works at runtime but is not part of `NodeOptions` in any shipped type, so a TypeScript init file gets an excess-property error. `:178` runs `nitro dev` under `NODE_OPTIONS`; in dev the SDK initializes in the main thread and in the worker, and each request sends two segments, a dev-proxy `GET` with source `url` plus the worker's route-named one. `:295` and `:314` say outgoing requests are instrumented; global `fetch` propagates and yields an `http.client` span, while `$fetch` is not a global in Nitro 3. `:24` says Node.js 18.19.0+; the package declares 20.19 and later (DOC-Q62).

What to change:

- Warn that the `.map` files are deleted even without a token, note that the option is untyped, mention the dev-proxy segment, use `fetch` in the outgoing example, and update the Node prerequisite.
